quduri.b: Yes, in the Azan of Fajr, as-Salaatu ghayru min an-nawm [Prayer is better than sleep] is added after Hayya 'ala al-Falaah.

quduri.f: Is there Tarji' in Azan?
quduri.b:
There is no Tarji' according to the Ahnaf.23

23 Tarji'is to silently say the two Shahadah and then repeat it loudly. It is Sunnah according to the Shawafi'.

quduri.f: Explain the words and time of the Iqamah.
quduri.b: When the people stand for Jama'ah [congegrational] Salah, the Muazzin will repeat the words of the Azan. After Hayya 'Ala al-Falaah he will add Qad Qamaati as-Salaah [Salah is established] twice. The people present in the Masjid should be able to hear him. This is the iqamah.

quduri.f: Is there a difference in the way the Azan and Iqamah are rendered?
quduri.b: Yes, the Azan is lengthened out and the Iqamah is recited hastily.

quduri.f: What is the ruling on facing the Qibla during the two? [i.e. during Azan and Iqamah]
quduri.b: It is established from the Nabi ﷺ until our present day to face the Qiblah while calling Azan and Iqamah.

quduri.f: Should the face be turned when reciting any words?
quduri.b: It is Mustahab for the Muazzin to turn to the right when saying Hayya 'alas Salah and to the left when saying Hayya 'alal falah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of putting the fingers in the ears during the two calls?
quduri.b: It is Sunnah during Azan only. The Nabi ﷺ ordered Bilal رضي الله عنه to do so. He said, "It will raise your voice." [narrated by Ibn Majah].

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Azan and Iqaamah for missed Salah?
quduri.b: Both should be called. If he wishes to perform several missed Salah at the same time, both should be recited for the first. Thereafter he may recite both for each Salah or suffice with the Iqamah.

quduri.f: Can Azan and Iqamah be called without Wudu?
quduri.b: It is only appropriate that the Muazzin has Wudu. It is permissible to call the Azan without Wudu but Makruh to call Iqamah like that. It is also Makruh for a junub to call the Azan.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a junub having called the Azan and Iqamah?
quduri.b:
The Azan should be repeated, not the Iqamah.24

24 This is the more authentic view as stated in al-Hidayah and al-Mujtaba.

quduri.f: Is the Azan of a child allowed?
quduri.b: Yes, if the child is intelligent ['aqil] and can distinguish [Mumayyiz]. His Azan needs not be repeated.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Azan before the Waqt?
quduri.b: It is not valid and must be repeated. Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى however has permitted the Azan of Fajr before its time.

quduri.f: Describe the preconditions of Salah by which Salah is not valid.
quduri.b:
The following is necessary upon the Musalli:
Pure from both Hadath from the beginning of the Salah until the end.
His body must be pure from Najasah.
That the place of Salah be pure.
That he wear pure clothing which cover the 'awrah [private region]. The Salah with clothing which reveals the 'awrah is invalid as is Salah with clothing soiled with Najasah.
The Salah should be in its Waqt. It may not be before the entry of its time.
He must face the Qiblah.
He should have an intention in his heart which Salah he is performing. There should be no blockage (gap) between the intention and the Tahrimah. The Muqtadi [follower] should in addition intend that he is following the Imam.

quduri.f: What should someone who neither has pure clothing nor has the means of removing the Najasah do?
quduri.b:
He should perform the Salah in that Najis clothing. The Salah will be valid and need not be repeated.25 

25 That is in the concise words of al-Quduri. Al-Hidayah expands on it thus, "There are two scenarios. If a quarter or more of the clothing is pure then he should pray in it. If he prays naked it will not be valid. A quarter of a thing can represent a full. If it is less than a quarter is pure then the ruling remains the same according to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله and one of two views of Ash-Shafii. They say that Salah in the dirty clothing is leaving one Fard, but Salah naked is leaving several. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى he has a choice between the two, but praying in the clothing is better because covering the private region is not specified to Salah, whereas purity is.

quduri.f: How should one pray who does not have clothing to cover his 'Awrah?
quduri.b:
If he prays and stands and makes Ruku' and Sujud it will be correct. It will be better if he sits and does Ruku' and Sujud by way of indication only. In either case he should hide from the people.26

26 There are four scenarios: 1. Salah sitting with indications; 2. or with full Ruku' and Sujud. 3. standing with indications; 4. or with full Ruku'and Sujud. According to ad-Durr al-Mukthar all four are permissible but the first is best. See its chapter on preconditions of Salah.

quduri.f: What are the limits of a man's 'Awrah which must be covered for the Slaah to be valid?
quduri.b: A man's 'Awrah is from below the navel to the knee. The knee is included but not the navel.

quduri.f: What is a woman's 'awrah?
quduri.b:
If she is a free woman then her 'awrah for the validity of Salah is her entire body. The only exception is her face, hands and feet. This is only for the validity of Salah. It does not mean that she is allowed to show her face to non-Mahrams.27 A slave-girl's 'awrah is the same as a man's, except that she will cover her stomach and back. The rest of her body is not 'awrah.

27 Ad-Durr al-Mukthar warns about this saying, "A young woman is forbidden from showing her face to men, not because it is 'awrah, but because of fear of temptation, just as even if there is no desire, touching is worse."

quduri.f: What should one do who is unable to face Qiblah due to fear of animals or some other reason?
quduri.b: He should face whichever direction he is able to.

quduri.f: If one is confused about the Qiblah and there is none to ask about it, what is the ruling?
quduri.b: He should make an effort to ascertain and then face wherever he thinks the Qiblah most probably is.

quduri.f: If after the effort he prayed and then learnt that his Qiblah was wrong, should he repeat the Salah?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What should he do if he learns whilst already in Salah that his Qiblah is wrong?
quduri.b:
He should turn to the Qiblah and continue his Salah. He need not start anew.

NOTE: When one is in al-Masjid al-Haram, it is necessary that one faces the Ka'bah exactly. As for one outside, even in Makkah, it is sufficient to face the direction of the Ka'bah.

quduri.f: List the Fard acts of Salah.
quduri.b:
There are six Faraid:
at-Tahrimah [the first Allaahu Akbar]
Qiyam [standing]
Qira'ah [recitation of the Quran] even if it be an Aayah.
Ruku'
Sujud
The final sitting for the duration of Tashshahud.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of the Faraid?
quduri.b: It is necessary to do them. The Salah is not valid if even one is omitted, whether intentionally or forgetfully. The salah must be repeated and Sujudus Sahw will not suffice.

quduri.f: What are the Wajibat of Salah?
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
Recitation of Surah al-Fatihah.
To join a Surah or three Aayat with it.
To read al-Fatihah before the Surah.
To recite in the first two Rak'at of the Faraid.
Coming to a standstill in each posture [Itminan].
The first sitting.
Tashshahud in the first and second sitting.
The word, "Salam," when intending to end the Salah.
Qunut in Witr.
The extra Takbirs of 'Id.
For the Imam to read Qira-ah aloud in Fajr, Jumu'ah, the two 'Ids, Tarawih, Witr of Ramadan and the first two Rak'at of Maghrib and 'Isha.
For the Imam to read Qira-ah softly in Zhuhr and 'Asr and after the first two Rak'at of Maghrib and 'Isha.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Wajib?
quduri.b: If a Wajib is omitted deliberately, it is Wajib to repeat the Salah. If it was forgotten then Sujudus Sahw suffices.

quduri.f: What are the Sunan of Salah?
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
Lifting the hands at the time of Tahrimah in line with the ears if a man and with the shoulders for a woman. Men will then place their right hands on their left below the navel.
Thana after Tahrimah.
Ta'awwuz [A'uzu billah minash Shaytanir Rajim].
Tasmiyah.
To say, "Amin" after al-Fatihah.
Tasbih.
Tahmid.
Takbir of Ruku', Sujud, Qiyam [standing] and when rising from Ruku'.
Tasbih of Ruku' and Sujud.
Holding the knees with the hands during Ruku' with the fingers spread out.
During the two sittings and between the two Sajdah to sit on the left foot flat under the buttocks with the right foot raised at the side.
To point the finger at Tashshahud.
Placing the hands on the thighs during the sittings.
Qira-ah after the first Rak'at in the Faraid. In non-Faraid Qira-ah is necessary in each Rak'ah. The Imam's Takbir, "Sami'Allaahu liman hamidah," and Salam.
Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ in the final Tashshahud.
Du'a after that which resemble those of the Quran and Hadith.
To turn right and left during the two Salam.
For the Imam to intend greeting the men, guardian angels and pious Jinn when making both Salam.
The follower should intend greeting the Imam when turning in the direction the Imam is. If he is directly in line, he should intend both times.
The follower should intend greeting the other followers, guardian angels and pious Jinn in both directions.
One praying alone should intend the angels only.

quduri.f: What are the etiquettes of Salah?
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
A man should remove his hands from his sleeves at the time of Takbir.
To look at the place of Sujud when standing, at the top of his feet when in Ruku', at the nose when in Sujud, at the lap when sitting and at the shoulders when making Salam.
Avoid coughing as far as possible.
Closing the mouth when yawning.

quduri.f: Explain the method of Salah from beginning to end.
quduri.b:
When intending to start Salah, recite Takbir to begin without voewel elongation, whilst standing and raise the hands until the ears. Afer Takbir place the right hands over the left below the navel. Then recite Thana سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، وَتَبارَكَ اسْمُكَ، وَتَعَالَى جَدُّكَ، وَلاَ إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ "Pure is You O Allaah with Your praises. Blessed is Your Name and high is Your station. There is no illah but You." Then recite Ta'awwuz and then Tasmiyah. These three are silent. A follower does not recite the last two because there is no Qira-ah for him. Thereafter al-Fatihah is recited. Then Amin is said softly even when it is a loud Salah. Thereafter a Surah or any three Aayat are read. After Qira-ah read Takbir and go into Ruku' without raising the hands. Then grip the knees with the hands. The fingers should be spread out and the calves straight. The back must be stretched out straight in line with the buttocks. The head should neither be raised nor dropped. In Ruku' he will say at least thrice, سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ "Pure is my Rabb Most Magnificent." He will then raise his head from Ruku', saying "Allaah has heard he who has praised Him." He will then say immediately سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ "Praise be to You my Rabb," if he is praying alone. In congegration the Imam will suffice with the first sentence and the follower with the second. He will stand up straight. He will then say Takbir رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ and go into Sujud by first lowering his knees, then his arms then his hands. He will stretch his fingers to the Qiblah, making Sujud with his nose and forehead, his armpits open. His stomach must be away from his thighs. His toes should face the Qiblah. Recite at least سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى "Pure is my Rabb Most High." Then raise the head, reciting Takbir. Sit up straight, coming to a standstill, hands on the thighs. Recite Takbir and go into Sajdah, reciting the same at least thrice. Then say Takbir to stand again without leaning on the hands or sitting in between. First the head should be raised, then the hands, then the knees and stand for second Rak'ah. There will be no Thana or Ta'awwuz this time. When the second Sajdah of the second Rak'ah is completed, place the left foot flat under the buttocks and raise the right foot, toes facing the Qiblah. Place the right hand on the right thigh and the left on the left. Fingers are spread out on them. Recite the tashshahud of Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه 
التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله
"Greetings, salutations and purity be to Allaah. Salam to you O Nabi and Allaah's mercy and blessings. Salam be on us and Allaah's pious slaves. I testify that there is no illah but Allaah and I testify that Muhammad ﷺ is His slave and Rasul (messenger)."
He will indicate with his right index finger at the time of the Shahadah, making a circle with the thumb and middle finger and closing the small and next finger. If he intended two Rak'at, Salah 'alan Nabi ﷺ is recited after Tashshahud. Du'a from Quran and Hadith is then recited, but not what resembles the words of people. Salam is then made to the right saying, "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah." The same is done to the left. He should turn so much that someone looking behind at his shoulders will see his cheeks. He will intend that he is greeting the Imam, the guardian angels and the fellow Musallis as we have mentioned before.
If he intented four Rak'at at the time of Tahrimah he will stand up from Tashshahud for the third Rak'ah. He will not raise his hands, nor recite Ta'awwuza and Thana. After the two Sajdah he will stand for the fourth Rak'ah. The third and the fourth is completed with standing, Qira-ah, Ruku' and Sujud as we discussed with the first two. He will sit after the second Sajdah of the fourth Rak'ah just as he sat for the first two Rak'at. He will recite the Tashshahud and Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ offer du'a and make Salam to the right and left as discussed.

If he intended three Rak'at at the time of Tahrimah, he will sit after the second Sajdah of the third Rak'ah. He will recite the Tashahud and Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ, offer du'a and make Salam.
التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله [1, 2]
التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله [1, 2]

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Sajdah on the tail of the turban or the extra part of the clothing?
quduri.b:
If it is on the forehead and he makes Sajdah it is valid but Makruh. If done with an excuse then it is not Makruh.28

28 Ad-Darr al-Mukthar states, "It is Makruh Tanzihi to makes Sajdah on the turban tail except for a reason although it remains valid as long as it is completely or partly on the forehead as has been discusses. If it is only on his head and he makes Sajdah like that deficiently then it is invalid because Sujud was not made on its place. It is also a condition that the place of Sajdah be clean and that the bulk of forehead touches the ground. People are neglectful of that." [Description of Salah]

quduri.f: Is the descriptin you have given the Salah of a man only, or a man and woman? [i.e. question 149)
quduri.b:
It is for both. A woman however differs with a man as follows:
She will place her hands on her chest.
She will not take her hands out of her sleeces at the time of Takbir.
She will raise her hands to the height of her shoulders.
She will not spread out her fingers during Ruku'. She will keep them closed and place them on her knees.
She will lower herself slightly for Ruku' to the extent that she almost reaches the full extent but she will proceed beyond that.
She will keep her elbows in during Ruku'.
She will keep her stomach close to her thighs during Sajdah.

She will sit in the tawarruk position in every sitting. i.e. She will extend her legs to the right side. Right calf on the left calf. [Buttock] sitting on the ground.
She will place her arms on the ground during Sajdah.

quduri.f: Explain the laws of Qira-ah for the Imam, Muqtadi [follower] and Mufrid [solitary Musalli].
quduri.b:
The Masail are as follows:
Qira-ah in general is Fard in every Salah.
Qira-ah of al-Fatihah is Wajib.
To read a Surah or three Aayat thereafter is also Wajib. Qira-ah in itself by fulfilling one of these two is Wajib.
The third and fourth Rak'at of Fard Salah is exempted from the above rule. Here al-Fatihah is Sunnah, not Fard or Wajib.
It is Wajib to specify Qira-ah in the first two Rak'at of Fard [i.e. it cannot be substituted into other Rak'at]
It is Wajib to read al-Fatihah before the rest of the Qira-ah.
One has a choice if one wishes to read al-Fatihah after the first two Rak'at of the Fard. To do so is better. If he wants he can recite Tasbih. If one added any Qira-ah to al-Fatihah after the first two Rak'at Sadatus Sahw is not required.
The follower will not read behind the Imam, whether in audible or in-audible Salah.29 
It is Wajib upon the Imam to read aloud in the two Rak'at of Fajr, Jumu'ah, the two 'Ids and the first two Rak'at of Maghrib and 'Isha.
Both the Imam and Munfarid reads in-audibly in all Rak'at of Zhuhr and 'Asr, the third Rak'ah of Maghrib and the last two Rak'at of 'Isha.
A Munfarid may choose to read loud or soft those Qira-ah which the Imam must read aloud [Maghrib, Esha and Fajr].
It is Sunnah for the Imam and Munfarid to read Tiwal al-Mufassal [long surah] in Fajr and Zhuhr30 Awsat [medium length]31 in 'Asr and 'Isha and Qisar32 in Maghrib. This is for residents. Travellers should read what they may.
29 Muslim narrates that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari رضي الله عنه narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "And when he reads, then you keep silent." [Chapter on Tashshahud in Salah]

30 From Suratul Hujarat to al-Buruj.

31 From Suratul Tariq until al-Bayyinah.

32 From Suratuz Zilzal till the end of the Quran.

quduri.f: Should the Imam or Munfarid read Bismilaah or Ta'awwuz aloud when the Qira-ah is loud?
quduri.b: No, they must be read softly.

quduri.f: Should the Imam or Munfarid read Amin aloud after al-Fatihah?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Does a woman read aloud when praying a loud Salah on her own?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Can Qira-ah be specified in certain Salah?
quduri.b: Qira-ah should not be specified when it be construed that no other Qira-ah is allowed in that Salah. It is in fact Makruh to specifiy a certain Surah for all Salah or some Salah and never read anything else.

quduri.f: If there is no Wajib specification, is there anything from the Sunnah about reading certain Surahs in some Salah, which if the Musalli chooses to read then he will be rewarded?
quduri.b:
Yes, there do appear such Surahs which will be rewarded. Some are:
It is Sunnah to read Alif Lam Min Tanzil in the first Rak'ah of Fajr of the Day of Jumu'ah, "Hal ata 'aalal Insan" in the second Rak'ah. [al-Bukhari and Muslim from Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه]
It is Sunnah to read Suratul Jumu'ah in the first Rak'ah of Salatul Jumu'ah and "Iza ja akal Munafiqun" in the second. [Muslim from Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه]
It is Sunnah to read "Sabbihisma Rabbikal A'la" in the first Rak'ah of Salatul Jumu'ah and "Hal ataka Hadithul Ghasiyah" in the second. [Muslim from Nu'man bin Bashir رضي الله عنه".
It is Sunnah to read "Sahhibisma Rabbikal A'la" in the first Rak'ah of both 'Ids and "Hal ataka Hadithul Ghashiyah" in the second. [Muslim from Nu'man bin Bashir رضي الله عنه]

quduri.f: How is Witr performed? How many Rak'at does it consist of?
quduri.b:
Witr is three Rak'at prayer after 'Isha. It is not permissible before it. The method is recite Takbir for beginning then Thana, Ta'awwuz, Bismillaah, al-Fatihah and the Surah thereafter. Then make Ruku' and two Sujud and then stand and pray the second Raka'ah as in any other Salah. At the end of it sit and read Tashshahud. Then stand for the third Rak'ah, read al-Fatihah and then a Surah. Then read Takbir33, raising the hands to the ears34. Read the Qunut35 and upon completion36 read Takbir and make Ruku'. Complete the Rak'ah like any other Salah's.

33 Ibn Abi Shaybah narrates from Shu'bah, "I have heard al-Hakam, Hammad Abu Ishaq saying that after completion of Qira-ah, read Takbir and then Qunut."
34 'Abdurrahman bin al-Aswad narrated from his father who narrates that 'Abdullaah bin Mas'ud رضي الله عنه used to raise his hands in Qunut of Witr. [Ibn Abi Shaybah (390/3) Madinah edition; al-Imam al-Bukhari in Juz Raf'il Yadayn. In it he verifies that 'Abdullaah رضي الله عنه used to read al-Ikhlas in the last Rak'ah of Witr then raise his hands and read Qunut before Ruku']
35 Ibrahim عليه السلام said, "Read in Qunut of Witr: Allaahumma inna nasta'inuka wa nastaghfiruka." [Ibn Abi Shaybah (381/3)]. Abu 'Abdirrahman said, "Abdullaah bin Mas'ud tau of Rasght us how to read in Witr: Allaahumma inna nasta'inuka wa nastaghriuka wa numinu bika wa nuthni 'alaykal khayr." [Ibn Abi Shaybah]
36 'Alqamah narrates that Ibn Masud رضي الله عنه and the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم of Rasulullaah ﷺ used to read Qunut in Witr before Ruku'. [Ibn Abi Shaybah (383/3)] 'Abdurrahman bin al-Aswad narrates from his father that when Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه completed his Qira-ah, he read Takbir and then Qunut. Thereafter he made Takbir and Ruku'. [Ibn Abi Shaybah (383/3)]

quduri.f: Are al-Fatihah and a Surah read in all Rak'at of Witr?
quduri.b: Yes, in all.

quduri.f: Is there Masnun Qira-ah in Witr?
quduri.b:
Yes, it is Sunnah to recite in the first Rak'ah after al-Fatihah Surah al-A'la; al-Kafirun in the second an al-Ikhlas in the third. Other narrations add al-Falaq and an-Nas with al-Ikhlas to the third Rak'ah.37

37 At-Tirmizi narrates it from 'Aisha رضي الله عنها and an-Nasai from 'Abdurrahman bin Abzi. Ahmad narrates from Ubayy bin Ka'b رضي الله عنه and ad-Darami from Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما. These two do not mention al-Falaq and an-Nas. [See Mishkatul Masabih, Chapter on Witr].

quduri.f: Is Qunut read loud or soft?
quduri.b: It is soft, swhether one is Imam, Munfarid or Muqtadi.

quduri.f: Can Witr be performed in congegration?
quduri.b: Yes, it is Sunnah to perform it in congregation every night of Ramadan after Tarawih.

quduri.f: Does the Imam read Qira-ah aloud in Witr?
quduri.b: Yes, in all three Rak'at.

quduri.f: Is there Qunut in any Salah besides Witr?
quduri.b: No, unless it is recited due to a disaster which aflicts the Muslims. In that case Qunut is read whilst standing after Ruku'. The Imam will make du'a for the Muslims and against their enemies.

quduri.f: How many Rak'at of Sunnah are made before and after the Fard?
quduri.b:
12 Rak'at of Sunnah are emphasised. They are called Sunnah Muakkadah [emphasized]. Ummul Muminin 'Aisha رضي الله عنها narrated that the Nabi ﷺ said, "Allaah will build a house in Jannah for he who is constant on twelve Rak'at of Sunnah - 4 before Zhuhr, 2 after, 2 after Maghrib, 2 after 'Isha and 2 before Fajr."38

Shurayh narrates that 'Aisha رضي الله عنها said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never prayed 'Isha, except that he would then come by me and pray 4 or 6 Rak'at."39

38 This is the words of al-Timirzi, similarly narrated by an-Nasai. At-Tirmizi adds, "In the chapter there are also narrations from Umm Habibah, Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه, Abu Musa and Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما." He then narrates the narration of Umm Habibah and declares it authentic. Muslim also narrates the Hadith of Umm Habibah and in the end says that she said, "I then always prayed these."
39 Whoever practices upon these four or six mentioned does well. However, only two are emphasised because of the narration encouraging consistency on it. Abu Dawud narrates the Hadith of Shurayh.

quduri.f: Are some of these [i.e. 12 Rak'at of Sunnah] more emphasised than the others?
quduri.b:
Yes, the most emphasised are the two before Fajr, then the four before Zhuhr. 'Aisha رضي الله عنها said, "the Nabi ﷺ did not emphasise any Nafl as much as he placed importance on two Rak'at before Fajr."

She also said that Nabi ﷺ,  "Never left the 4 before Zhuhr and 2 before early morning." [al-Bukhari and others have narrated both narrations]

quduri.f: Are there Sunan before and after Jumu'ah?
quduri.b:
Yes, there are 4 Rak'at before and 4 after.40

That is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the Sunnah is 6 after Jumu'ah.

40 The 4 afterwards are based on Muslim's narration from Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه who narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When you pray after Jumu'ah, pray 4." A group other than al-Bukhari narrate that Rasulullah ﷺ said, "When one of you prays Jumu'ah he must pray four afterwards." The first indicates Istihbab and the second Wujub. We have therefore combined the two as Sunnah Muakkadah. As for the four before, it is due to the consistency of Rasulullaah ﷺ on the four after Zawal which includes Jumu'ah as well.

quduri.f: Is there Sunnah before 'Asr?
quduri.b:
Yes, there is a Hadith which encourages 4 Rak'at before 'Asr. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "May Allaah have mercy on a man who prays four before 'Asr." [Abu Dawud]
'Ali رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to pray two Rak'at before 'Asr. [Abu Dawud]

quduri.f: Is there Sunnah before 'Isha?41
quduri.b:
Four Rak'at before 'Isha is Mustahab.

41 Al-Halabi says in his commentary on Munyatul Musalli, 'The four before are not mentioned specifically in a Hadith. Proof is taken from the Hadith of 'Abdullaah bin Mughaffal رضي الله عنه that Rasulullaah ﷺ said twice, "Between Azan and Iqamah there is Salah." Then he said after the third time, "For who wants to." This is when there is no obstacle to praying before the Fard and is regarded as Mustahab. Four specifically is based on the view of Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى that the word, "Salah" in its complete form and quality indicates 4.'

quduri.f: What is the ruling of these Sunan? [i.e. the Sunan before 'Asr and 'Isha]
quduri.b: The Sunan before 'Asr and before 'Isha are not Muakkadah.

quduri.f: Is there Sunnah Qira-ah in any of these Sunan?
quduri.b:
Yes, at-Tirmizi narrates that 'Abdullaah bin Mas'ud رضي الله عنه said, "I cannot count the amount of times I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ read in the two Rak'at after Maghrib and the two Rak'at before Fajr, 'Qul ya ayyuhal Kafirun...' and 'Qul HuwAllaahu Ahad.'"
Muslim narrates from Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to read in the first Rak'ah before Fajr, "Qulu amanna billahi wa ma unzila ilayna..."[al-Baqarah] and in the last Rak'ah, "Amanna billahi wash-had bi-anna Muslimum..." [Al-'Imran]
Muslim also narrates from Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to readi in the Rak'at before Fajr, "... amanna billahi wa ma unzila ilayna..."42 and from al 'Imran, "... Ta'alaw ila kalimatin sawaim baynana wa baynakum"

42 It means he read in the first Rak'ah, "Qulu ammanna billahi..." until the end of the Aayah. It is clarified in al-Bayhaqi that he read until, "wa nahnu lahu Muslimun." In the second Rak'ah he read the complete Aayah from Al 'Imran from, "Qul ya Ahlal Kitabi ta'alaw ila kalimatin..."

quduri.f: Besides Fardh, Witr and the above Sunan [i.e. 'Asr and 'Isha] are there any other Salaats prescribed?
quduri.b:
Yes, Shari'ah allows one to perform whatever Nafl one is capable of day and night. There is great virtue43 in that. The Makruh times we have mentioned should however be avoided.

43 Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "The first thing the slave will be questioned about concerning his deeds on the Day of Qiyamah is his Salah. If it is in order he succesful and victorious. If it is unsound then he has failed and lost. If there is a deficiency in his Fard, then the Rabb Most Blessed and High says, 'See if My slave has any Nafl to make up for the deficiency in his Fard.' Then all of the rest of his deeds are treated in the-like that.

quduri.f: Is the Nafl you mentioned for all times and conditions? Is there narrated anything about extra virtues at special times?
quduri.b:
Yes, the virtue of Nafl at the end of the night has been narrated.44 It is called Salatul Tahajjud. Also narrated is ad-Duha [early morning]45; the nights of Ramadan especially Laylatul Qadr [Night of Power]46; after Wudu47, when entering the Masjid before one sits48, when a matter befalls him49, when repenting [Tawbah]50, when in need [Hajah]51 and when seeking guidance [Istikharah]52.

44 Abu Umamah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "you should perform the Salah of the night. It is the way of the pious before you and draws you closer to your Rabb. It compensates for evil and erases sins."[at-Tirmizi].
45 Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who guards the two Rak'at of Duha will have his sins forgiven even if they are equal to the foam of the sea." [Ahmad, at-Tirmizi and Ibn Majah]
Mu'azah asked 'Aishah رضي الله عنها, How many Rak'at of Duha did Rasulullaah ﷺ pray? " 'Aishah رضي الله عنها used to pray 8 Rak'at of Duha and used to say, "I would never leave it even if my parents were to be resurrected for me." [Malik]
46 Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who fasts Ramadan with Iman and hoping for reward has his passed sins forgiven. He who prays the Salah of Ramadan with Iman and hoping for forgiveness has his passed sins forgiven. He who prays on the Night of Power with Iman and hoping for forgiveness has his passed sins forgiven." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]
47 Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Bilal رضي الله عنه at the time of Fajr, "O Bilal! Tell me what deed you have done in Islaam which you have most hope in? Indeed I have heard the stepping of your sandals before me in Jannah." Bilal said, "I have no greater hope in any deed other than whenever I make Wudu at any time of the day or night I pray with that Wudu however much Salah has been written for me." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]
48 Abu Qatada رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When one of you enters the Masjid he should pray two Rak'at before sitting." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]
49 Huzayfah رضي الله عنه narrates, "When any difficulty befell the Nabi ﷺ he would resort to Salah." [Abu Dawud]
50 'Ali رضي الله عنه narrates: Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه narrated to me and Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه was truthful. He said, I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'There is no man who sins and then arises to make Wudu, pray Salah and seek Allaah's forgiveness except that Allaah forgives him.'" [Ibn Majah]
51 'Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said: He who has a need from Allaah or any son of Adam عليه السلام should perform Wudu and it should be a proper Wudu. Let him pray two Rak'at, praise Allaah and offer salutations upon His Nabi ﷺ. Let him then recite, "There is no illah but Allaah the Most Clement and Generous. Pure is Allaah the Rabb of the Magnificent Throne. All praise be to Allaah Rabb of all the worlds. I ask of You that which necessitates Your mercy, resolve which earns Your forgiveness, bounty of all good and safety from all wrong. Do not leave me with any sin except that You have forgiven it, no worry except that You ease it and no need with which You are pleased with except that You fulfil it, O Most Merciful of those who show mercy." [at-Tirmizi and Ibn Majah]
52 Jabir رضي الله عنه narrates: Rasulullaah ﷺ used to teach us Istikharah in all matters just as he taught us a Surah of the Quran. He said, "When a matter worries one of you, he should pray two Rak'at outside of the Fard and then say, .... [the famous Istikharah du'a]" [al-Bukhari]

quduri.f: How many Nafl Rak'at should be prayed with a single Salam?
quduri.b: In the day one may pray two or four Rak'at of Nafl with a single salam. More than that will be Makruh. At night one may pray up to 8 Rak'at with a single Salam according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the limit at night is two.

quduri.f: What do you say about someone who has started Nafl Salah and then broke it off?
quduri.b: Nafl becomes compulsory to complete once it has commenced. It should therefore be repeated.

quduri.f: If he intended four, sat in the second and broke off during the last two Rak'at, how many should he repeat? [i.e. Nafl Salah]
quduri.b: He should repeat two because the first pair was completed. Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى says that he should repeat all four.

quduri.f: Is it allowed to pray Nafl sitting when one is able to stand?
quduri.b: Yes, but the reward is halved.

quduri.f: What do you say about starting Nafl Salah standing and then sitting?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is allowed. His two companions say that it is only allowed with an excuse.

quduri.f: Is it allowed to pray Nafl on a beast?
quduri.b: Yes, one may pray riding on a beast, facing whatever direction the animal is facing and making the postures by indication. This is only allowed travelling out of the city.

quduri.f: When should one fulfil a missed Salah?
quduri.b: As soon as one remembers, except during the three times Salah is forbidden.

quduri.f: When a Salah has been missed, how does one fulfil it?
quduri.b: He should perform them in the ame order as they would originally have been prayed. This is Wajib on one who is Sahibut Tartib [one with sequence].

quduri.f: What does "One with sequence" mean?
quduri.b:
In the terminology of the Fuqaha one with less than six omitted Salah is called, "One with sequence." It is Wajib on him to fulfil the Salah which are on time as well as the missed ones in their correct sequence. It is Wajib on him to pray the omitted Salah in their correct order. He may not pray the "on time" Salah before the missed ones. If he does the opposite then he must repeat what he prayed.

For example, one of sequence prayed a missed 'Asr but he still has the missed Zhuhr to fulfil. It is Wajib on him to then pray the missed Zhuhr and repeat the missed 'Asr.

An example of "on-time" versus missed - a man of sequence remembered a missed Salah at the time of Zhuhr. He then prayed the Zhuhr before the missed Salah. It is Wajib for him to pray the missed Salah then repeat the Zhuhr.

quduri.f: Is sequence Wajib between Witr and Fard?
quduri.b: Yes. If he does pray the Witr before the 'Isha, then it is Wajib to repeat the Witr after praying 'Isha. If he fell asleep without having prayed Witr and dawn has set in, it is Wajib for him to pray Witr before he prays Fajr. If he does the opposite he must repeat Fajr.

quduri.f: Does the Wajib nature of sequence drop under any circumstances?
quduri.b:
Yes, it does in any of the following circumstances:
When the number of missed Salah reaches 6, excluding Witr.53 
Forgetting a missed Salah.
When running out of time.
When the missed Salah reaches 6, he may pray first whichever one he wishes to. He may pray the Salah which is "on time" even if he remembers that he has missed Salah.

When he forgets that he has a missed Salah and prays a Salah in its correct time that Salah is valid and need not be repeated.

If he awakens just before sunrise and he remembers that he has missed 'Isha or Witr, he should pray Fajr then and the 'Isha and Witr after the sun has sufficiently risen. He need not repeat Fajr, becaise sequence was dropped due to lack of time.

53 Ad-Durr al-Mukthar (488/1) states sequence is not necessary when time is short or when the missed Salah is forgotten. These are excuses. When they reach six according to belief they will be difficult to fulfil in sequence.

Ibn 'Abidin sayd in his Hashiyah that "according to belief" to exclude that which is Fard in practice, i.e. Witr. Even though sequence is Wajib between Witr and the others which are Fard, Witr will not be added to the missed ones in this instance because Witr is a completion of the deeds of the day and night. The numbers increase through the increase of times, and Witr does not have an independent time of its own.

quduri.f: What actions and words nullify Salah?
quduri.b:
The actions are:
Eating or drinking, even if forgetfully.

Performing many actions not of Salah.
Deliberately talking.
Walking three or more steps continuously.
Turning the chest away from the Qiblah.
Unconsciousness.
Insanity.
Hadath Akbar, whether through looking or nocturnal emission.
Standing in line with a woman who may be sexually desired in a general Salah in which she has joined from the Tahrimah and she is in the same place without any obstacle.
Fulfilling a Rukn [essential deed of Salah] with an exposed 'awrah or Najasah which prevents Salah.
Laughing so loud that you can hear your laugh.
The words are:
To speak a word, be it deliberately, forgetfully or by mistake.
Making Salam to someone.
Returning Salam verbally.
To sigh.
To groan.
To moan.
To verbally cry due to pain or calamity, but not due to remembering Jannah or Hell.
Replying to a sneezer, "May Allaah have mercy on you."
Replying "La ilaha illAllaah," to one asking about Allaah having a partner.
Saying "Inna lillah wa inna ilayhi raji'un," when hearing bad news.
Saying "Alhamdullilah," when hearing good news.
Saying "La ilaha illAllaah" or "SubhanAllaah" out of surprise.
Anything which is a reply or addressing someone, e.g. saying as speech, : Ya Yahya khuzil Kitaba biquwah - O Yahya take the Book with strength."
Rectifying someone who is not your Imam.
Such a mistake in Qira-ah or Takbir which corrupts the meaning, such as extending [madd] the Hamzah of Allaahu Akbar.54 
Twelve points of difference 

If one who performed Tayammum sees water whilst in Salah and he is able to use it.
He had wiped his Khuff and the time of wiping expired whilst in Salah.
He removed both his Khuff with minimal action.
He was unable to read Quran and then learnt an Aayah.
He was naked and found clothing.
He had to pray by indication and suddenly was able to make Ruku' and Sujud.
He remembered that he still had to pray the Salah which was before the one he was engaged in, and he was a man of sequence.
The Imam who could Qira-ah lost his Wudu and appointed one unable to read to continue the Salah.
The sun rose during Fajr.
The Waqt of 'Asr came during Jumu'ah.
He had wiped his bandage. It fell of and it proved to be healed.
A Mustahadah's bleeding stopped [woman who bleeds outside menses].
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى the Salah is void even if it occurs in the final sitting after sitting the duration of Tashshahud.

According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the Salah is complete if any of these scenarios occurred after sitting in the final sitting for the duration of Tashshahud.

54 It becomes a question, "is Allaah the greatest?"

quduri.f: List those Makruh acts which should not be done in Salah
quduri.b:
It is Makruh for the Musalli to:
To play with his body or clothing.
To move pebbles, unless they prevent him from Sujud. In that case he may level them once.
To pop or intertwine his fingers.
To place his hands at his waist.
To let his clothes hang down or pull them up.
To plait his hair.
To turn left or right by the movement of the neck.
To sit like a dog.
To spread one's arms on the ground in Sajdah.
To reply Salam with the hand.55 
To sit cross-legged, except with an excuse.
To wipe the dust off his forehead and nose.
To put something in his mouth which will prevent Qira-ah.
Anything which distracts one nad prevents concentration and humility is Makruh.
55 If he returns it verbally the Salah is nullified.

quduri.f: Explain the virtue of Jama'ah [congegration] and its status in Shari'ah.
quduri.b:
Jama'ah is Sunnah Muakkadah for men and has great reward. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Salah with jam'ah is 27 times greater than Salah alone." [al-Bukhari and Muslim from Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنه]
Abud Darda رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "There are never three people in a town or countryside who do not establish Salah together except that the devil overpowers them. So uphold Jama'ah for the wolf eats the far off sheep." [Ahmad, Abu Dawud and an-Nasai].
Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "By He who hold my life in His Hand! I feel like ordering firewood to be gathered. I shall then order Azan for Salah to be called and I'll order someone a man to lead the people while I go and burn the houses of those men who are still at home." [al-Bukhari]

quduri.f: Who is most entitled to be Imam?
quduri.b: The most entitled is he who has most knowledge of the Sunnah and Shari'ah, especially the rules of Salah. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى says that he who is most versed in reading Allah's Kitab is more entitled. If they are equal, then the most pious. If they are equal, then the eldest.

quduri.f: Are there people whom it is Makruh to make Imam?
quduri.b: Yes, it is Makruh to make Imam a slave, a Bedouin, an open sinner, a blind man who is not careful with purity and illegitimate offspring. Nevertheless, if they lead the Salah remains valid.

quduri.f: May women attend Jama'ah in the Masjid?
quduri.b: It is Makruh. Their homes are better for them. Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى said that an old woman who does not display beauty may attend Fajr, Maghrib and 'Isha. Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى said that she may attend all Salah.

quduri.f: What do you say about a Jama'ah of women?
quduri.b: It is Makruh. If however it is done, then the Imam will stand in their centre just as when there is a Jama'ah of naked people.

quduri.f: Where does the follower stand if he is alone with the Imam?
quduri.b: The Imam will place him at his right. If more join in he will move forward.

quduri.f: If there is only one woman follower, where does she stand with the male Imam?
quduri.b: Behind him.

quduri.f: If the followers ar emen, women and children, how do they stand?
quduri.b: The men will first form their rows behind the Imam, then the children, then hermaphrodites then women.

quduri.f: What are the rules of following the Imam?
quduri.b:
The details are as follows:
One praying Fard can pray behind an Imam praying Fard, if both are praying the same Fard. When they differ, it is not allowed to follow, e.g. one prays Zhuhr and the other 'Asr; or one prays the Zhuhr of today and the other the Zhuhr of yesterday.
One with Tayammum can lead those with Wudu.
One who has wiped his Khuff can lead those who washed their feet.
One praying sitting due to illness can lead those praying standing.
One who must perform full Ruku' and Sajdah cannot follow one who makes by indication.

One praying Nafl can follow one praying Fard.
The opposite is not allowed.
A non-excused cannot follow an excused, e.g. a man with continous urine or passing wind or a wound which is not stopping cannot lead a man who is healthy and has proper purity.
A pure woman cannot follow a Mustahadah.
One able to recite Qira-ah cannot follow one who is unable to read the minimum Fard Qira-ah.
A clothed person cannot follow a naked person.

quduri.f: What should a follower do when he learns that Imam did not have Taharah?
quduri.b: He must repeat the Salah.

quduri.f: 56 What should a Munfarid do if he completed a Rak'ah of Zhuhr or 'Isha with the Sujud and congegrational Salah commences?57
quduri.b:
He adds another Rak'ah and joins the Jama'ah.58

56 This part is not in al-Quduri. The author of this book added it from Fat-hul Qadir and al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah.
57 i.e. actual Salah of the Imam commences, not merely Iqamah. In that case if the Munfarid did not complete the Rak'ah with Sujud, he completes the two Rak'at. There is no difference amongst our 'Ulama about this. [an-Nihayah] [Refer to al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah (119/1)]
58 What does he do if he was sitting in Tashshahud of the second Rak'ah of Zhuhr or 'Isha and Jama'ah commences? He will make Salam after the Tashahud and join the Imam.

quduri.f: If he did not yet make Sajdah? [i.e. a Munfarid when congregational Salah commences]
quduri.b: He will break off his Salah and begin with the Imam.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he completed the Sajdah of the third Rak'ah of Zhuhr or Asr and Jama'ah commences?
quduri.b: He will complete his Salah and follow the Imam as Nafl.

quduri.f: If he did not yet make Sajdah of the third Rak'ah? [i.e. the Munfarid when congegrational Salah commences]
quduri.b: He will break off his Salah and join the Imam.

quduri.f: How does he break off? [i.e. the Munfarid when congegrational Salah commences]
quduri.b: He has a choice. If he wishes he can sit and make one Salam; or he recite Takbir standing and intend joining the Salah of the Imam. In that way both the breaking off the Salah he was praying as well as the joining with the Imam's Salah is achieved.

quduri.f: Explain what happens in 'Asr [i.e. the Munfarid when congegrational Salah commences].
quduri.b: If the Munfarid performed one or three Rak'at and the Jama'ah commenced then the ruling is the same as we mentioned in breaking off or completing in Zhuhr and 'Isha. The difference is that he will not join the Imam after completing 4 Rak'at because Nafl after 'Asr is Makruh.

quduri.f: What does a Munfarid do if he has prayed a Rak'ah or two of the Fard of Fajr or Maghrib and the Jama'ah commences.
quduri.b: If he has prayed a Rak'ah of Maghrib or Fajr he must break off his Salah whether he made Sajdah or not. He will also break off if he did not complete the Sajdah of the second Rak'ah. He will then join the Imam in these three scenarios. If he has made Sajdah of the second Rak'ah he will complete the Salah and not break it.

quduri.f: Will he [i.e. the Munfarid: see question 203] then join the Imam after completing as above?
quduri.b:
He will not join the Imam in this case.59

59 The author of al-Kanz says, "If he prayed a Rak'ah of Fajr or Maghrib and Jama'ah begins, he should break off and join the Imam."

quduri.f: What should a man do who has begun his Sunnah before Zhuhr or Jumu'ah and the Jama'ah or Khutbah begins?
quduri.b:
He makes Salam at the end of two Rak'at and then joins the Imam in Zhuhr or listens to the Khutbah as the case may be.60 

60 That has been narrated from Abu Yusuf رحمه الله. It is also said that he should complete it. [al-Hidayah]. Ibn Humam says in Fathul Qadir that completing Salam upon two Rakat is better because he can complete it after the Fard and the two Rak'at are not null by making the Salam. He thus neither omits the Fard of listening nor misses his Salah without excuse.

quduri.f: If he began Nafl and the Jama'ah began?
quduri.b: He should complete the pair he is engaged in and not increase upon it.

quduri.f: A man reaches the Imam who is praying Fajr, and the man did not yet pray the two Sunnah before. What should he do?
quduri.b:
If he fears that he will miss a Rak'ah but will at least gain the second Rak'ah, he should pray the two Rak'at Sunnah at the Masjid entrace and then join the Imam. If he fears that he will miss both, then he should leave the Sunnah and join the Imam.61

61 That is per al-Hidayah. Al-Kafiyah states, "The book does not mention what he should do if he thinks he will at least get the final sitting, but it is obvious from the statement that if he fears missing both Rak'at he should join the Imam, hence in this situation he should also join the Imam. The Faqih Abu Ja'far narrates a view of Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى that he should pray the Sunnah, because according to them attaining the Tashshahud is like attaining the Rak'ah."
Al-Hidayah states, "The stipulation of praying at the entrance of the Masjid is due to it being Makruh to pray whilst the Imam is in Salah."

quduri.f: Someone missed Fajr and intends to pray it after sunrise. Should he pray the Sunnah as well or is the Fard sufficient?
quduri.b:
He should pray the Sunnah as subsidiary to the Fard if he fulfils it before Zawal. If after Zawal then he should only pray the Fard.62

62 Al-Hidayah states that there is a difference amongst the Mashaikh regarding after Zawal.

quduri.f: If he did not pray the Sunnahs of Fajr due to joining the Imam or due to lack of time, when should he make it up?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is not made up, whether before or after sunrise. Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى said, "I prefer that it be made between sunrise and Zawal."

quduri.f: If he misses the Sunnah before Zhuhr, when should he make it up?
quduri.b: He should pray it after the Fard of Zhuhr in its time. If the time passes then it is not performed.

quduri.f: If he is intending to pray the Sunnah which he missed before the Fard, after the Fard, must he pray four missed Rak'at first or the two which come after the Fard?
quduri.b:
He should first pray the two Rak'at then the missed four.63

63 There is a difference on what is preferred. Al-Kanz states that the four are performed before the two.
Ibnul Hamam said in Fatahul Qadir, "Praying the two first is better because that is its Sunnah time. The Sunnah time of the four has been lost. The Sunnah time of the two should not now also be lost without necessity.

quduri.f: If one misses the Sunnah before Jumu'ah should one pray it after Jumu'ah?
quduri.b: Yes, and its rules are the same as the four Rak'at before Zhuhr.

quduri.f: What should a Musalli do if afflicted with Hadath during Salah?
quduri.b: He should leave the Salah, renew his Wudu and continue his Salah where he left off. To start anew is better.

quduri.f: If he is the Imam [i.e. when afflicted with Hadath during Salah], what should he do with the followers?
quduri.b: He appoints one of the followers as Imam and the new Imam completes the remainder of the Salah.

quduri.f: What if the appointed one is a Masbuq [did not join the Salah from the beginning] [i.e. if the Imam is afflicted with Hadath during Salah]?
quduri.b: He will lead the others for the rest of the Salah and then appoint a Mudrik (one who had joined the Salah from the beginning) and the Mudrik will complete the Salam as the Imam.

quduri.f: What should the Musalli do if Hadath afflicts him after he sat for the duration of Tashshahud in a sitting when he must make Salam?
quduri.b: He should leave the Salah, make Wudu and complete the Salam.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he spoke after the Hadath?
quduri.b: His Salah is void and he cannot continue it, whether he spoke deliberately, forgetfully or by mistake.

quduri.f: If that Musalli needs to walk to some place for Wudu or turns away from Qiblah for that purpose does his Salah break?
quduri.b: No, that is overlooked even if he walks three steps or more.

quduri.f: If Hadath Akbar afflicts the Musalli, can he continue with the Salah [after purity]?
quduri.b: He who sleeps in Salah and has Ihtilam, or becomes mad, or becomes unconscious, or laughs loudly in Salah, then the Salah is nullified. He cannot continue it. He should start his Salah anew after Ghusl in the first case and after Wudu in the remaining three cases.

quduri.f: What should a Musalli do when forgetful in Salah?
quduri.b:
If he adds an action which is an act of Salah, e.g. he repeated the Ruku' or added a Rak'ah, or he forgets a Wajib, e.g. he forgot al-Fatihah or the Sunan after it, or the first sitting or one of the two Tashshahud, or Qunut in Witr, or the Takbirs of 'Id, or the Imam read aloud in a soft Salah or soft in a loud Salah; then Sujudus Sahw must be made. It is two Sajdahs after the final Tashshahud then one Salam is made then another Tashshahud and then Salam is made.65

65 The preferred view is that he recite Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ and du'a in the final sitting. It is also said that he should recite in both sittings as a precaution.

quduri.f: Is Sujudus Sahw Wajib on the followers if the Imam makes a mistake?
quduri.b: Yes, it is Wajib on the Imam and the followers.

quduri.f: If the Imam does not make the Sujud what does the follower do?
quduri.b: Then the follower will also not make Sujud.

quduri.f: If the follower forgets, does he have to make Sujud [Sahw]?
quduri.b: Neither he nor the Imam will make Sujud.

quduri.f: What should someone do if he forgets the first sitting in a three or four Rak'ah Salah?
quduri.b: He should examine his state. If he is closer to sitting, he should return to the sitting, recite Tashshahud and complete the rest of the Salah. There is no Sujudus Sahw. If however he is closer to standing then he should not return to sitting but continue to the standing position and complete his Salah. After the final Tashshahud he should make Sujudus Sahw and make Salam.

quduri.f: What must he do if he forgot the final sitting?
quduri.b: If he forgot to sit in a 4 Rak'at Salah and stood for the fifth Rak'ah without having yet made Sajdah, then he should abandon the fifth Rak'ah and return to the sitting. He should make Sujudus Sahw.

quduri.f: What must he do if he made the Sajdah of the fifth Rak'ah [i.e. if he forgot the final sitting]?
quduri.b:
The Fard status of the Salah is nullified because the Fard of the final sitting has been omitted. It now becomes Nafl and he should add a sixt Rak'ah.66 

NOTE: Deduce from the above rule what to do when one forgets the final sitting in a two or three Rak'at Salah.

66 If he does not add the extra Rak'ah, there is nothing against him as per al-Hidayah. Does he make Sujudus Sahw? Fathul Qadir states, "There is no Sajdah because the deficiency of nullification is not repaired with Sajdah."

quduri.f: What should he do if he sat in the Tashshahud of the fourth Rak'ah then rose thinking that it was the second Rak'ah and remembered the correct number?
quduri.b: He should return and sit if he did not make Sajdah for the fith Rak'ah. He should make Sujudus Sahw and his Salah is valid.

quduri.f: And if he did make Sajdah of the fifth Rak'ah? [i.e. if he sat in Tashshahud of the fourth Rak'ah then rose thinking that it was the second Rak'ah]
quduri.b: He will continue with a sixth Rak'ah and make Sujudus Sahw. The first four Rak'at are those he intended at Tahrimah and extra two are Nafl.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of one who is doubting in his Salah if he prayed three or four Rak'at?
quduri.b:
If that is the first time that happened in his life he must start the Salah anew. If it happened often then he should continue with what he thinks to be most probable and sit at every possibility of sitting.67 If he does not have a probable thought then he should continue with what he is certain of, i.e. the least amount and make Sujudus Sahw in both situations.68 

67 Al-'Inayah gives an example: If the doubt arose in a 4 Rak'at Salah whether it is the first or second Rak'ah he should act upon whatever his self-examination says. If there is no conclusion then, he should make it the least, i.e. the first Rak'ah. Yet he should sit on the possibility that it is the second for the sitting is Wajib. Then in his next Rak'ah he must sit again because he has acted on it being the second. In his next Rak'ah he must sit on the possibility that it is the fourth Rak'ah. In the Rak'ah thereafter he must sit because he has acted on it being the fourth in which sitting is Fard. Deduce the same rule on a three Rak'at Salah.
68 Al-Quduri does not mention Sujudus Sahw when continuing on the least or on the most probable. 
Ad-Durr al-Mukthar mentions that Sujudus Sahw is Wajib in all scenarios of doubt, whether it be self-examinatio nor continuing on the least.
As-Siraj states that Sujudus Sahw is made when one continues on the least; and when he acts on the most probable thought after thinking for the duration of a Rukn.
The text of al-Fath is as follows, "If his examination reveals something he will complete his Salah upon that and make Sujudus Sahw. Similarly in all scenarios of examination or continuing on the least Sujudus Sahw will be made... if his examination does not reveal anything then he will continue on the least.
Ibn 'Abidin ash-Shami supports this in as-Siraj, "When he ponders and his thought reaches a probability, then it is compulsary for him to act upon it. There is no cause for Sujud to be Wajib on him except if he takes long to think as has been explained."
I say that what is in al-Fath is correct because it is supported by an authentic Hadith of al-Bukhari and Muslim. 'Abdullaah bin Mas'ud رضي الله عنه narrates from Rasulullaah ﷺ, "When one of you doubts in his Salah let him ponder what is correct and complete upon that. Then he should make Salam and two Sajdah."
There is no Nass [explicit text] in the clause of Sajdah becoming Wajib when thinking long. It is however a cause for Sajdah according to the Ahnaf when one pauses for the duration of a Rukn without Qira-ah.

quduri.f: What is the reality of a single Sajdah we see readers of the Quran performing during their Tilawah [recitation]?
quduri.b: That Sajdah is callled Sajdatut Tilawah. It is Wajib upon one who recites or hears an Aayah of Sajdah, whether he intended to hear the Aayah or not.

quduri.f: What are the numbers of these Aayat [i.e. for Sajda Tilawah] and in which Surahs do they occur?
quduri.b:
They occur in the following 14 Surahs:
al-A'raf
ar-Ra'd
an-Nakhl
al-Isra
Maryam
al-Hajj
al-Furqan
an-Naml
Alif Lam Mim Sajdah
Sad
Ha Mim Sajdah
an-Najm
al-Inshiqaq
al-'Alaq
The Aayat of Sajdah are well known amongst those who memorise the Quran, and signs are indicated in the Mus-haf as well.

quduri.f: When the Imam recites an Aayah of Sajdah, is it Wajib upon the followes to make Sajdah as well?
quduri.b: Whether the Imam reads it softly or loudly and makes Sajdah, the followers will make Sajdah with him.

quduri.f: If the follower recites the Aayah of Sajdah, is the Sajdah necessary upon him and the Imam?
quduri.b: It is not compulsory upon either one of them.

quduri.f: Is the Sajdah [Tilawah] Wajib upon people who are in Salah, and they hear a man who is not with them in Salah reciting a Sajdah Aayah?
quduri.b: It is Wajib, but they should make it after Salah, not during it.

quduri.f: If they perform it in Salah [i.e. people who are in Salah and they hear a man who is not with them in Salah reciting a Sajdah Aayah], will it suffice?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Will that extra Sajdah nullify their Salah?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man read an Aayah of Sajdah outside of Salah. He does not make the Sajdah. He then performs Salah and recites the same Aayah in it. If he performs a Sajdah for it, will it suffice for both recitations?
quduri.b: Yes, if both recitations were in the same Majlis [place and time].

quduri.f: What do you say about a man who read a Sajdah Aayah outside of Salah and made the Sajdah; then he commenced Salah and read the same Aayah in it. Does his first Sajdah suffice?
quduri.b: It does not suffice. He must make another Sajdah for that recitation.

quduri.f: Does one Sajdah suffice for repeating the same Sajdah Aayah?
quduri.b: One Sajdah will suffice if he repeats the same Aayah in the same Majlis. If he changes Majlis, the Sajdah equal to the number of Majlis is Wajib upon him. If he reads several Aayat of Sajdah, he must make Sajdah for each Aayah, even if it be in the same Majlis.

quduri.f: How should Sajdatul Tilawah be made?
quduri.b: Recite Takbir without raising the hands. Make a Sajdah then say Takbir and arise. There is no Tashshahud or Salam.

quduri.f: How should a sick person who cannot stand pray?
quduri.b: A sick person who is unable to stand in Salah, should sit and make Ruku' and Sujud.

quduri.f: If he is unable to make Sajdah and Ruku'? [i.e. the sick person]
quduri.b: He should indicate Ruku' and Sujud. The Sujud should be lower than the Ruku'. He should not raise anything to his head to prostrate thereon.

quduri.f: If he is unable to sit? [i.e. the sick person]
quduri.b: He should lie on his back with his legs towards the Qiblah with something below his head to raise it. He should face the Qiblah and pray like that, lying down and doing Ruku' and Sujud by indication.

quduri.f: What do you say about one who prays, laying on his side?
quduri.b: It is permissible if he lies on his side, praying with his face to the Qiblah and indicating his Ruku' and Sujud.

quduri.f: If he is unable to indicate with his head [i.e. the sick person], can he indicate with his eyes, eyebrows or heart?
quduri.b: He cannot indicate with anything besides his head. If he is unable to, then he should delay his Salah until he can.

quduri.f: How should one who can stand but cannot make Ruku' or Sujud pray?
quduri.b: Standing in not obligatory in that situation. It is best for him to pray sitting and by indications. If he stands and indicates then it is also permissible.

quduri.f: If someone was healthy and praying his Salah standing, then he became sick, how should he complete his Salah?
quduri.b: He should sit and make Ruku' and Sujud. If he cannot make Ruku' and Sujud he must make them by indication. If he cannot sit then he must lie down and indicate.

quduri.f: If someone was praying whilst sitting due to sickness and made Ruku' and Sujud, then became healthy during the Salah, does he begin his Salah anew?
quduri.b: No, he continues and stands.

quduri.f: If he prayed part of the Salah with indications and then became able to make Ruku' and Sujud, must he continue the Salah?
quduri.b: He must not continue. He must begin anew.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Salah missed due to unconsciousness?
quduri.b: He who is unconscious for five or less Salah must pray them when he gains consciousness. When he misses more than that, he does not pray.

quduri.f: Are there separate laws in Shari'ah pertaining to travellers?
quduri.b: Yes, there are separate laws mentioned in the relevant chapters of the books of Fiqh.

quduri.f: Explain those laws relating to Salah.
quduri.b: When he intends travelling the distance covered in three day's travelling by camel or foot and will leave his city or town, he will reduce [Qasr] his four Rak'at Salah i.e. he will only pray two Rak'at for Zhuhr, 'Asr and 'Isha. There is no reduction in Maghrib, Fajr, Witr, Sunan and Nafl.

quduri.f: Will he be rewarded for praying four Rak'at when he should have made Qasr?
quduri.b: His extra two Rak'at are Makruh. Qasr is emphasised.

quduri.f: Although Makruh, if he prayed four Rak'at, has his Fard obligation been fulfilled?
quduri.b: If he prayed four and sat in the second Rak'ah for the duration of Tashshahud then the first two suffice for his Fard and the next two are Nafl.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he did not sit in the second Rak'ah the duration of Tashshahud?
quduri.b: The Fard status of the Salah is void and becomes becomes Nafl. He must pray his Fard again.

quduri.f: Are there situations where a traveller prays four Rak'at?
quduri.b: Yes, if he is following a resident Imam or he has intended to stay at a town for 15 days or more.

quduri.f: If he intends staying less than 15 days?
quduri.b: He will continue Qasr, not complete [4].

quduri.f: A traveller enters a town and does not intend staying 15 days, but says, "I might go tomorrow or the day thereafter." What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He will continue Qasr even if it goes on for years.

quduri.f: The Muslim army enters the land of the enemy and intends staying 15 days. Do they pray the complete four?
quduri.b: They will continue Qasr because their intention is not definite.

quduri.f: A traveller leads residents in a four Rak'at Salah. Does he make Qasr?
quduri.b: Yes. The residents will complete their four Rak'at when the travelling Imam makes his Salam upon the second Rak'at.

quduri.f: Does the travelling Imam make any announcement to the followers?
quduri.b: Yes, it is Mustahab for the Imam to announce after Salam, "Complete your Salah for verily we are a travelling people."

quduri.f: If a traveller intends staying at Makkah and Mina for fifteen days is he a traveller or resident?
quduri.b: He is still a traveller because the intention of residence is based on a single habitation.

quduri.f: A traveller has returned to his town and did not intend to stay for 15 days. Does he complete or shorten his Salah?
quduri.b: He will complete four Rak'at when entering his town, however short the period. There is no condition of having to intend to stay.

quduri.f: A man was born in a town and lived there for years. He then made another town his hometown. He then enters the first town for some need. Does he complete or shorten his Salah?
quduri.b: He will make Qasr if the first town is the distance of three days journey or more from his new town. The Nabi ﷺ made Hijrah from Makkah to al-Madinah and made Qasr when he went to Makkah.

quduri.f: A traveller missed a Salah and upon entering his town wishes to pray it; or a resident missed a Salah and now wishes to pray while on travel. What do they do?
quduri.b: The principle behind it is that Qada [compensation Salah] is like Ada [original]. One who missed a Salah in travel makes it up as two Rak'at even when already at home. A Salah missed at home is fulfilled as four even when done during travel.

quduri.f: Is Qasr for an obedient traveller only or for sinners as well?
quduri.b: Both.

quduri.f: In this era people travel by car and plane and do not feel difficulty in it. Do they make Qasr despite that?
quduri.b: If they leave their hometowns intending a journey of three days distance then they will make Qasr. They journey in itself is in a place of the difficulty of journey.

quduri.f: Is a traveller allowed to join between two Salah, such as Zhuhr and 'Asr and Maghrib and 'Isha?
quduri.b: It is allowed in practice when the two times join, but not in each others' times. Allaah says, "Verily Salah is prescribed upon the believers at set times."

quduri.f: What do you mean it is allowed in practice but not in each other's times? [i.e. combining between two Salah]
quduri.b: A joining in practice is to delay Zhuhr and hasten 'Asr. Zhuhr is prayed right at the end of its Waqt and 'Asr right at the beginning of its Waqt. Similarly Maghrib is prayed at the end of its Waqt and 'Isha at its beginning. This is joining in practice and is called "Jam' Suwari" [Joining in Form] in the terminology of the Fuqaha. According to us a Salah in the time of the other is not allowed, whether delaying or bringing ahead. That is joining in a Waqt which the Fuqaha call, "Jam' Haqiqi" [Real Joining].

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Salatul Jumu'ah?
quduri.b: It is Fard 'Ayn [obligatory on each individual] on male who is free, mature, intelligent, and healthy, can see and is resident.

quduri.f: Are there conditions to establish it? [i.e. Salatul Jumu'ah]
quduri.b:
Yes, they are as follows:
That it be in a city or the prayer grounds of a city. It is not allowed in villages.
That the Sultan or one whom he orders establishes it. Or that the Muslims agree on it and appoint an Imam to lead them in Jumu'ah.70 
It has to be in the Waqt of Zhuhr. It is not valid before or after that.
A Khutbah [lecture] before the Salah. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى a concise mention of Allaah will suffice. According to the other two Imams a lengthy discourse which can be called a lecture is necessary.
A congregration. The minimum according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى is three, excluding the Imam. Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى said that the minimum is two, excluding the Imam.71
70 Al-Quduri only said, "That the Sultan or one whom he orders establishes it." The author added, "Or that the Muslims agree on it and appoint an Imam to lead them in Jumu'ah." Al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah quotes Ma 'arijud Dirayah, "In lands where the rulers are Kuffar the Muslims may establish Jumu'ah and a judge may be appointed with their consent. It is Wajib upon them to seek a Muslim ruler." (146/1 - Egyptian Edition)
Ibn 'Abidin ash-Shami has also quoted it like that from Ma'araijud Dirayah in Raddul Muhtar (540/1).

71 Neither al-Quduri nor al-Hidayah mentions general permission to attend as a condition for the validity for Jumu'ah. It is however mentioned in the books of the Ahnaf. It means that the doors of the Masjid should be open and all people allowed to enter. If a group enters and then locks the door upon themselves, then it is not valid as per al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah quoting al-Muhit. Ash-Shami mentions in his commentary on ad-Durr al-Muhtar, "This condition is not mentioned in the Zhahirur Riwayah nor in al-Hidayah. It is mentioned in an-Nawadir. Al-Kanz, al-Wiqayah, an-Niqayah, al-Multaqi and other reliable texts rule according to it."

quduri.f: List those reasons which excuse one from attending Jumu'ah
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
One who travelled the distance of Qasr.
Women are excused.
Sickness.
Blindness.
One is a slave.
It is thus not obligatory upon a traveller, woman, ill, blind or slave.

quduri.f: If these people [i.e. those who are excused, see question 272) attend Jumu'ah have they fulfilled the Fard of that Waqt?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Is the Salah of the Imam and followers valid if a slave, sick man, traveller or blind man leads freemen, healthy men and residents for Jumu'ah?
quduri.b: Yes, it is allowed and the Jumu'ah is valid.

quduri.f: What should one who has missed Jumu'ah for a reason do?
quduri.b: He should pray Zhuhr as should one who did not attend Jumu'ah without a valid reason. If he did not have a valid reason he has sinned.

quduri.f: Is it allowed to pray Zhuhr at home without any reason, before the Imam prays Jumu'ah?
quduri.b: He has committed a sin.

quduri.f: If he did that anyway [i.e. pray Zhuhr at home without any reason before the Imam prays Jumu'ah] and the Waqt of Zhuhr passes, has his Salah fulled fthe Fard of that Waqt?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he goes to join the Imam for Jumu'ah after having prayed his own Zhuhr?
quduri.b: The Jumu'ah is valid. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى the Zhuhr is void as soon as he sets off for Jumu'ah. According to his two companions it is void when he joins the Imam in the Salah of Jumu'ah.

quduri.f: Should those who are excused and prisoners pray Zhuhr in congegration on the Day of Jumu'ah?
quduri.b: It is Makruh. They should pray individually.

quduri.f: What should one who has missed a Rak'ah of Jumu'ah do?
quduri.b: Continue and then pray what was missed.

quduri.f: What should he do [one who has missed a Rak'ah of Jumu'ah] if he gains the Salah when the Imam is in Tashshahud or Sujudus Sahw?
quduri.b: He should continue the missed Rak'at of Jumu'ah according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى, if he attained most of the second Rak'ah, he should continue with Jumu'ah. If less, then he will continue with Zhuhr, i.e. he will pray four Rak'at with that Tahrimah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of buying and selling after the Azan of Jumu'ah?
quduri.b: "When the call is made for the Salah of Jumu'ah then hasten to the remembrance of Allaah and leave of trade." [Quran]

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Salah and talking after the Imam emerges?
quduri.b: When the Imam emerges, the people should not pray Salah or talk until he completes his Khutbah according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. According to his two companions there is no harm in talking as long as he did not begin the Khutbah.

quduri.f: How many times is Azan called for Jumu'ah?
quduri.b:
Twice:
When the sun drops from its zenith then they should turn their attention to Jumu'ah. They must leave trade and hasten to the remembrance of Allah.
When the Imam ascends the Mimbar [pulpit] and sits on it. Azan is then called in front of him. The Imam then gives two Khutbah after which the Salah commences.

quduri.f: Describe the Sunnah Khutbah.
quduri.b: The Imam will stand and give two Khutbahs, sitting a while in between them.

quduri.f: Does the Imam read a loud or soft Qira-ah during Jumu'ah?
quduri.b: Loud.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of listening carefully to the Khutbah if one is far?
quduri.b: The far one is like the near one. Listening carefully and maintaining silence is Wajib whether one is near or far, whether one can hear the Imam or not.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Salah of the two 'Id?
quduri.b: It is Wajib upon whomever Jumu'ah is Wajib upon.

quduri.f: What are the beginning and end times for it?
quduri.b: The beginning time is when Salah becomes permissible when the sun is high enough. The end time is when the sun drops from its high point. It is Mustahab to hasten the Salah on 'Idul Adha because the sacrifices follow the Salah. It is Mustahab to delay it on 'Idul Fitr.

quduri.f: What are the Sunan of the two days of 'Id?
quduri.b: It is Mustahab on the two days to use Miswak, make Ghusl, apply fragrance and wear one's best clothes. On the Day of Fitr eat an odd number of dates or something sweet and pay the Sadaqatul Fitr before going to the Musalla. On the Day of Adha delay eating until the return from the Musalla when Udhiyah is made and eat from it.

quduri.f: Is Takbir proclaimed on the way when going to the Salah of the two 'Id?
quduri.b:
Takbir is reciting loudly on the way to the Musalla on the Day of Adha according to our three Imams. On the Day of Fitr Takbir is recited according to the two besides Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى.72

72 That is according to al-Quduri. According to al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah Takbir is recited loudly on the way on al-Adha and stops when one reaches the Musalla. On the Day of Fitr the preferred view is that it is not recited loudly. It is Mustahad to recite softly as per al-Jawharah an-Nayirah (150/1). This shows that the difference regarding Takbir on Fitr is regarding method and not the Takbir itself. See Ibn 'Abidin's commentary on ad-Durr al-Mukthar (558/1).

quduri.f: Is there a known Sunnah regarding going to the Musalla?
quduri.b: It is Mustahab when going for either 'Id Salah or take one route and to return on another,

quduri.f: Can one pray Nafl in the Musalla before Salatul 'Id?
quduri.b: No Nafl is prayed in the Musalla before 'Id Salah or afterwards.

quduri.f: Describe the method of 'Id Salah.
quduri.b: The Imam and the people will come out of their habitations to the outskirts of the city. The Imam will lead the people in two Rak'at. He will commence with Takbiratul Ihram, then Thana, then three loud Takbir, raising his hands with each Takbir. He will then recite Ta'awuz and Bismillah softly. He will then recite al-Fatihah and a Surah loudly. He will then complete the remainder of the Rak'ah like any other Rak'ah. He will rise for the second Rak'ah, recite Bismillah softly and al-Fatihah and a Surah loudly. After the Qira-ah he will loudly recite Takbir thrice, raisign the hands of each time. He will then recite Takbir for a fourth time to go into Ruku'. He will not raise his hands this fourth time. The Rak'ah will then be completed as in any other Salah. He will make Salam after Tashshahud, Salah 'alan Nabi ﷺ and du'a.

quduri.f: Are the hands left hanging at the sides or placed below the navel between the extra Takbirs?
quduri.b: They are left hanging after all extra Takbirs except for the third Takbir in the first Rak'ah after which he will place his hands under the navel.

quduri.f: Those are the actions of the Imam [i.e. regarding leaving the hands during the Takbirs of 'Id]. What do the followers do?
quduri.b: The followers will imitate him in all acts except three things which they do not do - Ta'awwuz, Bismillah and Qira-ah. They will not make Takbir loudly but softly.

quduri.f: Is there Khutbah in the Salah of the two 'Ids?
quduri.b: Yes, two Khutbahs in each Salah is Sunnah. The Imam will deliver the Khutbah, teaching the people the laws of 'Id such as Sadaqatul Fitr in the Khutbah of 'Idul Fitr; and the laws of Udhiyah and Takbir of Tashriq in the Khutbah of al-Adha.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Khutbahs of the two 'Ids?
quduri.b: They are Sunnah and are delivered after Salah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling for those present to listen carefully?
quduri.b: Listening carefully and keeping silent is Wajib in every Khutbah, be it that of Jumu'ah or 'Id.

quduri.f: A man was delayed and missed the 'Id Salah. Does he pray it afterwards [Qada]?
quduri.b: There is no Qada of 'Id Salah.

quduri.f: If the new moon was covered by clouds and the Imam received testimony of the moon's sighting after Zawal, when will 'Id Salah be prayed?
quduri.b: The next day.

quduri.f: When will it [i.e. 'Id Salah] be prayed if something prevents the people from praying it the next day?
quduri.b: It will not be prayed after the second day.

quduri.f: When will the Salah be prayed if some obstacle arises on the Day of al-Adha?
quduri.b: It will be prayed the next day or the day thereafter, but not after that.

quduri.f: What is the Takbir of Tashriq?
quduri.b:
To recite after every Fard Salah73, "Allaahu Akbar! Allaahu Akbar! La ilaha illAllaah. WAllaahu Akbar, Allaahu Akbar, wa lillahil hamd."

73 There is no harm to recite it after 'Id because it has been the constant practice of the Muslims. To follow them is Wajib. The 'Ulama of Balk have ruled accordingly. [ad-Durr al-Mukthar]. The meaning of no harm here means it is recommended [ad-Durr al-Mukthar (564/1)].

quduri.f: What are the beginning and final times of this Takbir [i.e. of Tashriq]?
quduri.b: It begins after the Fajr of the Day of 'Arafah. The last is after 'Asr of the Day of Nahr. This is according to Imaam ABu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. According to his two companions it ends after 'Asr of the final day of Tashriq. The Fatwa is according to them.

quduri.f: Is this Takbir [i.e. of Tashriq] loud or soft?
quduri.b: The Imam and followers will recite aloud, women soft.

quduri.f: If the Imam forgets the Takbir of Tashriq, will the follower recite it?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: What is the Status of this Takbir? [i.e. of Tashriq]
quduri.b:
It is Wajib upon one who has prayed any of the five Fard or Jumu'ah. It is read immediately after Salam.75

75 The meaning of immediately is to recite it without such a pause which prevents one from continuing Slah. Thus if he leaves the Masjid, talks deliberately or accidentally, or breaks his Wudu deliberately then the Takbir falls away. There are two views regarding turning one's back to the Qiblah. As for falling into Hadath unintentionally after Salam then the more correct opinion is to read Takbir and not to go and renew Wudu. [Raddul Muhtar (562/1)]

quduri.f: What are the Muslims commanded to do when the sun eclipses?
quduri.b: The Imam will lead the Muslims in two Rak'at without any Azan or Iqamah. It will be prayed in the form of Nafl i.e. 1 Ruku'and 2 Sajdah per Rak'ah. The Imam will lengthen the Qira-ah and then offer du'a until the sun appears.

quduri.f: Is the Qira-ah in it [i.e. in Salatul Kusuf (Eclipse prayer)] loud or soft?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is soft and according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is loud.

quduri.f: Which Imam will lead the people in this Salah [i.e. in Salatul Kusuf (Eclipse prayer)]?
quduri.b: The Imam who leads them in Jumu'ah.

quduri.f: If the Jumu'ah Imam is not present [i.e. in Salatul Kusuf (Eclipse prayer)]?
quduri.b: The people will pray individually.

quduri.f: Is there a Khutbah in this Salah [i.e. in Salatul Kusuf (Eclipse prayer)]?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What do the Muslims do when the moon exclipses?
quduri.b: Pray individually.

quduri.f: Is there any other action besides Salah in the two eclipses?
quduri.b:
'Aishah رضي الله عنها narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Verily the sun and the moon are signs from amongst Allaah's signs. They do not eclipse due to the death or life of anyone. When you see that, make du'a to Allaah, Salah and Sadaqah."76
