Asma رضي الله عنها narrated, "The Nabi ﷺ commanded that we set slaves free during solar eclipse."77 

76 Al-Bukhari, Chapter on charity during eclipse.
77 Al-Hidayah states, "Rasulullaah ﷺ did it once and did not do it the next tiem, so it is not Sunnah."
Ash-Shami states in Raddul Muhtar, "That is because a Sunnah is what he constantly acted upon. Doing it once and then leaving it means that it is recommended."

quduri.f: What is the meaning of Istisqa?
quduri.b: Seeking rain when afflicted by drought.

quduri.f: What is done in Salatul Istisqa?
quduri.b: There is a Shar'i basis for the Salah but it is not Wajib. It is allowed to suffice on du'a and seeking forgiveness. Sometimes Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed Istisqa and sometimes he did not pray it, but made du'a for rain whilst on the Mimbar for Jumu'ah. All that is established from him ﷺ.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of the words of Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى found in the books of Fiqh, "There is no Sunnah Salah for Istisqa."?
quduri.b: It means that Salah is not specified in Istisqa, it is not Sunnah Muakkadah that Istisqa is not valid without the Salah (e.g. du'a).

quduri.f: How will the Imam lead the people in the Salah? [i.e. Istisqa]
quduri.b: The Imam and the people will walk to the outskirts of the city with humility. They will display meekness to Allaah and lower their heads. The Imam will pray two Rak'at with loud Qira-ah. He will face the people and deliver two Khutbahs. He will invert his cloak during the Khutbah. He will make the top bottom and the bottom on top. He will bring the right edge to his left shoulder and vice-versa. The people will not invert their cloaks. He will then face the Qiblah after the Khutbah and engage in du'a. The people will sit facing the Qiblah, making du'a, seeking forgiveness and repenting. It is appropriate that Istisqa be made with the presence of the weak ones, old men, old ladies and children.

quduri.f: Is there any other act besides what you have mentioned [i.e. see answer to question #319 regarding Salatul Istisqa]
quduri.b: Yes, they should give charity before going to the Salah.

quduri.f: Is there an extra Salah in the month of Ramadan besides the Fard and usual Sunan?
quduri.b: Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who keeps the fast of Ramadan with Iman and hoping for reward has his past sins forgiven. He who stands in worship in Ramadan with Iman and hoping for reward has his passed sins forgiven." [al-Bukhari and Muslim] It is obvious from the Hadith that there is a Salah in the nights of Ramadan, over and above that which is prayed in the other nights.

quduri.f: How is this Salah [i.e. Tarawih] prayed in the nights of Ramadan?
quduri.b: The Imam leads the people in 20 Rak'at after 'Isha. He will make Salah upon every two Rak'at with a total of 5 rests in between.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of 5 rests? [i.e. in Tarawih]
quduri.b: A rest [Tarwihah] after every 4 Rak'at. That is why it is called Salatul Tarawih. The Imam will rest with the people the duration of the 4 Rak'at.

quduri.f: Is this Salah [i.e. Tarawih] Sunnah for women as well?
quduri.b: Yes, it is Sunnah Muakkadah for men and women. The men will pray in congegration in the Masajid and for women their homes are best,

quduri.f: What is the status of congegration for men in Tarawih?
quduri.b: It is Sunnah Muakkadah with Kifayah [collective] status. If all the people of the Masjid abandon it they have sinned.

quduri.f: Is Witr prayed in congegration during Ramadan?
quduri.b: Yes, after the five rests, the Imam will lead them in Witr in congegration. He will read the Qira-ah aloud in all five Rak'at. He and the followers will read the Qunut softly.

quduri.f: Is Witr prayed in congegration out of Ramadan?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: How will the Imam lead the people when the enemy is attacking and there is much fear?
quduri.b: The Imam will divide the people in two groups. One group to confront the enemy, and the other to pray behind them. He will pray a complete Rak'ah with that group. When he raises his head from the second Sajdah, that group will go face the enemy. The next group will come and the Imam will lead them in a Rak'ah. He will make Tashshahud and Salam but they will not make Salam. Upon his Salam they will go to face the enemy while the first group will complete their second Rak'ah without Qira-ah. They will make Tashshahud and Salam. They will go back to the enemy. The second group will come, and pray their remaining Rak'ah with Qira-ah. They will make Tashshahud and Salam.

quduri.f: What will the Imam do if he is resident? [i.e. during Salatul Khawf (Congegration Prayer during fear)]
quduri.b: He will pray the four Rak'at Fard, two Rak'at with each group.

quduri.f: How will he pray Maghrib with them? [i.e. during Salatul Khawf if the Imam is a resident]
quduri.b: He will pray two Rak'at with the first group and one with the second.

quduri.f: If the fear is so intense that they cannot meet for congegration nor can they dismount? [i.e. for Salatul Khawf when facing the enemy]
quduri.b: They will pray individually on their mounts, doing Ruku' and Sujud by indication.

quduri.f: What if they are unable to face the Qiblah? [i.e. when the fear is so intense whilst facing the enemy and people have to pray individually]
quduri.b: They should pray wherever they can.

quduri.f: If some of them are dismounted on the ground, how should they pray? [i.e. whilst facing the enemy]
quduri.b:
They will pray without walking and must fulfil the Ruku' and Sujud. If they are unable to fulfil them then they should do so by indication.78

78 "The infantryman will indicate when he is unable to make Ruku' or Sujud. [al-Fatawa al-Hindiyah (156/1)]

quduri.f: If they were forced to start fighting while they were engaged in Salah, what is the status of the Salah?
quduri.b: If they fought or walked, it is void because of many actions.

quduri.f: What should they do if the enemy attacks and they are unable to perform Salah with Ruku' or Sujud, not even by indication, whether individually or following the Imam?
quduri.b:
They should delay the Salah as Rasulullaah ﷺ did at the Battle of Khandaq,79 and pray it when they can even if Qada.

79 Al-Bukhari narrates just before the Book of Azan that Jabir bin 'Adbillah رضي الله عنه narrates that 'Umar bin al-Khattab رضي الله عنه came after sunset and cursed the Kuffar of the Quraysh. He said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ, I was only able to pray 'Asr when the sun was about to set." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "By Allaah, I was unable to pray it." We then went to Bat-han. He made Wudu for Salah and we did likewise. He prayed 'Asr after sunset and then prayed Maghrib.

quduri.f: Allaah has made the Ka'bah the Qibla which the Muslim must face in Salah. Is Salah valid if prayed inside it?
quduri.b: Yes, both Fard and Nafl will be valid.

quduri.f: If the Imam prays in the Ka'bah and a follower's back faces the back of the Imam, is his Salah valid?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: And if a follower has his face to the face of the Imam? [i.e. when the Imam is inside the Ka'bah]
quduri.b: It is valid but Makruh.

quduri.f: And one whose back faces the Imam's face? [i.e. is his Salah valid whilst the Imam is inside the Ka'bah]
quduri.b: His Salah is not valid because he stood in front of the Imam.

quduri.f: When the Imam stands outside the Ka'bah in al-Masjid al-Haram and the people circle the Ka'bah and follow him, is their Salah valid?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Is that a general rule [i.e. when the Imam stands outside the Ka'bah in al-Masjid al-Haram and the people circle the Ka'bah and follow him] or are certain followers excluded?
quduri.b: The follower who is closer to the Ka'bah on the side that the Imam is facing is excluded. His following is incorrect for being ahead of the Imam. The Salah is valid of one who is closer to the Ka'bah than the Imam if he is at a side different to the Imam's.

quduri.f: Is Salah on the roof of the Ka'bah valid?
quduri.b: It is valid but Makruh for not showing honour to the Ka'bah.

quduri.f: What should those who are present by someone is dying do?
quduri.b: When someone is about to die, he should be laid to on his right side and face the Qiblah. He should be encouraged to recite the Shahadatayn. When he dies his jaws should be tied and his eyes closed. The laws of a woman are like that as well.

quduri.f: How is a corpse washed?
quduri.b:
The corpse should be laid on a platform perfumed an odd number of times80. A cloth should be placed over his private region and his clothing removed. Wudu is then made for him, excluding washing his mouth and nose. His head and beard is washed with Khitmi81. He will then be laid on his left side. He will be washed until it is seen that the water reaches the platform beneath him. [Then do the same with the corpse on the right side.] The washer will then make him sit and lean against him. He will gently wipe the stomach. If something comes out of the corpse he will wash it there. He will not repeat the full Ghusl. He will then let the corpse lie on its left side and wash it, pouring camphor water over it. That is the third and final wash.

80 The corpse shoud be laid on a platform perfumed an odd number of times, up to a maximum of seven times just like when he is put in coffin cloth and when he dies, i.e. on three occasions. [ad-Durr al-Mukthar].
Ash-Shami said, "That the perfume should be taken around the platform one, thrice, five times or seven times, nothing more. This is in al-Fath, al-Kafi and an-Nihayah. At-Tabyin sets the maximum at five. 'On three...' means that the corpse is perfumed on three occasions i.e. when the soul departs to remove the bad odour when he is washed; and when he is dressed..."(574/1)
81 A plant with a pleasant aroma.

quduri.f: Is anything besides water used for cleaning? [i.e. the deceased]
quduri.b: Yes, the water can be boiled with lotus or potash and used to wash the corpse. Soap is also allowed.

quduri.f: If these things are not available? (i.e. lotus, potash or soap for cleaning the deceased)
quduri.b: Then with plain water.

quduri.f: Explain the number of Kafan [shrouds] and method of shrouding for men and women.
quduri.b:
There are details in this matter as follows:
The Sunnah kafan of a man is Izar [lower cloth]; Qamis ["shirt"] and lifafah [covering]. The minimum is Izar and lifafah. Under necessity, whatever can be found. To use only one cloth without an excuse is Makruh.
The izar is from head to feet. The lifafah is the same. The Qamis is from below the neck to the feet without pockets, attachments or sleeves.
The shrouds are perfumed in odd numbers. The lifafah is laid out, then the izar over it. After drying the corpse so that it does not wet the shrouds, it is placed on the izar. Hanut perfume is applied to his head and beard. Camphor is applied to his places of Sajdah i.e. forehead, nose, palms, knees and feet. He is first dressed in the Qamis82. Then the izar is folded over the corpse from his left side then from his right hand side. The same is then done with the lifafah. The right folds must be over the left folds.
If it is feared that the shrouds will open, the sides may be tied with something.
The Sunnah kafan of a woman is a Dir' ["armour"], izar, khimar ["headscarf"], lifafah and khirqah ["cloth"]. The khirqah is used to tie her breasts and Dir' refers to Qamis. The minimum kafan is izar, lifafah and khimar. Under necessity, whatever can be found. To use two cloths without an excuse is Makruh.

The khirqah should reach from the breasts to the thighs.
The khimar should be 3 arm spans long.
The shrouds are perfumed in odd numbers. The lifafah is laid out, then the izar over it. The corpse is placed on the izar. The dir' is put on. Her hair is made into two plaits and are placed over the dir' on her breasts. The khimar is then put over that.83 The khirqah is then tied84 above the Qamis. The Izar is then folded then the lifafah. The sides of the shroud can be tied if it is feared that it will open.
82 Spread half the Qamis on the izar and fold the other half, leaving the head side free. When the corpse is put on the izar enter his head into the cut out part of the Qamis. Then spread out the top half over the corpse.

83 The khimar is put over her head and plaits from two sides is placed over her chest above the Dir'.

84 According to some Fuqaha the khirqah is tied after the other shrouds. We prefer what is in al-Ikthiyar because it is supported by Ahadith.

quduri.f: Is there corpse's hair combed?
quduri.b: Neither the hair nor beard is combed; nor the nails clipped; nor the hair cut.

quduri.f: Describe the Salah for the dead.
quduri.b:
The imam will stand in line with the corpse's chest. The people will stand behind him and try to form three rows.85 The Imam and the followers will proclaim Takbir and recite Thana and Allaah's praises. If they wish they may recite "SubhanakAllaahumma ..." until the end. After a second Takbir, Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ is recited. After a third Takbir du'a is made for the deceased and the Muslim, living and dead. After a fourth Takbir, Salam is made.86

85 Malik bin Hubayrah رضي الله عنه narrates: I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "There is no Muslim who dies and three rows of Muslims pray upon him except that [Jannah] becomes compulsory." Because of this Hadtih Malik would form the people into three rows when they were few at a funeral. [Abu Dawud]
86 Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah رضي الله عنه narrates from Hafs bin Ghiyath who narrates from Ash'ath who narrates from ash-Shu'va that after the first Takbir Hamd and Thana is recited, Salat 'alan Nabi ﷺ after the second, du'a after the third and Salam after the fourth.
In India and Pakistan the du'a narrated by at-Tirmizi is most frequently recited, "Allamaghir lihayyina wa mayyitina .."

quduri.f: What du'a is read for a child's funeral?
quduri.b: Allaahummaj 'alhu lana farataw wa ajra

quduri.f: Will they raise their hands for the Takbir of Janazah Salah?
quduri.b: No, only for the first Takbir.

quduri.f: Is Jam'ah a conidtion for praying this Salah? [i.e. Salatul Janazah]
quduri.b: No. Even if a single woman or man prays it, the Fard Kifayah is fulfilled.

quduri.f: What are the conditions and Fard of the Salah [Janazah]?
quduri.b:
Conditions include being free of al-Hadath al-Akbar and al-Asghar. The clothing and place must be clean. The deceased must have been purified and placed before the Musallis. There are two Fard:
Qiyam
and four Takbir
Everything besides that is Sunnah.

quduri.f: Can the Funeral Prayer be held in a Masjid built for five time's Salah?
quduri.b:
It is Makruh. The Nabi ﷺ would pray it outside of the Masjid where the deceased would be placed.87

87 Al-Bukhari narrates from Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه that Rasulullaah ﷺ announced the death of the Negus on the day that he died. He went with the Muslims to the Musalla, formed them into rows and recited four Takbir upon him.
'Abdullaah bin 'Umar  رضي الله عنه narrates that the Jews brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ a man and woman from them who had committed Zina. He ordered their execution. They were stoned near the place Funeral Prayers were held at the Masjid.
The first Hadith clarifies that he went out to the Musalla to pray, even though the corpse was not present. The second Hadith states that Funerals were at the Masjid.
Muhammad bin 'Abdullah bin Jahsh رضي الله عنه narrates, "We were sitting in the courtyard of the Masjid where Funerals were held. Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting amongst us ..." This Hadith of Ahmad clarifies that the place of Funerals was the courtyard of the Masjid.
Ibnul Humam states in Fathul Qadir, "And then there is the narration in Muslim that when Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas رضي الله عنه died, 'Aisha رضي الله عنها said, 'Bring him into the Masjid so that I may pray upon him.' They refused her and she said, 'By Allaah, the Nabi ﷺ prayed over the two sons of Bayda in the Masjid - Sahl and his brother.

quduri.f: Who is most entitled to lead the Salah?
quduri.b: The most entitled is the Muslim ruler if he is present, if not then the Imam of the district, if not then the guardian.

quduri.f: If someone besides the ruler or the Imam prayed it [i.e. Salatul Janazah], is the guardian allowed to repeat the Salah?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: If the guardian has prayed the Salah [Janazah], may anyone else repeat it?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the deceased was buried without Salatul Janazah?
quduri.b: It may be prayed at his grave for up to three days, and not thereafter.

quduri.f: How should the men carry the corpse and how should they walk?
quduri.b: They should take the four legs of the bier. They should walk with speed without shaking. One who wishes to carry the bier in such a way that the corpse's right shoulder will be on his right shoulder, then move back so that the right back portion is on his right shoulder, then the front left shoulder on his left shoulder then move back so that the back left portion is on his left shoulder.

quduri.f: Can the people sit in the graveyard?
quduri.b: Yes, although it is Makruh to sit before lifting the bier from the men's necks.

quduri.f: How should the grave be?
quduri.b: The grave should be dug to half a man's height or till the chest. If dug deeper then it is good. It is preferred then that the Lahd type then be dug. If the earth is soft they choose the Shiqq method then it too is allowed.

quduri.f: How is the corpse entered into grave?
quduri.b:
From the Qiblah side. The one who places it in the grave will recite, "Bismillah wa billah wa 'ala millati Rasulillah ﷺ.88 He will make it face the Qiblah, lying on its right side. The knots tied to prevent the shroud from opening will be untied. The Lahd will be closed with level unbaked bricks and then covered with soil.

88 At-Tirmizi narrates from Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنه that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to recite that when he entered the corpse into the grave. The narrator also said, "Bismillah wa billah wa 'ala sunnati Rasulillah."

quduri.f: If baked bricks, wood or reed is used to level and close the Lahd?
quduri.b: Baked bricks and wood is Makruh, reed is no problem.

quduri.f: How should the grave be completed after the sand was placed on it?
quduri.b: The grave should be like a camel's hump, not level. It should not be higher than a hand span.

quduri.f: What is the ruling on making the grave firm with lime or cement?
quduri.b: These are sins which Rasulullaah ﷺ forbade.

quduri.f: Is Salah read on a baby who was born, cried and died?
quduri.b: A baby which cried after birth or showed any sign of life is named, washed and his funeral held.

quduri.f: If he neither cried nor showed any sign of life?
quduri.b: He will be wrapped in a khirqah and buried without Salah.

quduri.f: Is there a difference in the laws of a martyr?
quduri.b: Yes, some laws differ.

quduri.f: Describe those laws [i.e. those which differ for a martyr]
quduri.b: A Muslim has been slain by Kuffar; or is found in the battlefield with wounds from which he died; or has been oppressively killed by other Muslims in a situation where Diya [bloodmoney] is not Wajib; then he will be shrouded and prayed upon without Ghusl.

quduri.f: If the martyr died while Junub will he be given Ghusl or not?
quduri.b: Al-Imam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى said that he will be washed and his two companions said that he will not be washed. They disagree in the same way about a child martyr. Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى said that he will be washed and they said that he will not be washed.

quduri.f: We know that a martyr is not washed like other dead, but is his blood washed and his clothing removed?
quduri.b: The blood is not washed and his clothing is not removed except for his fur, outer garments, leather socks and weapons are removed.

quduri.f: Someone has been wounded in the battlefield. He then eats, drinks or is treated. He then dies. Is he regarded as a martyr?
quduri.b: If Allaah wills he will receive a martyr's reward and is a martyr in the Sight of Allaah. As for the laws amongst humans, he is not regarded as a martyr who is not washed. The eating, drinking and medication is termed as irtithath.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of one who is wounded on the battlefield and remains alive and the Waqt of Salah passes while he retains his senses; or he is carried alive from the battlefield?
quduri.b: This is also irtithath. He will be washed like a normal deceased.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of one killed in hadd [prescribed Islamic punishment] or Qisas [retaliation]?
quduri.b: He will receive Ghusl and Salah.

quduri.f: Is Salah performed upon rebels and highway robbers?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of Zakah linguistically and Islaamically?
quduri.b: Linguistically Zakah is purification and increase. In Shari'ah it is the decree of Allaah the Lawgiver, that the owner of a set amount makes a poor Muslim owner of a set portion of his wealth for the sake of Allaah, in a way that the first owner terminates his benefits of ownership in all aspects.

quduri.f: What is the status of Zakah in Islaam?
quduri.b:
It is a Fard amongst that which Allaah has made Fard. It is a Pillar of Islaam.91 Allaah has commanded it in His book, "And establish Salah and give Zakah." He who denies it being Fard is a Kafir and has left the pale of Islaam.

91 Must Fuqaha list Zakah before Fasting in following the sequence in the Quran and because it is the most virtuous act of worship after Salah. Allaah has linked Zakah with Salah 32 times in His Honourable Book. [Raddul Muhtar]

quduri.f: Upon whom is Zakah Fard?
quduri.b: It is Fard upon a free, mature, intelligent Muslim who owns the complete requisite amount in complete ownership upon which a year has passed.

quduri.f: What is the complete requisite amount [Nisab]?
quduri.b: It is to own 200 Dirham of silver; or 20 Mithqal of gold; or the equivalent of either amount in the prevalent currency; or a trader owning trade goods to the value of either amount.

quduri.f: A man has the requisite amount but in indebted. Is Zakah Fard upon him?
quduri.b: Substract the debt from his wealth. If the remainder equals or exceeds the Nisab then Zakah is payable on the remainded.

quduri.f: Is there Zakah on trade goods?
quduri.b: Yes, if it is worth either 200 Dirham or 20 Mithqal of gold.

quduri.f: What do you mean, "if a year passes"?
quduri.b:
If a free mature Muslim owns the Nisab or more, then he has to pay Zakah on it if he has owned it for a complete lunar year. The Solar year is not reckonded.92

92 Every year on the date the Zakah first became Wajib.

quduri.f: What do you say about residential buildings, the clothes worn on the body and furniture in the house?
quduri.b: There is no Zakah on these as well as one's transport, slaves used for service and weapons which are used.

quduri.f: If these items are for trading then is there Zakah? [i.e. for residential buildings, clothes worn on the body and furniture of the house, as well as one's transport, slaves and weapons]
quduri.b: Yes, if they reach the Nisab.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to give the price in Zakah if the Zakah was payable on gold, silver or goods?
quduri.b: Yes, giving the value of Zakah is allowed.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of someone who gave all his wealth in charity but did not intend Zakah?
quduri.b: The duty of Zakah has been lifted from him.

quduri.f: What should someone do if his wealth has been destroyed after Zakah has become Wajib?
quduri.b: If all his wealth has been destroyed then the duty of paying Zakah has also been lifted from him. If part of his wealth has been destroyed, then that proportion falls alway. That is if it was destroyed by others. If he himself destroyed it then Zakah does not fall away.

quduri.f: Upon what amount of silver is Zakah Fard?
quduri.b: When one owns 200 Dirham of silver and a year has passed in possession of it, then Zakah must be paid. He will pay a fortieth of his wealth, which amounts to 5 Dirham out of every 200.

quduri.f: If he owns more than 200 Dirham, how does he pay the extra amount?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى there is no extra Zakah until the extra amount reaches 40 Dirham. He will then pay another Dirham on the 40 in addition to the 5 and then again another Dirham for each additional 40 Dirham he might own. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he will pay in proportion to whatever exceeds 200, however little or much it may be.

quduri.f: Upon what amount of gold is Zakah Fard?
quduri.b:
When one owns 200 Mithqal93 of gold and a year has passed in possession of it, then Zakah must be paid. He will pay a fortieth of his wealth, which amounts to a half Mithqal. Thereafter for every 4 Mithqal he will pay 2 Qirat. There is no Zakah upon the extra amount less than 4 Mithqal according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. His two companions say that a half Mithqal is due on 20 Mithqal and anything above 20 is calculated proportionally.

93 Ad-Durr al-Muktar: "Nisab of gold is 20 Mithqal and silver 200 Dirham. 10 Dirham weights 7 Mithqal or Dinar. A dinar equals 20 Qirat. A dirham equals 14 Qirat. A Qirat is 5 barley. The Shar'i Dirham is thus 70 barley, and a Mithqal is 100 barley or 1 and three-sevenths of a Dirham."
As for the new weights, the people of accounting differ. Some say that 20 Mithqal equals 85 grams, others 87g, others 90g. Caution is desirous in the Shari'ah, hence one who owns 85g of gold or its value for a year should pay Zakah. There is a difference on silver as well. Some say 595.1g; or 609.2g; or 612.3g. Caution calls for that here too the least amount be declared the Nisab. So one who owns 595g of silver or lots value in the prevalent currency should pay Zakah on it.

quduri.f: Is there Zakah upon gold and silver ornaments or vessels?
quduri.b: All gold and silver are Zakatable, whether in nugger form, ornament or vessel and whether it is used or not.

quduri.f: What is the ruling on gold or silver which is debased with other metal?
quduri.b: If the overwhelming composition is silver then it is regarded as silver. If the overwhelming proportion is alloy then it is treated as an alloy. The same applies to gold.

quduri.f: A man neither has gold nor silver, but government recognised bank notes. Is there Zakah payable?
quduri.b: Yes, if the notes reach the value of either Nisab of gold or silver. It is like goods of value. Everything is bought with it and it is used in trade. The government is obliged to imburse one who brings these notes to the bank.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Zakah on trade goods?
quduri.b: Zakah is Wajib on trade goods if the value reaches the Nisab of gold or silver. They will be valued to reach the value of either amount so as to benefit the poor. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى they will be valued with whatever is used to buy them. If they are bought with gold, they will be valued with gold. If they are bought with silver, they will be valued with silver. If they are bought with neither gold nor silver they will be valued according to the prevalent city. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى they will be valued according to the prevalent currency in all conditions.

quduri.f: How is Zakah of wealth paid?
quduri.b: The proportion Allaah has decreed, i.e. one-fortieth must be given to those whom it is permissible to be given to with a simultaneous intention to fulfill the Zakah when paying it or a simultaneous intention when setting aside the obligated amount.

quduri.f: What is meant by, "simultaneous when setting aside the obligated amount?"
quduri.b: When he calculates his wealth at the end of the year, he takes out the amount to be paid in Zakah and makes an intention that every time he finds someone entitled he will spend from it on him. Ever time a poor person comes and he gives him from that separated wealth the Zakah is being fulfilled even if he does not bear in mind the intention of Zakah at the time of payment.

quduri.f: A man with Nisab gets additional wealth during the year. Is Zakah payable on it?
quduri.b: He will add the additional wealth to the same type he owns and calculate the Zakah.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to pay Zakah before the end of his Zakah year?
quduri.b: Yes, the Zakah has been rendered.

quduri.f: A man possessing Nisab paid his Zakah at the end of the year. During the following year his wealth falls below Nisab. Does he pay Zakah?
quduri.b: If he again has Nisab by the end of the second year, Zakah is Wajib upon him. Nisab only need be considered at the ends of the years. The drop during the year is of no relevant.

quduri.f: A man has trade goods worth less than Nisab. He however also has gold and silver. Does he pay Zakah?
quduri.b: If the total value of the gold, silver and goods reaches Nisab then Zakah is payable.

quduri.f: A man has less than 20 Mithqal of gold and less than 200 Dirham of silver. Does he pay Zakah?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى he will add the value of the two, and if the Nisab is reached Zakah is payable. According to his two companions they will not be added according to value, but according to proportion.

quduri.f: Please give an example of the above difference of opinion. [i.e. when a man has less than 20 Mithqal of gold and less than 200 Dirham of silver]
quduri.b:
A man has 100 Dirham of silver and 5 Mithqal of gold worth 100 Dirham. Zakah is Wajib according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى but not the other two. The Nisab has been attained according to him by way of value. It has not been attained according to them by way of proportion. On the other hand if the man had 100 Dirham and Mithqal worth 100 Dirham, Zakah is payable according to all of them. The Nisab has been reached according to both methods.95

95 The 100 Dirham is half Nisab and the 10 Mithqal is half Nisab. If the proportions are added then full Nisab is attained.

quduri.f: Is Zakah payable on anything else besides gold, silver and trade goods?
quduri.b: Yes, on Sawaim.

quduri.f: What are Sawaim?
quduri.b: Animals which graze in the fields like camels, goats and cattle. Zakah is only Wajib on them if they suffice on grazing for most of the year. If they have to be fed fodder for at least half the year, then Zakah is not payable.

quduri.f: What is Wajib in these categories? [i.e. related on Sawaim]
quduri.b: Each category has a different amount payable and different Nisab.

quduri.f: Is their Zakah on animals used for labour, carrying or are fed fodder at home?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Explain the amount of Zakah paid on camels.
quduri.b:
There is no Zakah on less than 5 camels. If there are 5 to 9 which have grazed freely and a year has passed on them then a sheep is payable. Two sheep are payable on 10 - 1 4 camels. 3 sheep are payable on 15 - 19 camels. 4 sheep are payable on 20 - 24 camels. A camel in its second year is payable on 25 - 35 camels. A camel in its third year is payable on 36 - 45 camels. A camel in its fourth year is payable on 46 - 60 camels. A camel in its fifth year is payable on 61 - 75 camels. 2 camels in their third year is payable on 76 - 90 camels. 2 camels in their fourth year is payable on 91 - 120 camels.

The sequence then begins anew. At the next 5 camels a sheep and 2 camels in their fourth year is payable. At 10, 2 sheep with the camels. At 15, 3 sheep with the camels. At 20, 4 sheep with the camels. At 25, a camel in its second year with the camels. This sequence continues until a total of 150 camels are owned. Upon that, 3 camels in their fourth year are paid.

The sequence then begins anew. At the next 5 camels a sheep and 3 camels in their fourth year is payable. At 10, 2 sheep with the camels. At 15, 3 sheep with the camels. At 20, 4 sheep with the camels. At 25, a camel in its second year with the camels. At 36, a camel in its third year with the camels. This sequence continues until a total of 196 camels are owned. Upon that and until 200, 4 camels in their fourth year are paid.

The sequence begins anew as per the calculations of 50 until after 150.

quduri.f: Is any distinction in the amounts made between Arabian camels and cross-breeds?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Explain the amount of Zakah payable on cattle.
quduri.b:
There is no Zakah on less than 30 heads of cattle. If the number reaches 30 cattle which spent most of a year freely grazing and they have been possessed for a full lunar year then Zakah of a calf - male or female - in its second year is payable. For 40 cattle a calf of either sex in its third year is payable. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى an additional calculation is made for an amount above 40 until 60. A fortieth of a third year female calf is due on one above 40; two-fortieths on 2; 3 fortieths on 3. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى there is no extra Zakah on the extra amount above 40 until 60. When the cattle reach 60 heads96 then 2 calves in their second year of either sex are due. On 70 a calf in the third year and a calf in the second year are due. On 80, 2 calves in their third year are due. On 90, 3 second year calves are due. On 100, 2 second years and 1 third year. In this way, in every 10 the Zakah will change between second and third years.

96 There is no difference amongst them on less than 40 and 60 and above.

quduri.f: How is Zakah on buffaloes calculated?
quduri.b: There is no difference between calculation on cattle and buffaloes.

quduri.f: Explain the Zakah payable on goats.
quduri.b: There is no Zakah on less than 40 sheep. If one owns 40 sheep which have freely grazed for most of a year and have owned them for a year, then on 40 - 120 sheep, 1 is due in Zakah. 2 Sheep are due on 121 - 200 sheep. 3 sheep are due on 201 and then 4 sheep are due on 400. Then 1 sheep for every 100.

quduri.f: Is there a difference between the Zakah of sheep and goats?
quduri.b:
No.98

98 Ash-Shami stated, "if he has sheep below the Nisab and also has goats that if they are added together then the Nisab is reached, the Zakah becomes Wajib. The Nisab will be taken from the respective animal and if it was reached by combing the two then Zakah is taken from whichever is most. If they are equal then from whichever he wants to.

quduri.f: Is Zakah payable on horses?
quduri.b:
If one owns Sawaim horses (whether male or female) for a year then one has a choice - either pay a Dinar for each horse or value them and pay 5 Dirham in every 200 of the value. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى if only stallions are owned then Zakah is not due.99

99 Al-Hidayah: because they do not reproduce. Similarly if there are only mares owned.

quduri.f: Is there a difference regarding Zakah on horses?
quduri.b: Yes, Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى disagree with Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and say that there is no Zakah on horses.

quduri.f: Is Zakah payable on mules and donkeys?
quduri.b: Only if they are for trade in which case the Zakah payable on trade goods must take them into account.

quduri.f: What does Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى say about the offspring of camels and cattle?
quduri.b: There is no Zakah on the babies of camels, sheep and goats according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى unless they are with adults. It is Wajib according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى. [There are further details to his view which can be read in al-Hidayah].

quduri.f: What does the Zakaat-collector do if he does not find in the herd what must be taken?
quduri.b: He will take a lesser animal and more to equal the amount due, or he will take a higher animal and pay the difference back.

quduri.f: Should the collector take the best wealth or the worst?
quduri.b: He should take something in between.

quduri.f: If the Nisab remains but the non-Zakatable excess has been destroyed, is Zakah calculated on the entire remainder or is it decreased in proportion to the destroyed wealth?
quduri.b: The principle according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى is that Zakah is Wajib on the Nisab not the excess. Hence the Wajib is intact according to them. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Zufar رحمه الله تعالى the Wajib decreases in proportion to the loss.

quduri.f: I do not understand. Please explain by way of an example. [i.e. with regards to question 419: if the nisab remains but the non-zakatable excess has been destroyed]
quduri.b:
Ponder over this example carefully. A man has 9 camels over which a complete year has passed. 4 then were destroyed. He must pay a complete sheep, just as if there had been no excess over 5. The destroyed 4 are overlooked as normal excess in which Zakah is not paid until the camels reach 10. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى.

According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Zufar رحمه الله تعالى he has to pay 5-ninths of a sheep. They have spread the Wajib across the 9 camels and proportionately decreased the loss over the nine.

A second example: A man has 80 goats of which 40 were destroyed after the year. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى a sheep is due on the remainder. According to the others, a half sheep.

If 60 were destroyed then a half is due according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and a quarter according to the others. [See Fathul-Qadir, al-'Inayah and al-Jawharah an-Nayyirah]

quduri.f: Is Zakah payable on fruits and crops?
quduri.b: Yes, one-tenth or one-twentieth is paid according to the water used.

quduri.f: Is there a Nisab in that? [i.e. regarding fruits and crops]
quduri.b: Not according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. Zakah is on whatever comes from the earth, whether little or many, except wood, reeds and grass which does not have Zakah according to him. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى there is no Zakah unless something has remaining fruits and it reaches 5 Wasq. There is no Zakah on vegetables according to them.

quduri.f: What is a Wasq?
quduri.b: A measurement of the people of al-Madinah equal to 60 Sa'.

quduri.f: What are the details of the payment of a tenth and half of that?
quduri.b: A tenth is due on plants naturally water e.g. rain. A twentieth is due from plants watered by artificial irrigation such as water-wheels and water-scoops, according to one of the two views.

quduri.f: What do Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى say about crops which are not measured with Wasq such as saffron and cotton?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى if the crop is valued at 5 Wasq of the lowest value crop measured in Wasq then a tenth is due. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى a tenth is due when the crop reaches 5 of its biggest measurements e.g. 5 bales of cotton and 5 Amna [a measurement] of saffron.

quduri.f: Is Zakah paid on honey?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى, yyes, whether a little or a lot. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى there is no Zakah until it reaches 10 bags, according to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى 5 Farq.

quduri.f: How much is a Farq?
quduri.b: 36 'Iraqi Ritl.

quduri.f: Is 'Ushr paid on land on which Khiraj is paid?
quduri.b: The Khiraj suffices.

quduri.f: Are expenses like workers' wages, expenses on cattle etc. deductible from the tenth or twentieth.
quduri.b: No the Zakah is paid from the entire amount, be it a tenth or twentieth.

quduri.f: Upon whom can Zakah be spent?
quduri.b:
Allaah has explained it in His Honoured Book, "Verily Sadaqah is for the Fuqara, Masakin, the workers on it, whose hearts are to be united, slaves, debtors, in the way of Allaah and travellers." There are thus 8 categories:
Fuqara
masakin
workers on it
whose hearts are to be united
slaves
debtors
in Allaah's way
travellers

quduri.f: Who is a Faqir?
quduri.b: He who has minimal possessions which does not reach Nisab.

quduri.f: Who is a Miskin?
quduri.b: He who does not have anything.

quduri.f: What is meant by, "workers on it"?
quduri.b: Those whom the ruler sends to collect the Zakah from the Muslims. They go to them and collect, spending their time in that. The ruler will pay them from the Zakah according to their labour.

quduri.f: What is the meaning os alves?
quduri.b:
To help a Mukatab100 free himself.

100 A slave who has a contract with his owner that if he pays the owner a certain amount he will be set free.

quduri.f: Who is a debtor?
quduri.b: One who is indebted that he is unable to repay it from his wealth.

quduri.f: What is meant by, "in the way of Allaah"?
quduri.b: Those who have gone to Jihad and have been separated from their groups and are in need of money for expenses.

quduri.f: Who is a traveller?
quduri.b: A traveller who does not have money on his journey even if he has money at home.

quduri.f: Define whose hearts are to be united.
quduri.b:
They are those whom Rasulullaah ﷺ gave from the wealth of Zakah to, to soften their hearts to enter Islaam. They were leaders of tribes. It was hoped that through them becoming Muslim, their people would accept Islaam. When Islaam gained victory and became independent of them the ruling of giving to them was dropped. They are not given wealth after the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ.101

101 Ibnul Humam said, "They were of three types - Kuffar whom Rasulullaah ﷺ gave to soften their hearts to enter Islaam; some whom he gave to in order to avert their evil; and some who had embraced Islaam but were weak and needed strengthening."

quduri.f: That leaves 7 categories [i.e. besides "whose hearts are to be united"]. Must one paying Zakah give each category or will some suffice?
quduri.b: He can pay a single person of a single category, or may spread it amongst more.

quduri.f: Can Zakah be paid to a Kafir who is Faqir or Miskin?
quduri.b: No, even if he is under Muslim rule.

quduri.f: Can Zakah funds be used for shrouding or building a Masjid, Madrasah, bridge or public road?
quduri.b: No, and if done the Zakah must be paid again. The principle in Zakah is that one entitled must take ownership of it. There is no taking possession in the examples given.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the Zakah was given to one in charge of the Madrasah?
quduri.b: It is allowed if he made the supervisor his representative to spend it on the Faqir and Miskin students, on condition that the supervisor makes them the owners. The Zakah is not fulfilled by simply making the food permissible for them; nor by constructing buildings of the Madrasah; nor by using it for the salaries of the teachers or other employees of the Madrasah.

quduri.f: Is Zakah fulfilled if used to buy a slave and then freeing him?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Is it allowed to pay one's Zakah to one's poor relatives?
quduri.b:
There are two kinds of relatives. One kind is by birth e.g. parents, grandparents, children and grandchildren. The other is nor by birth e.g. brothers, sisters, paternal uncles and aunts, maternal uncles and aunts, and their descendants. Zakah cannot be paid to the first category. The Zakah is not fulfilled if given to any parent or grandparent or descendant of either sex.
Zakah can be given to the second category for which there is two rewards - the reward of Zakah and the reward of maintaining family ties.

quduri.f: How should it be given? Must you say, "This is Zakah?"
quduri.b: There is no need to expose that. One may give it in the guise of a gift as long as one intended it as Zakah, the Zakah is fulfilled. The recipient must also be of the categories we explained who are entitled to take Zakah and may not be of Banu Hashim.

quduri.f: Is Zakah fulfilled when given to one's husband/wife?
quduri.b: It is not fulfilled according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى, according to his two companions it is fulfilled if a woman gives it to her husband.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of giving Zakah to a rich man or his son?
quduri.b:
It is not permissible to give Zakah of any kind of wealth to a rich man i.e. the one who has Nisab102 free of his principle needs. It cannot be given to his son who is small and has not reached puberty. It can be given to a rich man's adult son if he is poor, not possessing Nisab.

102 Fathul Qadir (202/2): "In summary Nisab is of three kinds. One is which makes Zakah Wajib upon its owner. It increases naturally or by adding, and he is free of debt. Another Nisab is that which does not necessitate Zakah and that is when it is encompassed by the needs of the owner who can then accept Zakah. If not in his need, then Zakah is Haram for him e.g. his clothing equals Nisab and he does not need them all nor he does not need to use all his furniture in his house; or a slave whose service he does not need; or a horse he does not ride; or a house he does not need to live in. If he is really in need of any of these then he is a Faqir and one can give him Zakah. However, begging is not allowed for him. The third Nisab is that which prohibits beginning. It is when he owns enough food for the day or does not own it but is capable of earning it or owns 50 Dirham (with different views on this amount)."

quduri.f: Is there such a Faqir or Miskin to whom Zakah cannot be given?
quduri.b: Yes, Zakah cannot be given to Banu Hashim, even if they are poor. They are the descendants of 'Ali رضي الله عنه, Al-'Abbas رضي الله عنه, Ja'far رضي الله عنه, 'Aqil رضي الله عنه and Harith bin 'Abdil Muttalib رضي الله عنه.

quduri.f: If these people [i.e. Banu Hashim] are in need, how can they be helped?
quduri.b: Donate to them without intention of Zakah or any other compulsory charity.

quduri.f: A man paid his Zakah to someone whom he thought is entitled. It then became known that he was rich or a Hashimi or a Kafir; or he gave it to a poor man in the dark who turned out to be his father. Has his Zakah been fulfilled?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it has been fulfilled. Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى says that he should pay it again in all these scenarios.

quduri.f: What do out three Imams say about someone who paid Zakah to someone he thought was entitled and then leart that he is his Mukatab or slave?
quduri.b: They all say that his Zakah has not been fulfilled.

quduri.f: Can Zakah be paid to a healthy man who earns but does not own Nisab?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Is it permissible for somone to send his Zakah to a land where he does not live?
quduri.b: In principle, each people should spend their Zakah amongst themselves and not send it to another land. It is Makruh to do that unless it is sent to relatives or to a people in greater need than his own people.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Sadaqatul Fitr?
quduri.b:
It is Wajib upon a free Muslim if he owns Nisab of any form of wealth, in excess of his residence, clothing, furniture, transport and weapons.103

103 It applies to a well-off person who is forbidden to take Zakah.

quduri.f: On whose behalf does one have to pay?
quduri.b: Himself, his small children and his slave who serves him, even if the slave is a Kafir.

quduri.f: Does he pay for his small children from his own wealth or theirs?
quduri.b: If they have wealth then from theirs, otherwise from his own.

quduri.f: Is a man obligated to pay on behalf of his wife and adult children?
quduri.b: No, even if they are of his household, just as he is not obligated to pay for his slaves whom he buys and sells.

quduri.f: Who should pay for a slave owned by partners?
quduri.b: It is not Wajib on any of them.

quduri.f: When does Sadaqatul Fitr become Wajib?
quduri.b: It is Wajib at true dawn of 'Idul Fitr. Someone who dies before that need not have it paid on his behalf. Similarly one who is born or accepts Islaam after that is not obligated nor is it Wajib on his behalf.

quduri.f: Is there a recommended time? [i.e. for Sadaqatul Fitr]
quduri.b: On 'Idul Fitr before going to the Musalla.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of paying it [i.e. Sadaqatul Fitr] before 'Idul Fitr?
quduri.b: It is allowed.

quduri.f: If he delays it [i.e. Sadaqatul Fitr] after 'Idul Fitr?
quduri.b: It is not forfeited. He must still pay it.

quduri.f: Who are entitled to receive Sadaqatul Fitr?
quduri.b:
The Faqir and Miskin who do not own any form of wealth.104

104 An indication that the well-off person who cannot receive Zakah, also cannot take Sadaqatul Fitr. Those others mentioned who cannot be given Zakah also cannot be given Sadaqatul Fitr.

quduri.f: What is the benefit of paying Sadaqatul Fitr?
quduri.b: Abu Dawud narrates that 'Abdullaah bin 'Abbas رضي الله عنه said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ made Sadaqatul Fitr compulsory as a purification of the fast from any wasted time or obscenities and as a means of feeding the poor."

quduri.f: How much is Sadaqatul Fitr?
quduri.b: A half Sa' of wheat, or a full Sa' of dates, raisins or barley.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he paid [i.e. Sadaqatul Fitr] with something else, such as Dirhams, money, rice or corn?
quduri.b: It is fulfilled if he paid with something of equal value to one of the above nad intended it as Sadaqatul Fitr.

quduri.f: How much is a Sa'?
quduri.b:
It is 8 'Iraqi Ritl according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is 5 and a third Ritl.105 

105 Sharhul Wiqayah: "A Sa' equals 8 Ritl of Majj or lentils because these two seeds are the most uniform unlike other seeds which differ greatly in size and other qualities... Know that this Sa' is the 'Iraqi one not the Hijazi which is 5 and a third Ritl..."

quduri.f: What is the ruling on fasting in Islaam?
quduri.b:
The fast of the month of Ramadan is Fard upon every mature Muslim, male and female. Allaah says, "O you who believe! Fasting has been prescribed upon you just as it was prescribed upon those before you that you may acquire Taqwa." [al-Baqarah:183]
The fasts besides the fast of Ramadan are voluntary and one gets rewarded for them just as in other voluntary worship. Howver, if one has made nazr [vow] of a fast then it becomes Wajib to fulfil it.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of Sawm linguistically and in Shari'ah? What are the beginning and ending times?
quduri.b: Sawm means abstention linguistically. In Shari'ah it means to abstain from food, drink and sex from true dawn until sunset with the intention of fasting.

quduri.f: Is there any leeway for anyone not to fast during Ramadan?
quduri.b: Yes, someone who is a traveller of Qasr distance; or is sick and fears that the fast will worsen the sickness, then they are allowed not to fast during Ramadan. They must filfil the missed days thereafter. It is however better for the traveller to fast if he will not experience difficulty by it.

quduri.f: A traveller did not fast during his travel, or a sick person did not fast during his sickness. Then they die in that state of travel or sickness. Is anything Wajib upon them?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: If the sick person is cured or the traveller becomes resident, is Qada necessary?
quduri.b: Yes, upon the sick person in the days he is well and upon the traveller in the days he stays resident, whether homeland or temporary.

quduri.f: Is there anyone else besides a traveller and a sick person who are allowed not to fast in Ramadan?
quduri.b: A pregnant woman or a woman feeding milk to a baby who fears destruction of herself or her baby is allowed not to fast in Ramadan. The missed days must be kept afterwards.

quduri.f: Is there anyone who compulsorily does not fast in Ramadan?
quduri.b: Yes, it is Wajib on a woman in her menses or childbirth period not to fast. They are not allowed to fast, their state negates fasting.

quduri.f: Will they [i.e. a woman in her menses or childbirth period] fulfil their missed fasts after Ramadan?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Are there people upon whom missed Salah is not Qada, but Fidyah [compensation] is Wajib upon them?
quduri.b: Shaykh Fani.

quduri.f: What is meant by Shaykh Fani?
quduri.b: Someone so old that he will neither be able to fast during Ramadan nor after it right until the end of his life.

quduri.f: What is Fidyah?
quduri.b: To feed everyday a Miskin just as one feeds them in Kaffarat.

quduri.f: What is done when someone did not fast due to travel or illness and then had days to make Qada but did not do so and then his death approaches?
quduri.b: He should seek forgiveness and turn unto Allaah. He must also leave a bequest to his executor, instructing him to feed on his behalf a Miskim from his wealth a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of dates or barley.

quduri.f: If a child attains puberty or a Kafir embraces Islaam in the day of Ramadan, what should they do?
quduri.b: They should abstain for the rest of the day from that which terminates fast and should fast the remainder of Ramadan.

quduri.f: Do they [i.e. a child who attains puberty or a Kafir who embraces Islaam in the day of Ramadan] keep Qada for the partial day they reached?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of someone who was unconscious during Ramadan?
quduri.b: If someone fell unconscious during a day of Ramadan after having made intention of fast, need not keep Qada of that day. He will keep Qada of any subsequent days.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of an insane person who regains his sanity during the day of Ramadan?
quduri.b: He will make Qada of the passed days and fast the remaining days.

quduri.f: If a traveller who was not fasting reached home during the day of Ramadan or a woman in her menses attained purity during the day, what should they do?
quduri.b: They should abstain from the three nullifiers for the rest of the day out of honour for the month.

quduri.f: When does the fast of Ramadan become Wajib and when does the month become established?
quduri.b:
Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Fast when you see it and stop fasting when you see it. If it is cloudy then complete 30 days of Sha'ban." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]

It is thus Wajib on the people to search for the new moon on the 29th of Sha'ban. If they see it they must fast the next day. If the moon is covered by clouds [they cannot see it] they must complete 30 days of Sha'ban and then fast.

quduri.f: If a single man testified that he saw the new moon of the 29th of Sha'ban and the sky was not clear, will his testimony be accepted?
quduri.b: Yes, the testimony of a single Muslim will be accepted in that case, be it male or female, free or slave.

quduri.f: And if the sky was clear and one or two men testified?
quduri.b: The testimony will not be accepted unless a large group testifies so that there is no doubt of their news.

quduri.f: That concerns establishing the new moon of Ramadan. What of the new moon for 'Id?
quduri.b: If the sky is not clear then the testimony of two men or a man and two women will only be accepted. If it is clear then a whole group must testify so that there is no doubt.

quduri.f: What should a man do who has seen the moon of Ramadan or 'Id and the Imam did not accept his testimony?
quduri.b: If it occurred for Ramadan then he should fast alone. If it occurred for 'Id then he should fast with the people and ignore his sighting.

quduri.f: You mentioned the condition of intention when you defined fasting. What are the details thereof?
quduri.b:
The intention is the affirmation in the heart that one is fasting a particular fast.
There are several categories of fasts:
Fard i.e. Ramadan
Specified Nazr [vow] such as vowing to fast next Thursday or the day a particular date will occur.
General vow such as vowing to fast for the sake of Allaah.
Qada of Ramadan.
A Wajib Qada of nullified Nafl Fast.
Kaffarat e.g. broken oath; broken fast; Zhihar and killing.
Nafl.
The fast of Ramadan and specified vow and Nafl can be intended from the night but it is not a condition that it is made at night. If no intention was made until the morning then it is valid until before half the day.107 

Fasts of Qada of Ramadan; general vow; Kaffarat and Qada of nullified Nafl are not valid except with an intention from the night.

107 It is necessary that there be an intention for most of the day. The half is from dawn until bright morning, not Zawal which is later. The intention must therefore be made before that so that most of the day is covered.

quduri.f: If someone is performing a Tamattu' or Qiran108 Hajj because he cannot afford Hady, must he intend the fast from the night?
quduri.b:
Yes, just as the fasts of the other Kaffarat.

108 These will be defined in Kitabul Hajj

quduri.f: It is apparent from your words that Qada is made for nullified Nafl. Please explain.
quduri.b: The one performing Nafl is in control of himself before commencing. Once he begins it is Wajib to complete. If he nullifies it then it is Wajib to make Qada of what he started, be it fast, Salah, Hajj or 'Umrah.

quduri.f: What nullifies Fast?
quduri.b:
Ejaculating due to kissing or touching.
Swallowing a pebble or iron or seed.
Intercourse whether vaginal or anal.
To take an enema or snuff.
To put drops of medicine in the ear.
Taking medication which reaches the stomach or brain.
Having Suhur [predawn meal] and thinking that dawn did not arise when it did.
Having Iftar [breaking fast meal] thinking that the sun set when it did not.
In all these scenarios the fast is void. Qada must be kept but not Kaffarah.

quduri.f: If he places drops on the outer opening of the urethra?
quduri.b: The fast is not void according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. It is void according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى.

quduri.f: Does unintended vomiting or induced vomiting nullify the fast?
quduri.b: If he is overpowered by vomiting then the fast is not void. If he deliberately vomits a mouth full then he must render Qada.

quduri.f: What makes Qada and Kaffarah Wajib together?
quduri.b: One who intentionally has intercourse - vaginal or anal - or one who eats or drinks food or medicine. His fast is void and he must make Qada and Kaffarah.

quduri.f: What is the Kaffarah?
quduri.b: To free a slave. If unable to then fast two months consecutively in which there is no Ramadan or days wherein fasting is forbidden - we shall explain that InshaAllaah. If he is unable to do that then he must feed 60 Miskin.

quduri.f: Is there kaffarah for voiding fasts besides Ramadan?
quduri.b: No, even if it is voiding Qada of Ramadan.

quduri.f: Mention those things which the fasting person undergoes which do not break the fast.
What is Makruh for the fasting person to do?
quduri.b: To kiss, if he cannot control himself. If he can control himself then there is no harm. It is also Makruh to taste or chew or clean the mouth with anything besides Miswak, such as medicinal powder. It is Makruh for a woman to chew food for her child is she can avoid it. If it is unavoidable then there is no harm.

quduri.f: Must Qada of the fasts of Ramadan be kept consecutively?
quduri.b: No, one may keep them separately or consecutively.

quduri.f: What should he do if he delayed it [i.e. Qada of the fasts of Ramadan] so long that the next Ramadan arrived?
quduri.b: He should first fast the current Ramadan and then keep the Qada. There is no Fidyah to be paid for this.

quduri.f: A man died with unfulfilled Qada. He left a bequest that his executor pays his Fidyah from his estate. What is the duty of the executor?
quduri.b: The bequest may be fulfilled from a third of the estate only. The executor will then feed on his behalf a Miskin for every day missed, a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of dates or barley.

quduri.f: Are there fasts outside of Ramadan?
quduri.b: The Fast of Ramadan is Fard. If he keeps Nafl fasts outside of Ramadan he will be rewarded if Allaah wills

quduri.f: Are there days when voluntary Fasts are forbidden?
quduri.b:
Yes, there are five days when fasting is forbidden:
'Idul Fitr
'Idul Adha
The three days thereafter called the Days of Tashriq.

quduri.f: Is there greater virtue for some fasts over others?
quduri.b:
Yes, the Ahadith mention the virtues of certain special fasts:
'Aisha رضي الله عنها narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to fast Mondays and Thursdays." [at-Tirmizi]
Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "deeds are presented Mondays and Thursdays. I like that my deeds be presented and I am fasting." [Ibid]
Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ would never leave the fasts of Ayyamul Biaz whether at home or travelling."109 
Abu Qatadah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "For the fast of 'Arafah110 I hope that Allaah will forgive the sins of the passed year and the next year. For the fast of Ashura111 I hope that Allaah will forgive the sins of the passed year." [Muslim]
Abu Ayyub al-Ansari رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who fasts Ramadan and then follows it with six days of Shawwal is like one who fasted the whole period (year)." [Muslim]
109 Narrated by an-Nasai. In the narration of at-Timirzi they are explained as the 13th, 14th and 15th of each month.

110 9th Zul Hijjah.

11 10th Muharram.

quduri.f: What is the definition and status of I'tikaf?
quduri.b: It is to stay in the Masjid with an intention. It is Sunnah Muakkadah upon Kifayah during the last days of Ramadan. If a single man of the area sits for I'tikaf then the obligation is lifted from the community, if not, then they are all guilty of abandoning that Sunnah.

quduri.f: Is there any other kind of I'tikaf in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: Yes, there are Mustahab and Wajib I'tikaf. The least Mustahab I'tikaf is for a single moment in which one enters the Masjid and intends I'tikaf. He will remain in I'tikaf until he leaves the Masjid.

quduri.f: When does I'tikaf become Wajib?
quduri.b: When one makes a nazr [vow] of I'tikaf it becomes Wajib.

quduri.f: If one vowed I'tikaf of the day, does the night become Wajib as well?
quduri.b: Yes, the nights are subsidiary to the days, even if he did not stipulate it.

quduri.f: Is fasting a condition for a vowed I'tikaf?
quduri.b: Yes, even if he says, "For Allaah I will make i'tikaf for a month without fasting."

quduri.f: What is the Mu'takif [one making I'tikaf] forbidden from?
quduri.b: He is prohibited from sex and its incitements such as touching and kissing. If he has sex in the day or night, forgetfully or deliberately; or ejaculates due to kissing or touching his I'tikaf is void and one must make Qada.

quduri.f: Can the Mu'takif leave the Masjid?
quduri.b: He may not leave except for natural needs such as urinating and defecating. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى if he leaves for even a moment without an excuse then the I'tikaf is void. According to his two companions it is only void if he left for more than half a day.

quduri.f: If he is in I'tikaf in Masjid where there is no Jumu'ah, how does he pray Jumu'ah?
quduri.b: When the time is for Jumu'ah he will got to a Masjid where Jumu'ah is prayed and return to I'tikaf after the Salah.

quduri.f: What is the Mu'takif allowed to do?
quduri.b: He may eat, drink and sleep in the Masjid. He may buy and sell in the Masjid without bringing the commodity itself.

quduri.f: We see that people in I'tikaf not talking, thinking that that nullifies the I'tikaf. What do the Fuqaha say about that?
quduri.b: Talking does not nullify the I'tikaf. However, he should only speak good things and bad speech is prohibited in all circumstances. Silence with the belief that it is part of I'tikaf is Makruh.

quduri.f: What is Hajj linguistically and Islaamically?
quduri.b:
Linguistically it is an intention to do something which is honoured. In Shari'ah it is the visiting of specified places at specified times with specified actions. We shall explain all these in detail InshaAllaah.112

112 The special place is the Ka'bah and the Plains of 'Arafat. The special time is the times specified for Tawaf, staying at 'Arafat. The special acts are Ihram with the intention of Hajj which should be made before the Tawaf and 'Arafat.

quduri.f: What is the status of Hajj in Islaam?
quduri.b: It is a pillar of Islaam. Whoever disputes its being Fard is out of the pale of Islaam. Allaah says, "For Allaah upon the people is that they make Hajj of the House upon whoever has the means to do it."

quduri.f: Upon whom is Hajj Fard?
quduri.b: Hajj is Fard upon free, mature, intelligent, healthy Muslims on condition that the way is safe and they have means of travel, provision and transport, whether through possession or rental. Another condition is that his wealth be in excess of his residence, other necessities and expenses on his family until his return.

quduri.f: Are there any additional conditions for a woman?
quduri.b: Yes, she must travel with a Mahram or husband. She may not travel without one of them if her home is at least the distance of Qasr away from the Ka'abah.

quduri.f: What is Fard in Hajj?
quduri.b:
There are 3 Fard:
Ihram
Wuquf [staying] at 'Arafat
Tawafuz Ziyarah

quduri.f: What is Wajib in Hajj?
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
Wuquf of Muzdalifah after dawn on the Day of Nahr.
Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa.
Pelting the Jimar.
Tawafus Sadr [when first coming] for one from Afaq [outside the Haram and Hill].
Shaving or shortening the hair.
Extending the Wuquf of 'Arafat until sunset.
For one performing Qiran [Qarin] or Tamattu' [Mutamatti'] to slaughter a Hady.
A Mufrid [one performing Ifrad] should observe the sequence of pelting and then shaving. The Qarin and Mutamatti' should observe the sequence between pelting then slaughter then shaving.
To perform Tawafuz Ziyarah during the Days of Nahr.
Shaving or shortening the hair within the Haram;
and that they be in the Days of Nahr.

quduri.f: What are the Sunan? [i.e. of Hajj]
quduri.b:
They are:
Tawaful Qudum for a Mufrid from Afaq as well as a Qarin.
Ramal and Idtiba' in Tawaf and to intend Sa'y thereafter between as-Safa and al-Marwa.
To go to Mina on the Day of Tarwiyah and to spend the following night there.
To leave Mina for 'Arafat after the sun has risen on the Day of Arafat.
To spend the night of the Day of Nahr at al-Muzdalifah.
To make Ghusl at 'Arafat.
To spend the nights at 'Mina of the days of Nahr (i.e. 10th/11th/12th)

quduri.f: What are the Miqat which are not permissible to pass except in a state of Ihram?
quduri.b:
The Nabi ﷺ established 5 Miqat:
Zul Hulayfah for the people of al-Madinah. [about 14km from al-Madinah in the direction of Makkah]
Zatul 'Irq for the people of 'Iraq. [It is no longer known where it is, they therefore go through al-Madinah and enter into Ihram at Zul Hulayfah]
al-Juhfah for the people of Syria. [This was a big town in the era of Rasulullaah ﷺ. It was 4 miles from Rabigh on the left side when going to Makkah. It has become effaced and the roads of the Hujjaj do not pass through it. The people of Syria enter Ihram when they pass Zul Hulayfah]
Qarn for the people of Najd.
Yalamlam for the people of Yemen. [It is also called Sa'diyah today. It is a mountain the people of Yemen pass when going to Makkah]
These are for the people of the lands mentioned and whoever passes them.

quduri.f: Those Miqat are for people living outside those borders. What about those people who live at the Miqat, between the Miqat and the Haram, or in the Haram?
quduri.b: He who lives at the Miqat will enter into Ihram there. The Miqat of one living between the Miqat and the Haram is the Hill. The Hill is the area between the Miqat and Haram. The Hajj Miqat of one living in the Haram is the Haram and his 'Umrah Miqat is the Hill.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to enter Ihram before these Miqat?
quduri.b: Yes, in fact it is better to enter early into Ihram in the months of Hajj when it is better if he can control himself from the Ihram restrictions.

quduri.f: And if he enter Ihram after the Miqat?
quduri.b: That is not permissible. If he did it after passing the Miqat then Damm is Wajib on him.

quduri.f: A man travelling to Makkah does not pass any of the mentioned Miqat. Where should he enter Ihram?
quduri.b: When he crosses a line going through two Miqat on either side of him.

quduri.f: What is Ihram?
quduri.b:
Intention of Hajj or 'Umrah with Talbiyah.113

113 The intention need not be joined specifically with Talbiyah which is Sunnah. It is allowed to join it with any other Zikr. Talbiya must be with the tongue, if only in the heart then it is not valid. [Raddul Muhtar 158/2]

quduri.f: Is there a Sunnah method of Ihram?
quduri.b:
Yes. When one intends Ihram one should make Wudu, although Ghusl would be better. He will then don two new or at least washed cloths which are not stitched like clothing. One will be the Izar [cover the lower body] and one will be the Rida [cover the upper body]. He will apply fragrance if he has. He will pray two Rak'at covering his head. Thereafter he will uncover his head and say as an intention of Hajj, "O Allaah, I intend Hajj, so ease it for me and accept it from me."

He will then recite the Talbiyah,
"Labbayk, Allaahumma labbayk. Labbayka la sharika laka labbayk. Innalhamada wanni'mata laka wal mulk. La sharika laka"
"At Your service, O Allaah at Your service. At Your service, there is no partner unto You, at Your service. Verily praise and bounties belong to You and the kingship. There is no partner with You."

He will not add in between these words. It is allowed to add words afterwards. Once he recited the talbiyah then he is in Ihram. He should now be careful of the Ihram restrictions.

quduri.f: If a woman is in her menses or childbirth period, may she enter Ihram of Hajj or must she wait until the bleeding stops?
quduri.b: She will not wait. She will make Ghusl if she finds a place to do it. She will then comb her hair and enter Ihram without the two Rak'at. She will intend Hajj or 'Umrah and recite Talbiyah. She is now in Ihram. When she enters Makkah she will await the end of the bleeding. She will then make Ghusl and Tawaf.

quduri.f: What are the restrictions when in Ihram?
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
Obscenity.
Lewdness.
Dispute.
Hunting land animals.
Showing where prey are to be found;
Indicating where it is [i.e. prey].
Wearing a shirt, trousers, cap, robe or anything which is stitched or embroided or made in the shape of the body.
Wearing gloves or leather socks, unless one does not find sandals. In that case it will be cut to expose the Ka'ab [humped bone on top of the feet].
Covering head or face. No cap or turban may be worn.
Applying fragrance.
Shaving or shortening the hair on the head or the beard or removing a hair from the body wherever it may be.
Cutting the nails.

Wearing cloth dyed with substances like safflower and saffron unless it has been washed and does not exude fragrance.

quduri.f: Are these [i.e. the 13 restrictions mentioned in question 532] the restrictions of Ihram of Hajj or 'Umrah?
quduri.b: Both.

quduri.f: Is there a difference between the restrictions of a man and a woman?
quduri.b: They apply to both, except that she will wear the clothing she normally wears. She will cover her head but not her face.

quduri.f: Can one in Ihram [Muhrim] bath?
quduri.b: Yes, but without any kind of fragrance including soap. He may not wash away dirt [in such a way that hair falls].

quduri.f: May the Muhrim rest in the shade of a house, car, tent etc?
quduri.b: All these are allowed.

quduri.f: What is the ruling to read a great quantity of Talbiyah?
quduri.b: It is Mustahab, especially after Salah and dawn, when changing in any state, when morning or evening begins, when ascending a height, when going down a valley or meeting a group

quduri.f: What does a Mufrid do when entering Makkah?
quduri.b:
He should first go to al-Masjid al-Haram in a state of Wudu. When he sees the Ka'bah he should recite, "Allaahu Akbar!" and, "La ilaha illAllaah!" He will then make Tawaf which will be the first Tawaf of the Hajj -e- Mufrid. It is a Sunnah for the Afaqi who came from beyond the Miqat. It is called Tawaful Qudum. It is not a duty for the people of Makkah and the Hill.114

114 Ghunyatun Nasik: It is Sunnah for the Mufrid Hajj and the Qarin. If he entered before the months of Hajj then it is not Sunnah for one making 'Umrah, the Mutamatti', the Makki, the people of the Miqat and those living between there and Makkah."
Al-Fath: "It is Sunnah for the Afaqi not for others."

quduri.f: Explain how Tawaf should be performed?
quduri.b: He will begin by al-Hajar al-Aswad. He will face it and raise his hands when saying "Allaahu Akbar." he will then say, "La ilaha illAllaah", and place his hands on it [Istilam] and kiss it if he can do it without harming any Muslim. If he cannot kiss it without harming a Muslim he will place his hands on it and kiss his hands. If he cannot, then at least one hand and kiss it. The right hand is preferred. If he cannot do that hen he should touch the stone with something he is holding such as a staff, then kiss that object. If he cannot do that he should stand in line with the stone and face it. He will raise his hands in line with his ears as at the time of Takbir, with his palms facing the Stone. He will be indicating as if he is placing his palms on the Stone. He will then kiss his palms. He will then move to the right of the Stone to the section where the Door of the Ka'bah is. He will keep the Ka'bah to his left and will pass on the outside of the Hatim. He will make Istilam of the Yemeni Corner when he reaches it. He will then again make Istilam of the Stone and kiss it. This is a complete single circuit. Seven circuits must be completed. Istilam of the Stone must be done as mentioned. The Tawaf begins and ends with Istilam of the Stone.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Ramal and Idtiba'?
quduri.b: They are Sunnah for one intending to perform Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa after the Tawaf. Ramal is only Sunnah in the first three circuits. Idtiba' is Sunnah in all seven. Thus one who intends Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa will perform Ramal and Idtiba', otherwise not. The one performing 'Umrah will perform both acts in his Tawaf because he will make Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa after his Tawaf of 'Umrah.

quduri.f: Explain the Sunnah of Ramal.
quduri.b: It is to shake the shoulders during his walk like one going for a duel between two armies. He should hasten in his walk.

quduri.f: What is Idtiba?
quduri.b: To take the end of the Rida from his right shoulder and throw both ends of his left shoulder. The right shoulder will be left exposed.

quduri.f: Is anything Wajib after Tawaf?
quduri.b: Yes, two Rak'at.

quduri.f: Were are they [i.e. the 2 Rak'at after Tawaf] prayed?
quduri.b: It is best at Maqam Ibrahim عليه السلام, in such a way that it is between him and the Ka'bah. If prayed anywhere else in the Masjid where it is easy for him, it is permissible.

quduri.f: Are the Masnun Surahs to be recited in them? [i.e. in the two Rak'at after Tawaf]
quduri.b: Jabir رضي الله عنه narrated that Rasulullaah ﷺ recited al-Kafirun in the first Rak'ah and al-Ikhlas in the second Rak'ah. [Muslim]

quduri.f: How is Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa performed?
quduri.b:
When the one performing Hajj or 'Umrah intends to make Sa'y he must make Istilam of the Black Stone after the two Rak'at of Tawaf. He will then go to as-Safa and ascend it at least a bit. He will recite, "Innas-Safa wal-Marwa min Sha'airillah." He will face the Ka'bah and recite Takbir and, "La ilaha illAlaah", and salutations upon Rasulullaah ﷺ. He should ask Allaah for his needs. As per the narration of Muslim it is Sunnah to recite the following thrice, "La ilaha illahu wahdahu la sharika lahu. Lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shayin qadir. SadaqAllaahu wa'dahu wa nasara 'abdahu wa hazamal Ahzab wahdah. - There is no illah but Allaah alone who has no partner. To Him belongs all kingship and praise and He has power over everything. Allaah was true to His promise and helped his slave and alone defeated the confederates."

He will then head for al-Marwah at a normal pace. When he reaches the green markings he will hasten until the next green marking whilst reciting, "O my Rabb, Forgive me and have mercy. You are Most Honourable and Noble. Overlook that which You know of."115 

After the passing the second green marking he will resume a normal pace. When he reaches al-Marwah, he will climb it and do the same as per as-Safa. This is one circuit. He will complete seven circuits. He began at as-Safa and will end at al-Marwa. He will remember Allaah throughout the Sa'y. Everytime he passes between the green markings he will run, going time and coming time. A woman will not run, she will walk at her normal pace throughout the Sa'y.

115 At-Tabarani, narrated from Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه.

quduri.f: The Hajji has completed the Tawaful Qudum and the Sa'y. What should he do whether there are many or few days left for Hajj?
quduri.b: He will stay in Makkah in Ihram. He will make Tawaf at every opportunity. He will pray the 5 Salah in al-Masjid al-Haram. He will not miss them with congegration, because the Salah there is worth 100,000 Salah elsewhere. On the Day of Tarwiyah he will go to Mina.

quduri.f: What will he do when he reaches Mina?
quduri.b: He will stay there until after sunrise on the Day of 'Arafat. He will pray 5 Salah with congegration at Mina.

quduri.f: What will he do when the sun has risen on the Day of 'Arafah?
quduri.b: When the sun rises over Thabir, the mountain at Mina, he will head for 'Arafat and stay there until the sun sets. After Zawal the Imam will lead the people in Zhuhr and 'Asr. He will deliver two Khutbahs before Salah in which he will teach the people about the Salah, the Wuquf of 'Arafat, the Wuquf at al-Muzdalifah, the pelting of the Jimar, the slaughter, the sahving and Tawafiz Ziyarah. He will lead them in Zhuhr and 'Asr in the Waqt of Zhuhr, with one Azan and two Iqamah. This is joining of the two Salah in the earlier Waqt. The conditions for this are that the Imam of the Muslims or his representative lead the Salah, that they be in Ihram of Hajj and the Waqt be Zhuhr. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. The one praying on his own or behind any other Imam besides the Imam of Hajj will pray each Salah in its own Waqt. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the Salah will be joined even for one praying on his own.

quduri.f: What will he do after Salah? [i.e. on the Day of 'Arafah]
quduri.b: He will then stay at a place of Wuquf. All of 'Arafat is a place for Wuquf except the low point. It is recommended that he engage in as much du'a as possible until sunset. He will pray 'Asr in its Waqt if he did not do so with the Imam of Hajj. It is Mustahab to make Wuquf near Jabal ar-Rahman, standing as much as possible and making du'a. It is also allowed to engage in du'a at one's tent. It is Mustahab for the Imam of Hajj to make Wuquf at 'Arafat upon his mount, making du'a and teaching people the laws of Hajj.

quduri.f: After the Wuquf at 'Arafat, what should be done after the sun sets?
quduri.b: When the sun sets he should leave 'Arafat and head for al-Muzdalifah. He will not pray Maghrib at 'Arafat, nor on the way to al-Muzdalifah. At al-Muzdalifah he will pray Maghrib and Isha combined, whether the Imam of Hajj or not. This is the joining in the latter Waqt.

quduri.f: Will he join the Salahs if praying alone [i.e. combining Maghrib and Isha at al-Muzdalifah]?
quduri.b: Yes. Congegration is not a condition.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of praying Maghrib at 'Arafat or on the road?
quduri.b: It is void and must be repeated.
