quduri.f: What will he do after these two Salah? [i.e. the combined Maghrib and Isha at al-Muzdalifah]
quduri.b: He will spend the night at al-Muzdalifah until true dawn. He will then pray Fajr with congegration while it is still dark. He will remain and remember Allaah and offer du'a until just before sunrise. All of al-Muzdalifah is a place for the Wuquf except for the Valley of Muhassar.

quduri.f: What does the Hajj do after the Wuquf at al-Muzdalifah?
quduri.b:
A short while before sunrise he will head for Mina. When he reaches there he will pelt Jamratul 'Aqabah with 7 pebbles, such as the pebbles used in Hazaf [a game where a pebble is flung from the nail of the numb]. He will recite each time he pelts, "In the Name of Allaah, Allaah is the greatest. For the pleasure of ar-Rahman, and to displease the Satan."

He will not hang about there after the pelting. He will end the Talbiyah with the throwing of the first pebble.

quduri.f: Does he have to slaughter? [i.e. the Mufrid]
quduri.b: For the Mufrid slaughter is Mustahab only.

quduri.f: What does he [i.e. the Hajji after pelting] do next?
quduri.b: After pelting Jamratul 'Aqabah on the Day of Nahr, the Mufrid will clip his hair. To shave it is better. He is now released from Ihram and all restrictions except (taking benefit from) woman are lifted from him. He may wear stitched trousers and shirts etc. He may apply fragrance to his body and clothing, cut his hair and clip his nails. The Mutammati' and Qari must slaughter the Hady after the pelting of Jamratul 'Aqabah. He will then only cut or shave his head.

quduri.f: If a Mufrid wants to slaughter, should he cut or shave his head before or after the slaughter?
quduri.b: Both are allowed, but to do so after the slaughter is better.

quduri.f: Where will he cut or shave?
quduri.b: Within the boundaries of the Haram. If he does so outside the boundaries then he has to pay the Damm.

quduri.f: Are there any other duties remaining on the Day of Nahr after shaving?
quduri.b: Yes, Tawafuz Ziyarah which is a Fard Tawaf. Its time is the three days from sunrise on the Day of Nahr until sunset on the 12th. It is best to do it on the Day of Nahr. After shaving or cutting his head he will go to Makkah and circle the Ka'bah seven times as we discussed under Tawaful Qudum. After Tawaful Ziyarah women become permissible for him as well.

quduri.f: Will he make Ramal and Idtiba' as well? [i.e. during Tawafuz Ziyarah]
quduri.b: If he did not do Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwa after Tawaful Qudum he must do so now after Tawafuz Ziyarah. He will not make Ramal in the first three circuits of Tawafuz Ziyarah. There is no opportunity for Idtiba' as he wears normal clothing after shaving.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he delays the Tawafuz Ziyarah after the thre days you have mentioned?
quduri.b: Damm is Wajib upon him according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى but not according to his two companions.

quduri.f: What does he do after Tawafuz Ziyarah?
quduri.b: He will return and stay at Mina. He will pelt the 3 Jimar on the 11th and 12th. Each day the pelting will be after Zawal. He will first pelt the Smallest Jamrah, which is closest to Masjidul Khayf; then the Middle Jamrah; then the Biggest Jamrah which is Jamratul 'Aqabah. He will pelt each Jamrah with 7 pebbles, reciting Takbir and "La ilaha illAllaah" with every pebble. After pelting the first two he will turn to the right of the place of pelting and make du'a. He will not pause for the du'a after pelting the Biggest Jamrah, but will offer his du'a whilst walking away from it.

quduri.f: If he pelts during these two days before Zawal, is it valid?
quduri.b: The Waqt of pelting in these two days is from Zawal until true dawn. He who hastens and pelts before Zawal must repeat his pelting.

quduri.f: What does he do after pelting the 3 Jimar on these two days?
quduri.b:
He may either leave for Makkah or stay at Mina and pelt on the 13th as well. Allaah says, "He who hastens for the two days only there is no sin on him. He who tarries beyond that, there is no sin on him - for those who have Taqwa."

However, if the sun sets on the 12th and he is still at Mina, it is Makruh for him to leave Mina before pelting on the 13th. If he is at Mina when true dawn arises on the 13th, then the pelting of that day becomes Wajib.

quduri.f: When must one who tarries to pelt on the 13th do it?
quduri.b: It is Sunnah to pelt after Zawal. The time on this day is until sunset, so it is incorrect after sunset. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is allowed to pelt before Zawal, although it is Makruh for being contrary to the Sunnah. His two companions say that pelting is not correct before Zawal on that day as well.

quduri.f: A man stays at Mina to pelt during these days. Is it permissible for him to take his luggage to Makkah?
quduri.b: It is Makruh for him to take his luggage to Makkah while he stays at Mina.

quduri.f: What should he then do when he reaches Makkah after the first or second Nahr?
quduri.b: After the pelting the only act of Hajj which remains is Tawaful Wida'. It is also called Tawafus Sadar. It is Wajib upon the Afaqi. When he returns to Makkah he may now perform Tawaful Wida' and return to his homeland. If he is prevented from leaving for any reason, he can stay how long he wishes.

quduri.f: Should he then perform Tawaful Wida' when he leaves Mina or delay it until he ultimately leaves Makkah?
quduri.b: As soon as he makes a Tawaf after Tawafuz Ziyarah is counts as Tawaful Wida', even if his intention was Nafl Tawaf. It is however Mustahab for him to delay his intended Tawaful Wida' until he is going to leave for his homeland.

quduri.f: Is there Ramal and Idtiba' in Tawaful Wida'?
quduri.b: No, because there is no Sa'y thereafter.

quduri.f: A man enters Ihram at the Miqat and does not enter Makkah. He goes and does Wuquf at 'Arafat without having made Tawaful Qudum. What should he do?
quduri.b: Tawaful Qudum falls away from him.

quduri.f: A man reaches 'Arafat after sunset on the Day of 'Arafah. Is his Hajj valid?
quduri.b: Whoever makes Wuquf of 'Arafah anytime from the Day of 'Arafat from Zawal until dawn of the Day of Nahr has attained Hajj; however short the time.

quduri.f: Is it a condition to make du'a at 'Arafat to attain Hajj?
quduri.b: The du'a is Sunnah. One who passes through 'Arafah even for a short time, whether he was awake or asleep or unconscious; as long as he was in Ihram his Wuquf is valid, even to the extent that he did not know that that was 'Arafat.

quduri.f: Are all these the regulations for a man alone or for a woman as well?
quduri.b:
A woman does the same except that she does not expose her head.
She will not drape her Rida or veil over her face.
She will not raise her voice in Talbiyah.
She will not make Ramal in Tawaf.
She will not run between the green markings during Sa'y.
She will clip her hair and not shave it.
If she is in her menstrual or childbirth period when entering Ihram or after entering, and does not become pure until the Day of Tarwiyah, she will not perform Tawaful Qudum. She will in that case go to Mina and perform all the rest of the Hajj rituals, except that she will not make Tawafuz Ziyarah until she is pure. If she has menses or childbirth after Tawafuz Ziyarah and the time has come for her departure, then she may omit Tawaful Wida' without any penalty.

quduri.f: What is 'Umrah linguistcally and in Shari'ah? What are its Fard and Wajib actions? How is it performed?
quduri.b:
Linguistically 'Umrah means to visit. In Shari'ah it encompasses the following four:
Ihram
Tawaf of the Ka'bah
Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah
Shaving or cutting the head
The first two are Fard and the second two are Wajib. When one wants to perform 'Umrah then one will enter Ihram at the Miqat. First perform Wudu or Ghusl and then two Rak'at. Then say the intention of 'Umrah, "O Allaah I intend 'Umrah. Ease it for me and accept it from me." Then recite Talbiyah as we mentioned in the Ihram of Hajj. Once the Talbiyah is recited then Ihram has been entered. Upon entering Makkah he will circle the Ka'bah seven times and then make Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah. He will then shave or clip hair off the head. Upon doing that the 'Umrah is complete and he has emerged from the Ihram as well.

quduri.f: Are there restrictions in the Ihram of 'Umrah?
quduri.b: Yes. They are the same as the restrictions of the Hajj Ihram mentioned.

quduri.f: What is the Miqat for 'Umrah Ihram?
quduri.b: For the Afaqi it is the same as the Miqat of Hajj. The Hilli will enter Ihram from the Hill. The one in the Haram will leave for the Hill where he will enter Ihram.

quduri.f: What is the status of 'Umrah in Islaam?
quduri.b:
It is Sunnah Muakkadah once in a lifetime for one who is able to reach Makkah. It has great virtues.116 

116 Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "One Umrah to the next expiates what is between them. There is no reward for an accepted Hajj except Jannah." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]

quduri.f: What is the ruling of talbiyah in the Ihram of 'Umrah?
quduri.b: Talbiyah is a condition for entering Ihram. It is Mustahab to recite it frequently thereafter just as in the Ihram of Hajj. One will stop reciting it when beginning the first circuit of Tawaf.

quduri.f: Is there Tawaful Qudum and Tawaful Wida' in 'Umrah?
quduri.b: No. Every Tawaf made after Ihram will be part of the 'Umrah.

quduri.f: Is there a specified time for 'Umrah as in Hajj?
quduri.b:
No. One may perform 'Umrah whenever one wishes, except that it is Makruh Tahrimi from the 9th Zul Hijjah until the last day of Tashriq. There is greater reward for 'Umrah during Ramadan. 'Umrah then earns the reward like that of Hajj.117

117 Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "An Umrah in Ramadan equals a Hajj." [Muslim]

quduri.f: Can 'Umrah be made with Hajj?
quduri.b: Yes, it will be explained in the discussion on Tamattu' and Qiran.

quduri.f: May the Ihram of Hajj and 'Umrah be joined?
quduri.b: Yes. It is better than Ifrad and Tamattu'. Tamattu' is better than Ifrad. Whoever joins the two Ihram is called Qarin and his Hajj is Qiran.

quduri.f: Describe the Qiran.
quduri.b:
One will enter Umrah and Hajj together at the Miqat. After the two Rak'at one will recite, "O Allaah! I intend Hajj and 'Umrah. Ease them for me and accept them from me."
Then recite Talbiyah which will enter you in Ihram of Hajj and 'Umrah. When entering Makkah circle the Ka'bah seven times with Idtiba' for 'Umrah. Make Ramal in the first three and then at a normal pace in the remaining four. Then make Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah for 'Umrah. Those are the acts of 'Umrah. Then make Tawaful Qudum followed by Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah for Hajj as we explained in the Hajj of the Mufrid. Remain in Ihram until the Day of Tarwiyah when one will go to Mina and perform the Hajj just like the Ifrad described.

quduri.f: Is there anything extra that the Qarin must do compared to the Mufrid?
quduri.b: Yes, it is Wajib upon him to slaughter a Hady after pelting the Biggest Jamrah on the Day of Nahr. He will slaughter a sheep or a sevent of a Budnah in grattitude to Allaah for allowing him to join the two acts of Hajj and 'Umrah. He will then only shave or clip his hair. He is then released from both Ihram at the same time just as he had entered both at the same time. He is not allowed to shave or clip except after the slaughter. All restrictions are now lifted from him except the restriction of women which is only lifted after Tawafuz Ziyarah.

quduri.f: What does he do [i.e. the Qarin] if he does not have money to buy a Hady?
quduri.b: He will fast three days during Hajj, the last day being the Day of 'Arafat. He will then fast 7 days when he returns home. That completes 10.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he missed a day of fasting and it is already the Day of 'Nahr?
quduri.b: He has no option now except slaughter of a Hady.

quduri.f: is it allowed to fast the remaining 7 whilst still in Makkah, i.e. before returning home?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of one who entered Ihram of Hajj and 'Umrah but did not enter Makkah but he went straight to 'Arafat?
quduri.b: When he makes Wuquf at 'Arafat he has dropped the 'Umrah and does not have to slaughter the Hady of Qiran. He must pay Damm for omitting the 'Umrah and must make Qada of it as well.

quduri.f: What is Tamattu'?
quduri.b: It is to enter Ihram at the Miqat and then go to Makkah and perform 'Umrah during the months of Hajj. He will stop Talbiyah when commencing Tawaf. After Tawaf he will make Sa'y. After shaving or clipping his hair he is out of the Ihram of 'Umrah. He will remain at Makkah without Ihram and will make as many Tawaf as he can. He will pray the 5 Salah in congegration in al-Masjid al-Haram. He will then enter Ihram of Hajj in the Haram on the Day of Tarwiyah. He will perform his Hajj just as the Mufrid. After pelting the Biggest Jamrah on the Day of Nahr he will slaughter a Hady out of gratitude to Allaah for allowing him to join the Hajj and 'Umrah. If he cannot afford it then he must fast three days in Hajj, the final day being the Day of 'Arafah. He will also fast 7 days when he returns home. He will not shave his head until he has slaughtered. We have mentioned certain rules of the fast under Qiran.

quduri.f: What do you say about someone who entered Ihram of 'Umrah and brought his Hady with him?
quduri.b: There are two kinds of Mutamatti'. One who does not bring a Hady, and we have described his Tamattu'. The other is the one who makes Ihram of 'Umrah only at the Miqat and goes to Makkah with his Hady. If it is bovine he will tie a bag or sandal around its neck. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى, Ish'ar is done on camels. The famous narration from Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى is that it is Makruh because people started to exceed the bounds. It is the slitting the hump from the right. When he enters Makkah he will make Tawaf and Sa'y of 'Umrah. He will not leave his Ihram but will continue in that state. On the Day of Tarwiyah he will renew his Ihram and do his Hajj as a Mufrid does. He will slaughter the Hady after pelting the Biggest Jamrah. He will then shave or clip his hair. Upon that he will be free of both Ihrams.

quduri.f: If the Mutamatti' advances his Ihram and enters Ihram before the Day of Tarwiyah, is it allowed?
quduri.b: Yes, that is also Tamattu'.

quduri.f: What are the months of Hajj?
quduri.b: Shawwal, Zul Qa'dah and the first ten days of Zul Hijjah.

quduri.f: The rites of Hajj are during five days. Why have Shawwal and Zul Qa'dah been made months of Hajj?
quduri.b: Because certain laws apply then. One of these are that if one entered Ihram of 'Umrah and completed most of the circuits of the Tawaf before the new moon of Shawwal set in, then one will not be a Mutamatti'. Another is that it is Makruh to enter into Ihram of Hajj before the new moon of Shawwal.

quduri.f: Someone entered into Ihram of 'Umrah during Shawwal or Zul Qa'dah. He completed the rites of 'Umrah. He went home and returned for Hajj. What is the status of his Tamattu'?
quduri.b: His Tamattu' is void in this scenario if he is not bringing a Hady. He will not give Damm of Tamattu'. This is because Tamattu' is the joining of Hajj and Umrah in a single journey. By going home inbetween it is no longer in a single journey.

quduri.f: Can the people of Makkah perform Qiran and Tamattu'?
quduri.b: No. The people living within the Miqat - the people of Makkah, the Haram and the Hill may not perform Qiran and Tamattu', only Ifrad.

quduri.f: What is a Jinayah [violation] in Hajj and 'Umrah?
quduri.b:
There are two kinds:
Violating the restrictions of Ihram.
Violating the actions of Hajj and 'Umrah, such as leaving a Wajib, mixing the order, delaying a Fard or Wajib from its time.

quduri.f: Explain the violations of Ihram.
quduri.b:
They are 8:
For men to wear stitched clothing.
For men to cover their heads.
For men and women to cover their faces.
To apply fragrance on the body, clothing or bedding.
Shaving or clipping hair from any part of the body.
Cutting the nails.
Hunting a land animal, indicating or showing where it is.
Sex and it preludes such as kissing and touching with lust.

quduri.f: Explain the details of the violation of wearing stitched clothing and its penalties?
quduri.b: If a Muhrim wears stitched clothing; that is clothing which is normally worn as in conformity with the body or a part of the body, whether deliberately or forgetfully or by mistake; whether willingly or by force; whether with or without an excuse then there is a penalty.

quduri.f: What is the penalty? [i.e. if a Muhrim wears stitched clothing]
quduri.b:
He must pay Damm if he wore it for a day or a night or the duration of one of the two; i.e. he must slaughter a sheep118 in the Haram.

118 Damm is a Thani sheep free of defect. Thani will be discussed under Hady. Sadaqah for violations of Ihram is a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of dates/barley/raising or their price.

quduri.f: What is his penalty if he wore it for less than that? [i.e. if the Muhrim wore stitched clothing for a day or a night]
quduri.b: Sadaqah like Sadaqah of Fitr if he worte it for at least an hour, if less, then a handful of wheat.

quduri.f: If he wore it [i.e. a Muhrim with stitched clothing] for several days and nights will he pay a separate penalty for each day?
quduri.b: A single Damm will suffice. However, if he wore it again after the slaughter or cotninued to wear it then another penalty is due.

quduri.f: If he wore different kinds of prohibited clothing at the same time for the duration of the day, e.g. trousers and shirt, does he pay multiple pentalties?
quduri.b: No, a single Damm suffices.

quduri.f: If he wore a shirt as a cloak or a lower-body garment; or wore a trouser on the upper part of his body, what is the penalty?
quduri.b: No penalty. The violation is to wear normal clothing in the normal manner.

quduri.f: Is there a penalty for wearing an Izar or Rida with stitched intervals or edges?
quduri.b: No, that does not make them garments in the shape of the human body or organs. However, it is better that there be no stitching.

quduri.f: What is the penalty for wearing stitched fragranced clothing for the duration of a day?
quduri.b: One Damm for the clothing and another for the fragrance.

quduri.f: Is there a penalty for wearing shoes or socks?
quduri.b: Damm is Wajib if he wore them for a day or night or the duration of one. If he wore less than that Sadaqah is Wajib. The penalties are only if they covered the Ka'b, the protruding bone on the upper part of the foot.

quduri.f: Explain the penalties for covering the face and head.
quduri.b: If the Muhrim covers his whole head or face or even a quarter of either one; or a Muhrimah covers her face or a quarter for a day or a night or the duration of either, then Damm becomes Wajib. This is irrespective whether they did it ignorantly or knowingly, willingly or by force, by mistake, forgetfully or deliberately, wakefully or in sleep, with an excuse or without. If done less than the mentioned time or less than a quarter of the said organs then Sadaqah is Wajib.

quduri.f: What is Wajib if the Muhrim covers his ears, or nape, or the part of his beard below the chin?
quduri.b: Nothing.

quduri.f: What if he [i.e. a Muhrim] covers his head with a metal sheet or stone or wood?
quduri.b: There is no penalty. The restriction is on wearing that which is normally considered a covering such as a cap, turban, hanky, etc.

quduri.f: Is there a penalty if he puts his head under the covering of the Ka'bah?
quduri.b: No. However, if the covering covers his head or faces it is Makruh.

quduri.f: What is the penalty if the Muhrim/ah applies fragrance on the body?
quduri.b: Damm is Wajib if fragrance is applied to a complete organ or more. If on less than a complete organ then Sadaqah is Wajib. By organ is meant for example the head, thigh, calf, lower arm and upper arm. This is if the fragrance is a little. If it is much then the Damm is Wajib even if it is on less than an organ. The custom of the people will determine what is meant by a little and a lot. These apply to large organs as mentioned. As for smaller organs like fingers, ears and eyes, then the ruling is on the least of what is Wajib in the big organ regarding Damm or Sadaqah.

quduri.f: If fragrance was applied to the entire body, are there multiple penalties?
quduri.b: If done at a single time then there is one Damm. If done in multiple sittings then the Damm must be added up according to the number of sittings.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if a woman applied Hinna to her hand?
quduri.b:
Damm is Wajib for that as well.

NOTE: There is no condition in fragrance that an amount of time has to pass. Thus if the fragrance was applied and immediately washed off, the Damm or Sadaqah as applicable, is due. As opposed to clothing, where Damm is payable when worn for the mentioned duration.

quduri.f: What is the penalty for the Muhrim who applies fragrance to his clothing?
quduri.b: Damn is Wajib if he applies it to the clothing he is wearing or clothing he then puts on; and the applied area is more than a hand-span by a hand-span; and the time he wears it is complete day or night. If it is a hand-span by a hand-span then he wears it for a day or night then he must pay Sadaqah. If less than that then a handful of wheat. This is if the fragrance is little. If it is a lot then Damm is Wajib even if the less than a hand-span of the cloth was afflicted. [Raddul Muthar (201/2)]

quduri.f: What is the penalty for applying scented oil?
quduri.b: It is the same as fragrance. Thus if he applies it on his head, Damm is Wajib.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a Muhrim cutting his nails?
quduri.b: If he cuts the nails of his hands and feet, or the nails of one hand or one foot in one sitting then one damm is Wajib. If he cuts all the nails of the hands and feet in separate sittings, then there is a separate penalty for his sitting.

quduri.f: What is the ruling for cutting less than 5 nails?
quduri.b: Sadaqah for each nail.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of cutting 5 nails from separate places, e.g. 2 nails from each hand and one from a foot?
quduri.b: There is also Sadaqah according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى.

quduri.f: What is the penalty upon the Muhrim for shaving his hair?
quduri.b: Damm is Wajib if he shaves his head or beard or a quarter of either. For less than a quarter the penalty is Sadaqah. If he shaves his armpits or pubic hairs then Damm is Wajib. Shortening the hair and shaving it is the same in regards Damm and Sadaqah. If it removed in some other way, or plucked out or combed out then it is the same as ruling as shaving.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the area of cupping was shaved on his neck?
quduri.b: Damm according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Sadaqah according to his two companions.

quduri.f: What is the ruling upon a woman in that? [i.e. shaving in Ihram]
quduri.b:
The ruling as above in shaving the armpits, pubic area and head is the same for a woman as for a man.

NOTE: The penalties are equally applicable whether he did it himself or someone else; with or without his order; willingly or forced; ignorantly or mistakenly; forgetfully or deliberately.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of one who wore stitched clothing; applied fragrance; covered his head or face; shaved his head; or clipped his nails for a valid reason?
quduri.b:
If the Muhrim violates any of these restrictions for a reason, e.g. he was afflicted with feverm there was severe heat or cold, headache or exessive lice then he has a choice in every situation wherein Damm is Wajib to either slaughter a sheep in the Haram or give Sadaqah of 3 Sa' of wheat, or 6 Sa' of raisins/dates/barley to 6 Miskin; giving each of them a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of raisins/dates/barely; or he can fast 3 days.
The rule applies equally to rich and to poor.

If the violation required Sadaqah instead, and he had a reason, then he has a choice Sadaqah or half Sa' of wheat or fasting a day.

quduri.f: Explain the violations of Ihram concerning sex.
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
If a Muhrim of Hajj or 'Umrah kisses or touches a woman or beardless boy with lust, then he must pay Damm, whether he ejaculated or not.
If a Muhrim of Hajj has vaginal or anal sex before the Wuquf of 'Arafat his Hajj is void and he must slaughter a sheep. He will continue the actions of Hajj as if he is still in Hajj and will perform Qada after that year.
If the Hajj had sex after Wuqf of 'Arafat, before Tawafuz Ziyarah and before he shaves his head, then he has to slaughter a Badnah and his Hajj is not void.
If he had sex after shaving his head, before Tawafuz Ziyarah; or after Tawafuz Ziyarah but before shaving, then he must slaughter a sheep.
If a Muhrim of 'Umrah has sex before completing 4 circuits, then his 'Umrah is void. He must make Qada and slaughter a sheep.
If a Muhrim of 'Umrah has sex after completing 4 circuits, then his 'Umrah is not void. He need make Qada but must slaughter a sheep.

quduri.f: Is there a difference between having sex deliberately and forgetfully?
quduri.b: No. The ruling is the same.

quduri.f: If the Hajj is going to make Qada of the Hajj he nullified, is he obligated to separate from his wife in that journey?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Explain the violations of the acts of Hajj?
quduri.b: There are several kinds of volitions. These include Tawaf without Taharah; omitting a Wajib; mixing the order; and delaying a Rukn or Wajib from its time. The details are as below.

quduri.f: What is the penalty for making Tawaf without Taharah?
quduri.b:
The details are:
If the Hajji makes Tawaful Qudum or Tawafus Sadar and he is Muhdith then he must pay Sadaqah of half a Sa' of wheat for every circuit. The same rule applies to any Nafl Tawaf.
If the Hajji makes Tawaful Qudum or Tawafus Sadar and he is Junub, or a woman who is in menses or childbirth periods then they must slaughter a sheep.
If the Hajji makes Tawafuz Ziyarah and he is Muhdith then he must slaughter a sheep,
If the Hajji makes Tawafuz Ziyarah and he is Junub, or a woman who is in menses or childbirth periods then they must slaughter a Badanah [camel]
NOTE: If he made Tawaf while Muhdith or Junub and then repeated the Tawaf with Taharah, then the penalty is dropped.

quduri.f: What is the penalty for omitting a Wajib act of Hajj?
quduri.b:
It is as follows:
One who omits Wuquf at al-Muzdalifah after dawn must pay Damm.
One who omits Sa'y between as-Safa and al-Marwah must pay Damm.
He who omits the pelting of the Jimar on all the days or the pelting of the Biggest Jimar on the Day of Nahr; or omitted most of the pebbles on a given day of pelting; must pay Damm in each of these scenarios. If in a day he left out one of the three Jimar then he must pay Sadaqah.
He who leaves 'Arafat before sunset must pay Damm unless he returns before sunset.
He who leaves out Tawaful Wida' or 4 circuits of it must pay Damm. If he omitted 3 then he must pay Sadaqah. The penalty is dropped if he returns to Makkah and makes Tawaful Wida'.

quduri.f: What does the Muhrim do if he mixed the Wajib order?
quduri.b:
It is as follows:
If Mutamatti' or Qarin slaughters before pelting the Biggest Jamrah or shaved before slaughter then he must pay Damm.
If a Mufrid shaved before pelting the Biggest Jamrah then he must pay Damm.

quduri.f: What delay makes a penalty Wajib?
quduri.b:
It is as follows:
Damm is Wajib when a Mutamatti' or Qarin delays his slaughter after the Days of Nahr.
Damm is Wajib if any Hajji delays his shaving or clipping after the mentioned days.
NOTE: Women will never be allowed for a Hajji until he performs the complete or most of the Tawafuz Ziyarah.

quduri.f: What are the violations of 'Umrah?
quduri.b:
It is as follows:
Damm is Wajib if he delayed entering Ihram to after the Miqat.
Damm is Wajib if one made Tawaf of 'Umrah as a Muhdith or Junub; or a woman was in her menses or childbirth period. There is no difference here between the Muhdith or the Junub, between a little and a lot. The Damm is Wajib if even a single circuit was made without Taharah.
Damm is Wajib if he shaved before Sa'y.
Damm is Wajib if he shaved his head outside the Haram.
NOTE: The penalty of Damm or Sadaqah for violating Ihram is the same whether it was Ihram of Hajj or 'Umrah.

quduri.f: Is there a penalty for a Muhrim of Hajj or 'Umrah if he kills a prey?
quduri.b: There is a Wajib penalty upon a Muhrim who kills a prey; shows someone where the prey is; or even indicates to a hunter. The forgetful one, deliberate one, beginner and repeat offender are all equally liable.

quduri.f: What is the penalty?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the prey will be evaluated in the place it is killed or the nearest place if it was on land. Two just Muslims will do the evaluation. The killer then has a choice between buying at that price a Hady to slaughter in the Haram or to buy food to give as Sadaqah to the Miskin. He will give each Miskin a half Sa' of wheat or a Sa' of dates/barley. If he wishes he can instead fast one day for each half Sa' of wheat or one Sa' of barley. If there was extra food less than a half Sa', he may give it as Sadaqah or he may fast a full day in lieu. The ruling is the same for a small prey which does not reach the value of a full Hady.

quduri.f: Does Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى bin al-Hasan have a different view? [i.e. regarding the penalty for a Muhrim of Hajj or 'Umrah killing prey, see question 634]
quduri.b: Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى rule according to monetary evaluation and then a choice as discussed above. Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى declared that the prey's equivalent animal be used where such exists. Thus the penalty of a deer or hyena will be a sheep; a kid for a rabbit; a Budanah for an ostrich and a lamb for a jerboa. As for hat which does not have a physical equivalent then his ruling is the same as the two Imams.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the Muhrim wounds the prey, plucks its hair or cuts limb?
quduri.b: He is penalised the value of the damage caused.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he plucked the feathers of a bird or cut the legs of an animal?
quduri.b: If the animal then escapes from his sole control then he is penalised with the full price.

quduri.f: If he breaks the egg of a prey?
quduri.b: If a dead chick emergens then the penalty is equivalent had it been alive. If there was no chick in it then he is penalised the value of the egg.

quduri.f: What is the penalty for killing lice or locusts?
quduri.b: He can give what Sadaqah he wishes. A date is more than a locust.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of killing a beast whose flesh is not eaten?
quduri.b: The penalty is imposed on him, except that it will not exceed the value of a sheep.

quduri.f: Is there a penalty if the beast attacked the Muhrim who then killed it?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Are there any animals or birds the Muhrim is allowed to kill?
quduri.b: He may kill crows, vultures, wolves, snakes, scorpions, rats and vicious dogs.

quduri.f: What is the penalty for killing mosquitoes, fleas and apes?
quduri.b: Nothing.

quduri.f: If the Muhrim is forced to eat the flesh of prey and kills it for that purpose, is there still a penalty upon him?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: What do you say about a dove with striped hindquarters or a tame deer?
quduri.b: There is still a penalty for killing them.

quduri.f: If a Muhrim slaughtered a prey, may a non-Muhrim eat from it?
quduri.b: The slaughter of a Muhrim is carrion. It is not permissible for him or anyone else.

quduri.f: Can a Muhrim slaughter that which people usually slaughter to eat?
quduri.b: Yes, a Muhrim may slaughter a sheep, cow, chicken and duck. He and others may eat from these animals if he slaughtered them.

quduri.f: A non-Muhrim hunted and killed a prey. Can the Muhrim eat from it?
quduri.b: He can eat from it if he did not show the hunter where it is nor ordered him to hunt it.

quduri.f: What is the penalty if two Muhrims joined to kill a prey?
quduri.b: Each will pay the full penalty.

quduri.f: If a Muhrim killed a prey and then sold it while in Ihram; or bought it from a Muhrim or a non-Mughrim; what is the ruling?
quduri.b: His selling is valid, his buying is void.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a Qarin who violates the Ihram?
quduri.b:
He has to pay 2 Damm, one for violating the Hajj Ihram and one for the 'Umrah Ihram.
The exception is if he crossed the Miqat without Ihram and then later entered into Ihram of Hajj and 'Umrah, then he is only liable for one Damm in that case.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of one who does not enter Ihram at the Miqat and intends entering Makkah?
quduri.b:
If an Afaqi Muslim who is Mukallaf [responsible for obeying Shari'ah] intends going to Makkah or enter the Haram, even if it is only for business or tourism, and he crosses the Miqat by land, sea or air without Ihram, then whether he later enters Ihram or not he has sinned and must pay Damm.119

119 Ibn Hajar said in Fathul Bari: Malik has quoted the narration of 'Ibn Umar in his Muwatta from Nafi', "'Abdullaah bin 'Umar left Makkah. When he reached Qadid news of trouble reached him and he returned to Makkah without Ihram." In short he regarded Ihram only for one intending Hajj or 'Umrah based on the narration of Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنه, "He who intends Hajj and 'Umrah...." This means that one going to Makkah without intending Hajj or 'Umrah does not need Ihram. The 'Uluma have differed about this. The famous view of ash-Shafi'i is that it is not Wajib... The famous view of the other three Imams is that it is Wajib in all circumstances. There are narrations from all of them that it is not Wajib. This is the view of Ibn 'Umar رضي الله عنهما, az-Zuhri, al-Hasan and the Ahluzh Zhahir.... Ibn 'Abdil Barr claimed that most Sahabah رضي الله عنهم and Tabi'in said that it is Wajib.

quduri.f: Is there a way out of the sin and Damm?
quduri.b: If one crossed the Miqat without Ihram, it is necessary to return to the Miqat, whether the one he crossed (which is best), or the closest one or even the furthest away. When he then enters Ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah at the Miqat, the sin and Damm will lapse.

quduri.f: What is the penalty if he [i.e. the one who crossed the Miqat without Ihram] does not return to the Miqat and enters Ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah in the Hill or Haram?
quduri.b: The sin and Damm remains. He must seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent. He must slaughter a sheep in the Haram - his Damm.

quduri.f: A man crossed the Miqat without Ihram. He fears that if he returns to the Miqat he will miss the Hajj and therefore enters Ihram where he is. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He should not return in that circumstance, but should slaughter a sheep for his violation of crossing the Miqat without Ihram. He must seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent.

quduri.f: A man crossed the Miqat without Ihram. He fears for the safety of his life or wealth if he returns to the Miqat and therefore enters Ihram of 'Umrah where he is. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: It is no longer Wajib to return to the Miqat. Slaughtering the sheep in the Haram will suffice.

quduri.f: A man enters Makkah or the Haram several times without Ihram. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: If he enters Makkah or the Haram without Ihram then for every entry he must make a Hajj or 'Umrah [which now becomes Qada]. If in the same year he enters Ihram for the Hajj or a vowed Hajj or Qada or vowed Qada or Sunnah 'Umrah or Mustahab 'Umrah; that will suffice him for his Qada of entry whether he made intention or the Qada or not. If he does that in the next year then he must make intention.

quduri.f: An Afaqi comes from a journey to the Miqat at Jaddah. He does not intend Hajj or 'Umrah, nor entry into Makkah or the Haram. What is his ruling?
quduri.b: There is no sin or penalty upon him.

quduri.f: If after coming to Jaddah he [i.e. an Afaqi coming from a journey to the Miqat at Jaddah] then wishes to enter the Haram or Makkah, what must he do?
quduri.b: In this scenario it is permissible for him to enter Makkah or the Haram without Ihram. If he intends Hajj or 'Umrah after reaching Jaddah, then he must enter Ihram from Jaddah or any place in the Hill.

quduri.f: Are the people of the Miqat or Hill allowed to enter the Haram or Makkah without Ihram?
quduri.b: They are allowed to when they do not intend Hajj or 'Umrah. If they enter Makkah or the Haram without Ihram, and intended Hajj or 'Umrah, then Damm becomes Wajib upon them. They will have to return to their Miqat, which is the Hill. If they entered Ihram of Hajj or 'Umrah at the Haram and did not return to the Hill; or they did return but did not make Talbiyah there before beginning Tawaf, they are sinners and the Damm is still payable.

quduri.f: Is one living in the Haram allowed to enter Ihram of 'Umrah in Makkah or the Haram?
quduri.b: No. For the people of the Haram, their Hajj Miqat is the Haram and their 'Umrah Miqat is the Hill. If they do not enter Ihram at their specified Miqat they have sinned and must pay Damm.

quduri.f: What are the violations of the Haram?
quduri.b:
They are two:
Killing prey in it.
Cutting its trees and grass.

quduri.f: What is the penalty for killing prey in the Haram?
quduri.b: He must give the value as Sadaqah to the poor. Fasting will not suffice.

quduri.f: What is the penalty oof two men out of Ihram who kill prey in the Haram?
quduri.b: Each is liable for a complete penalty.

quduri.f: If a Muhrim kills a prey in the Haram is there a multiple penalty upon him?
quduri.b:
No, the one penalty is incorporated into the other and the Sadaqah of the value of one prey will suffice.120

120 Whilst logic dictates that there be two penalties, the summary from al-Kifayah is that based on the juristic principle of Istihsan the prohibition of the Ihram is greater because it forbids hunting in the Hill and the Haram. Thus the greater prohibition already incorporated the lesser prohibition of hunting in the Haram.

quduri.f: What is the penalty of cutting or uprooting trees and grass of the Haram, whether by a Muhrim or non-Muhrim?
quduri.b: It is Wajib to give the value of the tree in Sadaqah if the tree does not have an owner and is not the kind people plant.

quduri.f: And if someone owns it? [i.e. a plant/tree in the Haram]
quduri.b: The destroyer will have to pay its value in Sadaqah as the right of Shari'ah; and also the same price to its owner as his right. That is if it is not dry. If dry, then he only need to pay the owner and there is no further Shar'i penalty.

quduri.f: Are there any exceptions? [i.e. regarding trees and grass of the Haram]
quduri.b: Yes, it is allowed to cut Izkhir, a famous grass. Dry trees and grass can also be cut.

quduri.f: Are these the rules [i.e. regarding cutting or uprooting trees and grass of the Haram] for Muhrims or non-Muhrims?
quduri.b: It applies to both. The cutting of trees and grass is prohibited due to the Haram, not the Ihram.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of two Muhrims cutting a tree on which there is a penalty?
quduri.b: The price of one is due on both.

quduri.f: Can one make Miswak from the trees of the Haram?
quduri.b: No, unless it is a dry tree.

quduri.f: What should a Muhrim do in the case of Ihsar?
quduri.b: If a Muhrim falls ill or an enemy prevents him from continuing, he is allowed to terminate his Ihram.

quduri.f: How does he do that? [i.e. a Muhrim terminating his Ihram due to sickness or danger]
quduri.b: If he is in the Haram then he should slaughter a sheep and shave or clip his hair. If he has not reached the Haram, then he should depute a man with a sheep or its price who will slaughter the sheep on his behalf in the Haram. They would stipulate an exact time when the sheep will be slaughtered. When it is slaughtered he will be out of Ihram.

quduri.f: What should he do if he is Qarin? [i.e. a Muhrim terminating Ihram]
quduri.b: He will pay two Damm if he is in the Haram. If not, he will send the two sheep to be slaughtered on his behalf after which he is released from both Ihram.

quduri.f: Why must the sheep be sent to the Haram? Can he not slaughter wherever he is?
quduri.b: The slaughter is the Damm of Ihsar. It is not permissible except in the Haram.

quduri.f: Can the Damm of Ihsar be made before the Day of Nahr?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى, yes. His two companions say that the slaughter for Ihsar of Hajj can only be done on the Day of Nahr.

quduri.f: What can one intending 'Umrah slaughter whne he has been prevented?
quduri.b: He may slaughter when he wants but it must be in the Haram. This is unanimous.

quduri.f: After the prevented one [Muhsar] from Hajj has been released from Ihram does any other obligation remain?
quduri.b: Yes, he must make Qada of a Hajj and an 'Umrah. As for the Muhsar of 'Umrah he must make Qada of 'Umrah only.

quduri.f: If a Qarin has been prevented, what must he do after release from Ihram?
quduri.b: A Hajj and 2 'Umrah.

quduri.f: A Muhrim was prevented from Hajj. He sent someone to slaughter on his behalf, and then the prevention terminated. What should he do?
quduri.b: If he can afford a Hady and Hajj, then he is not allowed to leave the Ihram. He must continue the rites of Hajj. If he cannot afford the Hajj but can only afford the Hady then he may leave the Ihram. If he can only afford the Hajj and not the Hady then he may leave the Ihram but it will be better if he fulfils the Hajj.

quduri.f: A man entered Ihram and reached Makkah. He was prevented from Wuquf at 'Arafat and Tawafuz Ziyarah. Is he classified as Muhsar?
quduri.b: Yes he is.

quduri.f: Is the Muhsar prevented from either Wuquf of 'Arafat or Tawafuz Ziyarah?
quduri.b: The laws of Ihsar do not apply to him. If he is prevented from Tawafuz Ziyarah he will do his Wuqf and then do the Tawafuz Ziyarah when the Ihsar has ended. If he cannot do the Wuquf then he is like one who has missed the Hajj and must do as anyone else who has missed it.

quduri.f: When the Hady is slaughtered, is it sufficient for his release from Ihram or must he first shave or clip his hair?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he is released from Ihram upon the slaughter. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى he must shave or clip to be released.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a Muhrim of Hajj who missed Wuquf of 'Arafat until dawn of the Day of Nahr?
quduri.b: His Hajj has been missed. He should remove his Ihram after doing the rites of 'Umrah i.e. he will make Tawaf, Sa'y and shave or clip his hair.

quduri.f: Is there anything after that? [i.e. for the Muhrim of Hajj who missed Wuquf of 'Arafat until dawn of the Day of Nahr and after removing his Ihram has to do the rites of 'Umrah]
quduri.b: Yes, he must make Qada of the missed Hajj the next year.

quduri.f: Is there Damm? [i.e. for the Muhrim of Hajj who missed Wuquf of 'Arafat until dawn of the Day of Nahr and after removing his Ihram has to do the rites of 'Umrah]
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Is there such a thing as a missed 'Umrah?
quduri.b: No, because 'Umrah is not specified to a particular time. As we mentioned before, it is permissible throughout the year and Makruh for 5 days.

quduri.f: What is Hady?
quduri.b: It is the animal slaughtered in Hajj and 'Umrah. Either the Muhsir slaughters it for release from Ihram, or the Mutamatti' or the Qarin slaughters it out of gratitude to Allaah for allowing the Hajj and 'Umrah to be joined. It is also slaughtered as compensation for violating the Ihram or omitting a Wajib of Hajj or 'Umrah. It may also be voluntarily slaughtered.

quduri.f: What animal is the Hady?
quduri.b: It can only be camel, cattle or goat/sheep, no other animal. Male and female is allowed.

quduri.f: Can any of the three categories [i.e. of Hady] be slaughtered as one wanted, or are there restrictions?
quduri.b: Yes, there are two conditions. The animal must be Thani or above; and must be free of defects.

quduri.f: What is a Thani?
quduri.b: A Thani is a goat which has completed a year and is in its second year; or a calf which has completed 2 years and is in its third year; or a camel which has completed 5 years and is in its sixth year.

quduri.f: Is less than a Thani sheep allowed?
quduri.b: Yes, a Jaza' or a sheep which has completed six months is allowed which is mixed with other Thani will seem to an onlooker like it is a Thani.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of free of defect?
quduri.b: That all the organs be intact. Thus a Hady with a cut hoof, leg, ear or tail is not vali;d nor one which has lost an eye; nor an insane animal; nor a cripple which cannot walk to the place of slaughter.

quduri.f: Can an animal which has only a part of an ear or tail cut off be used as a Hady?
quduri.b: If most of the ear or tail is cut off then it is not a valid Hady.

quduri.f: Can one slaughter the Hady wherever one wishes?
quduri.b: The slaughter is not valid anywhere besides the Haram.

quduri.f: In what circumstances are camels and cattle specified for slaughter?
quduri.b: A complete camel or cow must be slaughtered as compensation for making Tawafuz Ziyarah as a Junub and not repeating the Tawafuz Ziyarah. It is also the compensation for one who had sex after Wuquf at 'Arafat but before shaving and before Tawafuz Ziyarah. In these two scenarios only a cow or camel will suffice. In all other cases a sheep will suffice, be it for Damm of Ihsar, Damm of Tamattu', Damm of Qiran, Damm of violations; or simply voluntary Hady.

quduri.f: Can more than one person share in the slaughter of certain Hady?
quduri.b: Yes, up to 7 people can share in a camel or cow on condition that all 7 intend it as a worship.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of 7 people sharing in a Hady and one of them has only made intention of the meat?
quduri.b: The Hady is not valid for any of them.

quduri.f: Can the meat of Hady be eaten?
quduri.b: The owner of the Hady can eat form voluntary Hady, Tamattu' and Qiran. It is not allowed for him from Damm of Ihsar and Damm of violations.

quduri.f: Is there a specified time for slaughtering Hady?
quduri.b: It is not permissible to slaughter Hady of Tamattu' and Qiran before the Day of Nahr. It must be slaughtered on the Day of Nahr or the two days thereafter. He may not delay the slaughter of the Hady after the 12th of Zil Hijjah. He may not slaughter before pelting the Biggest Jamrah on the Day of Nahr. It is allowed to slaughter for Damm of Ihsar and violations at any time.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of delaying the Hady of Tamattu' or Qiran after the Days of Nahr?
quduri.b:
In addition to the delayed Hady, he must slaughter another Hady for the delay.121

121 If in additon he shaved before slaughter, then he will owe a third Hady as well for incorrect order.

quduri.f: Is it Wajib to give the meat of the Hady as Sadaqah to the poor of the Haram?
quduri.b: No, it is not specified for the poor of the Haram. It is permissible to give the Sadaqah to those poor or others.

quduri.f: Is it Wajib to take the Hady to 'Arafat?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the difference between Zabh [slaughter across the throat] and Nahr [spearing the throat]?
quduri.b: The Sunnah for camels is Nahr and for cattle and sheep it is Zabh. If done in the opposite it is permissible but Makruh.

quduri.f: Is it Wajib to slaughter or make Nahr oneself?
quduri.b: No, someone else can do it. It is however better to do it oneself if one is capable.

quduri.f: A man was brining a camel and then was forced to ride it, may he do so?
quduri.b: He may ride it only if forced to.

quduri.f: May he use the milk of the sheep or camel he is bringing for slaughter?
quduri.b: He may not milk them. He should moisten the udders with cold water to stop the milk.

quduri.f: If the Hady perishes on the way, what should he do?
quduri.b: If it was voluntary then he need not replace it. If it was Wajib then he must slaughter a substitute.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if a defect afflicts the Hady which prevents its validity for slaughter?
quduri.b: If it is Wajib Hady then he must slaughter a substitute and may do with the defective one what he wants to. If it is a voluntary Hady then he should slaughter it despite the defect.

quduri.f: What should he do if he was bringing a Budanah and it was about to perish on the way?
quduri.b: If it was voluntary he should slaughter the camel and dip the sandals he hung around it in its blood. He should then place it on the hump as a sign that he left it for the poor. Neither he nor the wealthy may eat from it. If it was Wajib then he must substitute it and do with the original what he wishes.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of hanging around its neck?
quduri.b: It is Mustahab for the voluntary Hady and Tamattu' and Qiran. Damm of Ihsar and violations should not have anything hanged around.

quduri.f: What should he do with the blanket and rope of the Hady?
quduri.b: Give it away in Sadaqah.

quduri.f: Can the slaughterer be paid his fee from the meat?
quduri.b: No. It must be given from his own funds. [Muslim and al-Bukhari, narratinon of 'Ali رضي الله عنه]

quduri.f: What is Bay' [trade]?
quduri.b: An exchange of a commidity for a commidity with the happy consent of the transacting parties.

quduri.f: How is a transaction contracted?
quduri.b: It is contracted by offer and acceptance when both speak in the past tense, e.g. one says, "I have sold," and the other sayd, "I have bought."

quduri.f: When one party has made an offer, does it become binding on the other party?
quduri.b: No. When one offers, the other has a choice. He may accept it in the same Majlis [sitting, gathering] or reject it. Once the second party accepts it, it becomes binding. Neither then has a choice.

quduri.f: Why have you mentioned accepting in the gathering?
quduri.b: When an offer has been made and either moves from the gathering before the acceptance then the offer is void.

quduri.f: Once the transaction has been completed, does the buyer have any further options?
quduri.b: Yes, if a defect becomes apparent in the goods he bought he has a choice. He may return then or he may take them. The buyer has the same option of returning or accepting as long as he did not see the goods.

quduri.f: Is a transaction valid with deferred payment?
quduri.b: Transactions are valid with immediate payment and deferred payment if the period has been defined.

quduri.f: A man sold goods. He pointed at it and did not declare the quantity, weight or measure. Or two men bartered goods and did not declare the quantity, weight or measure but each pointed at his goods. Are these two transactions valid?
quduri.b: Both are valid. Pointing out the goods or price does not require further defining for the validity of the transaction. Pointing out something is the most exact form of defining something.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the price was undefined in terms of amount and type of currency?
quduri.b: If the buyer said for example, "I have bought from you for silver/gold/Dirham/Dinar/wheat," and did not specify the amount or type, then the transaction is not valid. For the validity of the transaction the amount must be mentioned, e.g. "I bought from you for X amount of Dirham." The description must also be mentioned, e.g. "Egyptian/Syrian; Pure/Alloyed."

quduri.f: If only the description of the price was given, e.g. he said, "I sell you this for 10 Dirham," and in the city there are several descriptions of money used, is the transaction valid if the buyer accepted?
quduri.b: Yes, the money will be defined as the one the people most commonly use in the city.

quduri.f: The Dirham was left undefined and there are different kinds in terms of monetary value. Will the transaction be valid?
quduri.b: The transaction is incorrect unless one was defined and the amount is known.

quduri.f: Is a sale of food and seeds in measure or amount valid?
quduri.b: It is permissible to sell it for Dirham/Dinar/currency/seeds. However, it is not allowed to sell a quantity of food for food of the same type because of the possibility of Riba [interest].

quduri.f: A man said, "I am selling you this wheat to the extent that it fills this container." The buyer accepts although he does not know the exact amount the container can hold. Is this valid?
quduri.b: The sale of the specified container is valid even if he does not know the exact amount it will contain.

quduri.f: If he buys equal to the weight of a specific stone, whose weight he does not know, what is the ruling?
quduri.b: That is also permissible.

quduri.f: A man bought a basket of food, each Qafiz [a dry measure] for a Dirham. Is the transaction valid?
quduri.b: The transaction is only valid for 1 Qafiz and invalid for the rest, unless the total Qafiz has been stipulated. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. His two companions say that it is valid in both cases, whether the total had been mentioned or not.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى if someone sold a flock of sheep and said, "A Dirham per sheep."?
quduri.b: The entire transaction is incorrect according to him. His two companions say that it is correct in all.

quduri.f: What did Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى say about selling cloth for a Dirham per arm span and the total length had not been mentioned?
quduri.b: The transaction is incorrect in total as well as per arm-span.

quduri.f: What do you say about someone who sold a basket of 100 Qafiz of food for 100 Dirham, the buyer then discovers that it is less then 100 Qafiz?
quduri.b: The buyer can either cancel the sale or pay the proportionate amount only.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he found it to be more than 100 Qafiz? [i.e. if someone sold a basket of 100 Qafiz of food]
quduri.b: The extra amount must be returned to the seller.

quduri.f: A man bought a 10 arm-span cloth for 10 Dirham; or he bought a 100 arm-span land for 100 Dirham. He then found the cloth or the land to be less than what the seller claimed. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The buyer can either take it at full price or cancel the sale.

quduri.f: If he finds it to be more then what the seller claimed? [i.e. a man buying a 10 arm-span cloth for 10 Dirham; or buying a 100 arm-span land for 100 Dirham]
quduri.b: The cloth or the land is for the buyer at the stipulated price. The seller has no choice.

quduri.f: What do you say if the seller had to say, "I am selling you this which is 100 arm-spans for 100 Dirhams, each arm-span for a Dirham," and the item turns out to be more than that or less?
quduri.b: The buyer has a choice if it is less. He can take the item at the proportionate price or he can cancel the sale. If it is more then his choice is to take the total at a price of a Dirham per arm-span or he can cancel the sale.

quduri.f: A seller says, "I am selling you this bundle of 10 cloths for 100 Dirham. Each cloth is 10 Dirham." What is the ruling if they are more or less than 10?
quduri.b: If it is less then the sale is valid at the proportionate price. If it is more then the sale is Fasid [invalid].

quduri.f: A man sold a house and did not mention anything else. What else is included in the term "House"?
quduri.b: When a house is sold, it includes the courtyard, the building, the keys and locks, even if they were not specifically mentioned.

quduri.f: What do you say about the sale of a land which has trees on it?
quduri.b: The trees are included in the sale, whether they were mentioned or not.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the land with crops was sold, but the crops were not mentioned?
quduri.b: The crops are not included in the sale of the land, unless otherwise stipulated.

quduri.f: Someone sold a date-tree or other fruit-tree. Who owns the fruit?
quduri.b: The seller keeps the fruit, unless the buyer had stipulated otherwise. The seller must cut off his fruit and hand the tree over to the buyer.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to buy unripe fruit which is still on the tree?
quduri.b: It is permissible to sell fruit which is on the tree - whether ripe or unripe - but the seller must immediately cut them off.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if a condition of leaving the fruit on the tree was made?
quduri.b: The sale is Fasid.

quduri.f: If the fruit was on the tree and was sold except for a specified Ritl [weight], what is the ruling?
quduri.b: The sale is Fasid.

quduri.f: Is the sale of wheath in its sheathe and beans in its pods permissible?
quduri.b: It is allowed if sold for something of a different type. If sold for the same thing then it is not permissible due to the possibility of Riba [usury].

quduri.f: Something was sold by weight or measured dimensions. It was so much that a measurer/scale had to be hired. Who bears the hiring fees?
quduri.b:
The seller.122

122 Just as if a professional counter had to be hired.

quduri.f: The buyer offered Dirham/Dinar. The seller needed other currency and had it changed. Who bears the exchange fee?
quduri.b:
The seller.123

123 The buyer according to the narration of Ibn Sima'ah from Muhammed.

quduri.f: The Dirham or Dinar were many and needed to be weighed. Who bears the fees of the weighing?
quduri.b: The buyer.

quduri.f: Is it Wajib to give the goods first, or is it Wajib upon the buyer to pay first?
quduri.b: If paid for with money then the buyer must pay first. If goods are exchanged for goods or one currency for another, then they should exchange it simultaneously.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of right of withdrawal [khiyarush Shart] for the buyer and the seller?
quduri.b: It is permissible for either party.

quduri.f: Is there a limitation to it? [i.e. to right of withdrawal (khiyarush Shart)]
quduri.b: Yes, three days or less. More than that is not allowed according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى more than that is allowed if the one with the right stipulates it and the other party agrees.

quduri.f: Two men conducted a sale. The seller maintained the right of withdrawal for himself. The buyer took the goods which were then destroyed in his possession within the period of the right. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: In the principle the right being maintained by the seller prevents ownership from leaving him. The buyer thus took the seller's goods. If it perished in his possession during the period of the right he must replace it with the same kind of good if it is a standard good, and with the price if it is not standard.

quduri.f: Does the ownership remain with the seller if the buyer maintains the right of withdrawal?
quduri.b: The buyer maintaining khiyarush Shart does not prevent the ownership from leaving the seller. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى ownership is not transferred to the buyer either in that case. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is.

quduri.f: The buyer assumed khiyarush Shart and took possession of the goods. It perishes in his hands. Who is liable in this case?
quduri.b: The buyer is now liable to pay the seller the agreed upon price.

quduri.f: The buyer has khiyarush Shart and has the goods. A defect develops. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: If the defect is irreverisble e.g. a slave loses his hands; then it is as a perished good. The buyer must pay the price they had agreed upon. If it is reversible then he maintains khiyarush Shart for the period. Once the period passes the buyer can no longer return the goods. He is now liable for the agreed upon price even if the defect remained.

quduri.f: What is the benefit of khiyarush Shart to the owner thereof?
quduri.b: He may either rescind the sale or confirm it within the period.

quduri.f: Is it necessary to rescind or confirm the sale in the presence of the other party?
quduri.b: Confirmation can take place in his absence, but rescinding must be done in his presence.

quduri.f: What can the buyer do if the seller sold him a slave claiming him to be a baker or scribe and he was not?
quduri.b: The buyer can keep him at the agreed price or he can cancel the sale and return the slave.

quduri.f: The party with khiyarush Shart died before confirming the sale and before the period elapsed. Do his heirs inherit the right?
quduri.b: The right is terminated and cannot pass to the heirs. The sale is regarded as complete.

quduri.f: A man bought goods he did not see. Is the sale valid?
quduri.b: The sale is valid. However, the buyer maintains the right to cancel the sale or accept the goods when he eventually does see it. He may also cancel before seeing it.

quduri.f: Is there a time limitation for this right? [i.e. when a man bought good he did not see]
quduri.b: No, it remains until there is any indication that the buyer is pleased with the goods.

quduri.f: What do you say about a seller who did not see his goods?
quduri.b: He has no right of sight.

quduri.f: The buyer saw the outside of a basket, the outside of a folded cloth, the face of a slave-girl or the face of an animal and took it. Is his right void?
quduri.b: This is deemed a sighting and he does not have a further right of sight.

quduri.f: Is it deemed a sighting if he saw the courtyard of a house and did not see the rooms?
quduri.b: According to the writers of the original texts this is a valid sighting and he does not have further rights. This is however based on the fact the houses in al-Kufah were all standard. Hence the Fatwa is on the view of Imaam Zufar رحمه الله تعالى that he must see the inside of the house, because rooms differ.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if a blind man buys or sells?
quduri.b: His transactions are valid and he maintains the right of sight when buying.

quduri.f: How can he see when he is blind? [i.e. with regards to a blind amn having the right of sight]
quduri.b: He will touch the goods when the goods are such that are recognised by touch. Similarly he will taste or smell the goods. These will substitute his seeing them.

quduri.f: A blind man wishes to buy land. How will he recognise it?
quduri.b: The land will be described to him as there is no other way for him to recognise it. Once it is described and he is happy with it, his right has terminated.

quduri.f: A man sold someone else's possession, without his authorisation. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The owner can either confirm or rescind the scale. He may confirm the sale as long as the four parts of the sale exist - the buyer, the seller, the possession and the owner. If the owner dies before confirmation of the sale is rescinded and the heirs cannot confirm it. When the sale is rescinded the buyer must seek restitution from the seller not the owner.

quduri.f: A man bought two robes in one sale. Can he return both if he then sees one?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man saw an item and bought it after some time has elapsed. Does his right of sight remain?
quduri.b: If the item remained as it was when he saw it he has no right. If he sees that it has changed then he has the right of sight.

quduri.f: A seller who had right of sight dies. What happens to his right?
quduri.b: The sale is confirmed and the right becomes void. It is not transferable to the heirs.

quduri.f: A man bought an item and then discovered a defect which existed when in the hands of the seller. Can he return it?
quduri.b: If the buyer did not see the defect at the time of purchase, nor at the time he took possesion, nor did the seller tell him of it; then he has a choice. He may accept it at the full price agreed or he may return it.

quduri.f: Can the buyer not keep it and reduce the price as per the defect?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is deemed a defect in these Masail?
quduri.b: Whatever will necessitate a reduction in price in the practice of traders is deemed a defect.

quduri.f: Give some examples of defects which permit a return of the goods by the buyer.
quduri.b: A slave who runs away or urinates in the bed. A child who steals is defective, once he attains puberty it is no longer a valid defect. A slave girl who sweats and stinks. That is not a defect for a slave unless due to an illness. Fornication and being illegitimate are defects in slave-girls not slaves.

quduri.f: A defect occurred in the possession of the buyer then he learns of a defect which already existed in the hands of the seller. What can he do?
quduri.b: He may seek a reduction for the defect in the good, but he may not return it to the seller unless the seller is willing to accept the new defect.

quduri.f: A man bought a cloth and cut it, stitched it or dyed it. Or he bought cereal and mixed it in butter. He then discovered a defect which existed in the hands of the seller. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He may seek a reduction for the defect in the good, but he may not return it to the seller unless the seller is willing to accept it as it is.

quduri.f: What do you say about a man who bought a slave and freed him or the slave died, he then learns of a defect that was in the hands of the seller?
quduri.b: He may receive a reduction for the defect, but may not return it because there is nothing to validly return.

quduri.f: If the buyer killed the slave or he bought food and ate it.
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى he does not receive anything. According to his two companions he will receive a reduction for the defect.

quduri.f: A man sold a slave and then the buyer resold it. The second buyer returned him to the first buyer because of a defect. May he return the slave to the first seller?
quduri.b: If the second seller i.e. the first buyer is forced by a court ruling to take the slaveback then he may return him to the first seller. If he accepted the slave without a court ruling then he may not.

quduri.f: A man bought a slave. The seller said, "I am absolved of all defects." The buyer then finds a defect. Can he return the defective good?
quduri.b:
He may not, even though the seller did not list all the possible defects.

NOTE: Cheating and hiding defects are Haram. Muslim narrates from Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه that Rasulullaah ﷺ passed by a basket filled with food. He entered his hand in it and his fingers emerged wet. He said, "What is this, O owner of the food?" "It rained on it, O Rasulullaah ﷺ," he said. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Why did you not place it on top of the food so that people can see it? He who deceives is not of us."

Ibn Majah narrates from Wathilah bin Asqa': I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "He who sells a defective product and does not expose the defect is eternally under the anger of Allaah."

quduri.f: Explain the types of transactions in terms of correctness.
quduri.b:
There are four kinds of transactions:
Sahih or valid: That which the Shari'ah recognises in its origin and in its description as correct. The transaction is in effect in itself if there are not any other prohibiting factors.
Batil or void: The Shari'ah does not recognise it in its origin. Under no circumstances can the transaction be in effect.
Fasid or incorrect: The Shari'ah recognises it in its origin, but not its description. It can take effect if the buyer takes possession of the goods. The Fuqaha have granted leeway for this category and sometimes apply the term Fasid for Batil.
Mawquf or suspended: such as when someone sells someone else's property. The transaction is suspended until the real owner validates it or voids it.

quduri.f: Explain Batil transactions concisely.
quduri.b: If one or both of the goods/price is Haram or not owned then the transaction is Batil.

quduri.f: Give some examples [i.e. of Batil transactions].
quduri.b:
The sale of something non-existent or that which has no monetary value is Batil such as blood and carrion [except fish and locust]; camel sperm, camel foetus, fruits which haven't grown yet, an animal which was slaughtered and Bismillaah deliberately omitted, carrion hide before tanning, a slaughtered sheep joined with a sheep which died naturally, human hair [out of respect it is void], pig hair [due to its filth], human excreta for as long as it is not consumed by earth, selling that which the owner does not have in his ownership yet unless by means of Salam,126 fish which has not yet been caught, birds in the air, milk still in the udder, pearls still in the oyset, wool still on the sheep, wine, pigs, a slave joined with a free man just as selling the grass on a pasturage is void.127 

126 Will be defined in a later chapter inshaAllaah.
127 In view of the Hadith declaring it in the common property of the people. Similarly it cannot be rented in that that will destroy a public possession. Most Mashaikh have however given permission when a man plants and waters it himself.

quduri.f: If the master sells his Ummul Walad [slave girl who gave birth to the master's child], or Mudabbar or Mukatab is the transaction valid?
quduri.b:
All these transactions are void.128

128 Selling the Ummul Walad is like selling a free person because Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Her child has set her free."
An aspect of freedom is created in the Mudabbar in the future death of the master. The sale of the general Mudabbar is void, not the sale of the conditional Mudabbar. The general Mudabbar is the one to whom the master, "You are free after my death." The conditional Mudabbar is the one whom the master says to, "If I die on this journey/of this sickness then you are free."
A Mukatab is also entitled to freedom. If however he is pleased with being sold then it is allowed.

quduri.f: A man lays a net/trap and says to another that whatever is caught is for the buyer at a given price. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: It is void. The prey was not in his possession at the time of the transaction.

quduri.f: What do you say about a man who combined in a single sale a slave and a Mudabbar or his slave and someone else's slave?
quduri.b: The transaction is valid for his slave for a proportionate price. It is not valid for the Mudabbar and the other's slave.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a Batil transaction?
quduri.b: The transaction is not contracted and the buyer does not assume ownership when he takes the goods.

quduri.f: Give some examples of Fasid [incorrect] transactions.
quduri.b: Muzabanah - selling dates on the tree in exchange for plucked dry dates; or grapes on the vine in exchange for raisins. Mulamasah - the sale is in effect by mere touching without right of sight e.g. it was dark or the cloth was folded. There is also no right to withdraw within the gathering. Munabazah is that each throws his goods at the other and the sale is made. These were transactions which were regarded as correct before Islaam. Throwing a stone on a group of items. Whichever one it falls on is sold. Similarly selling an animal or slave-girl and excluding its foetus is Fasid. Selling an arms-span of a robe where it will cause damage to the whole big price as well for as selling a beam of a roof is incorrect. Or buying a [unspecified] robe out of two robes.

quduri.f: Does setting preconditions make the transaction Fasid?
quduri.b:
Yes, it is Fasid unless the condition is such which is needed for the transaction to reasonably take effect; it is suitable and there is a benefit for one party or the goods, or it is a condition he is entitled to, or it is known in the custom of the people, and if the Shari'ah has not forbidden these conditions.129

129 Thus conditions like the seller will keep the goods until the buyer pays do not make the transaction Fasid or condition established by Shari'ah like Khiyarush Shart. Or conditions well known in that society e.g. the seller will keep the fruits of a sold tree.

quduri.f: Give some examples which make the transaction Fasid.
quduri.b: If someone sold a slave on condition that he will set the slave free or make him Mudabbar or Mukatab; or the seller will use his services for a month; or he sells a slave-girl on condition that the buyer will seek to impregnate her; or a house on condition that the seller will inhabit it for a set time; or that he will not give the goods until the end of the month; or that the buyer will loan him a Dirham; that he must give him a gift. These conditions make the transaction Fasid.

quduri.f: What do you say about a man buying a cloth on condition that the seller cuts it and makes it into a shirt; or a sandal on condition that the seller puts in laces/straps.
quduri.b: The transaction is Fasid.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the seller sets a condition that he will defer payment to the Persian feast of Nawruz or Mahrajan, or the fast of the Christians or the end of the fast of the Jews; and the seller accepts the condition?
quduri.b: It is Fasid unless both parties know when these dates will be.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to set the time of payment until the harvest, or the milling of the wheat, or the plucking of the fruits, or the return of the Hajjaj?
quduri.b: The transaction is Fasid.

quduri.f: They agreed to the above times [i.e. until the time of harvest, or the milling of the wheat, or the plucking of the fruits, or the return of the Hajjaj] then agreed to drop that condition before that time arrived. Is the transaction correct?
quduri.b: Yes, it has now become correct.

quduri.f: Is the sale of dogs, cheetahs and beasts of prey permissible?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of selling silkworms and bees?
quduri.b:
The silkworm can only be sold with the silk.131 The bee can only be sold with its hive.

131 According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى the silkworm is a vermin and may not be sold at all. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it can be sold by the way when it shows that it is producing silk. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى upon whose view the Fatwa is, the silkworm can be sold under any circumstance since it has benefit.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a Fasid transaction?
quduri.b: If they had entered into the Fasid transaction in which there is an exchange of goods having a monetary value, and the buyer takes the goods with the consent of the seller, the buyer becomes the owner and is liable to pay the seller. However, it is Wajib upon both of them to cancel the transaction in obedience to Shari'ah.

quduri.f: They did not cancel the Fasid transaction. In fact, the buyer sold the goods to a third party. Does the new sale take effect?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: The buyer made a profit in selling the goods as above [i.e. after a Fasid transaction the buyer sold the goods to a third party]. What is the status of the profit?
quduri.b:
The profit is not wholesome. He should give it away in charity.132

132 The first seller however need not give away his profits.

quduri.f: What is the ruling on auctions?
quduri.b: There is no harm in it. Rasulullaah ﷺ auctioned a bowl and a blanket. [Abu Dawud, narrated by Anas رضي الله عنه]

quduri.f: Is the seller obligated to sell his goods at the last offered price in an auction?
quduri.b: No, he can choose.

quduri.f: Do Kuffar living under Muslim rule have to observe Islaamic financial regulations in terms of validity and incorrectness of transactions?
quduri.b: They are bound just like Muslims, except in wine and pigs. Their transaction with wine is just like a Muslim's transaction with juice. Their transaction with a pig is like a Muslim's transaction with a sheep.

quduri.f: Allaah says, "O you who believe, when the call is made for the Salah of the Day of Jumu'ah hasten to Allaah's remembrance and leave trade."
quduri.b:
Thus trade from the Azan of Jumu'ah until the end of the Salah is prohibited. Rasulullaah ﷺ has also forbidden Najash [to increase a bid and raise the price for others without intending to buy it oneself]; offering a higher price after the seller had already accepted the buyer's offer; and a city person going out and buying the crops of the farmers as they come to the city; and city-folk taking the goods of farmers and selling it for themselves.

NOTE: If someone owns two child slaves who are blood relations of each other, then he may not separate them in a sale by selling each to different masters. If one is a child and the other an adult it would be Makruh to separate them but the sale would be valid. If they are both adults then there is no harm in separating them.133

133 Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who separates a mother from her child, Allaah will separate him from his loved ones on the Day of Qiyamah."
Rasulullaah ﷺ gave 'Ali رضي الله عنه a gift of two small brothers. He ﷺ asked, "What has happened to the brothers?" He said, "One is sold." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Join them. Join them."
This applies to relatives who cannot marry each other. Thus relatives who can marry or those who cannot marry but are not blood relatives are not included in this rule. Thus a cousin who is also a foster-brother would be included in the rule.

quduri.f: What is Iqalah? What is its status in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: It is the rescinding of a transaction after the buyer and seller had already completed it. It can only be rescinded with the consent of both parties and for return of the original price.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if one of the two stipulates more or less than the original price [i.e. in the case of Iqalah]?
quduri.b: The condition is void. The goods will be returned at the original price.

quduri.f: Is Iqalah a cancellation of sale or a new sale?
quduri.b:
It is a cancellation with regards the original parties and a new transaction with regards the rights of third parties. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى.134

134 e.g. A man had a right to buy a property first. He allowed it to be sold to someone else. The sale was then rescinded. The man again has a claim on the "new" sale.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Iqalah when the product or the price perishes?
quduri.b: The perishing of the price does not prevent Iqalah, the perishing of the product does.

quduri.f: Some of the goods sold perished. Can the sale be rescinded in the remaining goods?
quduri.b:
Yes.

NOTE: To accept the request of the other party regretting the sale is Mustahab and entails great reward.135

135 Shurayh رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who agrees to cancel the sale of his brother, Allaah will cancel his sins on the Day of Qiyamah." [at-Tabrani in al-Awsat].

quduri.f: What is Murabah and Tawliyah in the terminology of the Fuqaha?
quduri.b:
Murabah is to mention what was required at the higher price with a profit.

Tawliyah is to mention what was acquired at the acquired price without a profit.

quduri.f: Are there conditions for the validity of Murabahah and Tawliyah?
quduri.b: Yes, the items must be such which have similar replacements e.g. they are products sold by volume or weight.

quduri.f: A man bought a cloth for example. He washed it, dyed it and embroided it. The price hence increased. Or he bought food and paid a porter to carry it. Or put a silk border on the cloth he bought. What is the method of Murabahah here?
quduri.b: Murabahah is allowed, but he may not say, "I bought it for so much," he must say, "This has cost me so much."

quduri.f: A man bought an item on Murabahah, and then discovered that the seller lied to him. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى he may either accept it at the total price or return it.

quduri.f: What can he do if he was cheated in Tawliyah?
