It is permissible at market rates or less, not more. This condition is also only when the slave is indebted. If the owner hands the item over before payment, the price is void.182

182 Because if the item is handed over before taking the price then it becomes a debt against the slave, and debts to the owner are not established against a slave. Once the price is void it is as if the owner sold without a price. The sale is thus not valid. What is meant by the price being void is that the owner cannot demand it from the slave and will instead take the goods back from him. [Al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: If the owner retains the goods until the slave pays?
quduri.b: That is permissible.

quduri.f: Can the owner declare the slave to be incapacitated?
quduri.b:
Yes, the slave will become incapacitated, on condition that the owner announces his incapacitation in the market.183

183 Because they believed that they could transact with him. That belief will not be rectified without knowledge. It is a condition that most of the people of the market are informed. [al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: Is there another way the Mazun slave can be incapacitated?
quduri.b:
Yes, if the owner dies, becomes insane or enters the land of the Kuffar as an apostate then the slave becomes incapacitated.184 When a Mazun slave runs away he becomes incapacitated. When a Mazun slave-girl gives birth to her owner's child she becomes incapacitated.1

184 If the slave becomes completely insane he becomes incapacitated, as when he enters the land of the Kuffar as an apostate. According to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he becomes incapacitated as soon as he abandons Islam. According to the other two Imams when he enters the lands of the Kuffar.

quduri.f: What is the status of the confession of a Mazun slave to debts, usurpations and amanat when he has been incapacitated?
quduri.b: The confession is valid for whatever he holds according to Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. According to the other two Imams his confession is invalid.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a guardian giving a child permission to trade?
quduri.b: The permission is valid. Once he has been given permission then his buying and selling is the same as a Mazun slave's. His transactions will take effect if he understands buying and selling.

quduri.f: What is Waqf?
quduri.b:
Literally it means to keep back. In Shari'ah it is to keep an item in the status of ownership of the Waqif [one making the endownment] whilst giving the benefit in charity.185

185 Which is according to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to the other two Imams, it is keeping an item in the status of the ownership of Allah. "Ownership of the Waqif" according to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى means before a court decision, because after a judge rules then the ownership is removed from the Waqif according to him as well.

quduri.f: Why has Waqf been given recognition in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: In order that people in need186 may utilise its benefit whilst the substance remains intact. Also, so that the substance can remain as Sadaqah Jariyah [perpetual charity] for the Waqif. Rasulullah ﷺ said, "When a human dies his deeds end except for three - perpetual charity, or knowledge through which people benefit, or pious offspring who pray for him." [Muslim]

quduri.f: When is the ownership of the Waqif over the endowment terminated?
quduri.b:
According to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it does not terminate unless the judge rules thus; or he attaches it to his death and says, "When I die then I make my house Waqf for ..." According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it terminates with his mere utterance. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it does not terminate until he appoints a trustee for the Waqf and hands it over to him, because it is the right of Allah.187

187 According to Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is not finalised until the judge rules that it moves out of his ownership by way of a bequest. According to the other two it is finalised without that. The general 'Ulama agree with that and that is correct. According to Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is finalised by his mere utterance because it is the same as setting a slave free. The Fatwa is upon this. [Raddul Muhtar]

quduri.f: Does the Waqf become the property of the Mawquf 'alayhi [one for whom the endowment has been made] after it leaves the property of the Waqif?
quduri.b: Once the Waqf is validated as per the differences we have mentioned, it leaves the property of the Waqif but does not become part of the property of the Mawquf 'alayhi.

quduri.f: Is there any condition for the correctness of the Waqf according to our three Imams?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the Waqf is not complete until it is made for a party which does not ever end.188 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى if he mentioned a beneficiary which comes to an end then it is correct. It will then pass onto the poor even if he did not mention it.

188 Whereby he says, "I make this a charity Waqf forever for the sake of Allah for the descendants of so-and-so as long as the line continues. If the line ends, then it is for the poor," because there will always be poor.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of jointly owned Waqf?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is permissible. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is not permissible.189

189 This difference is on that which can be divided. As for that which cannot be divided then joint Waqf is allowed according to Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى as well. There is no joint Waqf in Masajid and graveyards according to Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى as well.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Waqf of land?
quduri.b: It is permissible.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Waqf of items which can be moved and transported?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is not permissible. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى if a land is given as Waqf with its cattle and labourers who are slaves, then it is permissible. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى transport and weapons can me made Waqf in the way of Allah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of selling, making an owner and dividing a Waqf?
quduri.b: It may not be sold or an owner made over it. Joint Waqf can be divided if the partner so requests. This is according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى who recognises joint Waqf.

quduri.f: When does the ownership of the Waqif terminate over the land if he built a Masjid on it?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it does not terminate until he detaches it from his property by way of the path and allows people to pray in it. Thus when even one person has prayed in it, his ownership is terminated. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it terminates with his saying, "I have made this a Masjid."

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a water-source [e.g. well], hostel for travellers, hospice or graveyard?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى these remain his property until the court rules otherwise. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى his ownership terminates when he says he made these Waqf. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى when he gives people water from his water-source; or when the people start living in the hostel and hospice; or they bury the dead in the graveyard; then his ownership is terminated.

quduri.f: What must the trustee do with the income of the Waqf?
quduri.b: It is Wajib for him to first spend in on the maintenance of the Waqf, whether the Waqif stipulated it or not.

quduri.f: If a man made a house Waqf for living, who will repair and maintain it?
quduri.b: Whoever lives there will repair and maintain it. If he refuses or is poor, then the judge will rent it out and use the rent to repair it. Once it is repaired he will return it to the one who has the right of living there.

quduri.f: If a Waqf house is destroyed can the rubble be shared amongst those entitled to the Waqf?
quduri.b: The judge will use the rubble to restore the Waqf if he needs it. If he does not, he will leave the rubble until it is needed. It is not permissible to share it amongst those entitled to the Waqf.

quduri.f: A man declared a Waqf but stipulated the benefits/the trusteeship for himself. What is the ruling?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is permissible. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is not.191

191 As for the first [keeping the benefits] as-Sadr ash-Shahid said that the Fatwa is on the view of Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى in order to encourage people to establish Waqf.

quduri.f: What should someone do who finds an abanonded boy or a girl?
quduri.b: He should take the child lest it perish and should protect it. It is called Laqit because it has been picked up.

quduri.f: When the one who has discovered the child picks it up, who should bear its expenses?
quduri.b: He will spend money from the Baytul Mal [public treasury] on it.

quduri.f: A man finds a child. Can another man take the child from him?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: If someone claims that the child is his [i.e. the foundling], will his word be accepted?
quduri.b: Yes, his word will be accepted under oath.

quduri.f: What if two men both claim that the child is theirs?
quduri.b: If one of them can describe some feature on the child's body then it is his. If none can, then it is for both unless one of them claimed the child first, in which case he will get the child.

quduri.f: A child was found in a city or town of the Muslims. A Zimmi claims the child. Will the child's lineage be attributed to the Zimmi?
quduri.b: Yes, but the child will be classified as a Muslim because he was found in the realms of Islam.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the child was found in a town of Zimmis; or a place of worship of the Christians or Jews?
quduri.b: It is a Zimmi in this case.

quduri.f: A man claims that the child is his slave. Will his word be accepted?
quduri.b: No, the child will be free.

quduri.f: A slave claims that the child is his, will his word be accepted?
quduri.b: His word will be accepted but the child will be deemed free.

quduri.f: Money was found tied to the child. To whom will it belong?
quduri.b: It will belong to the child because it was in his hands. He is most entitled to own it.

quduri.f: A man found a child. He later wishes to get the child married or to transact in its wealth. May he do so?
quduri.b: He may neither get the child married nor may he transact with its wealth. He does however have trusteeship to spend from its wealth and buy necessities from it such as food and clothing.

quduri.f: If someone gives a gift to the child, who must take possession of it?
quduri.b: The one who found the child.

quduri.f: Can the one who found him send him to learn a craft or hire out his services?
quduri.b:
Yes.192

192 That is according to al-Quduri. Al-Jami'as-Saghir states that it is Makruh to hire out the child and that is more correct.

quduri.f: What is a Luqtah?
quduri.b: It is wealth flung in some place. It is called Luqtah [picked up] because one who sees it rushes to pick it up.

quduri.f: If someone sees it [i.e. wealth flung in some place] can he pick it up?
quduri.b: If he fears that it will be destroyed it is Wajib to pick up. If not, then it is not Wajib, but permissible. If he picks it up he should make someone witness that he has picked it up to safeguard it for its owner and will return it to him.

quduri.f: Once he picks it up [i.e. wealth flung in some place] what should he do?
quduri.b: If it is less than 10 Dirham then he should announce it for a few days. If it is at least 10 Dirham then he should announce it for a longer period up to a year. If the owner claims it, well and good, otherwise he should give it in charity.

quduri.f: What happens if the owner claims it after he gave it away?
quduri.b: The owner can validate the charity or he can make the donor liable.

quduri.f: Can a lost sheep, cow or camel be collected like this?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man picked up a lost animal. Who is liable for the expenses he incurred to maintain the animal?
quduri.b:
If he spends on it without the permission of the court, then he has given freely from his side. Nobody is indebted to him. If he did it with the court's permission then that is a debt against the owner.193

193 It is also said that he should announce until he is satisfied that the owner will not be claiming it. It is appropriate that he announce it at the place he found it and at the Jami' Masjid. If it is something one knows that the owner will not look for, such as date pits, one need not announce it and may use it. However, ownership remains with the owner.

quduri.f: If the finder spends so much on a found animal that his expenses equal the value of the animal, what should he do?
quduri.b: He should present his case before the judge. If the animal has some benefit the judge will hire it out and spend the rental on the animal's maintenace. If it has no benefit and fears that the maintenance costs will cover the value of the animal then he will sell it and safeguard the price. The better option is to order the maintenace of the animal and the costs will be a debt against the owner.

quduri.f: A man spent on the animal with the court's permission. The owner comes to claim it. Can the finder refuse to return the animal until the owner reimburses his costs?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man found a lost item. Someone comes and claims that he is the owner. Will he be given it based on his mere claim?
quduri.b: No, he must produce evidence.

quduri.f: The claimant cannot produce any evidence but gives a description of the item. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The finder is allowed to give it to him. However, the court cannot force him to do so.

quduri.f: The finder announced the found item for days/a year. He gave up on finding the owner and intended giving it away in charity. To whom can he give it?
quduri.b: He may give it to the poor, not the rich.

quduri.f: Can he not take it for himself? [i.e. the finder after announcing the found item for days/a year and after he gave up on finding the owner]
quduri.b: He cannot if he is rich. He may if he is poor.

quduri.f: The finder wished to give it to someone else because he was rich. He gave it to his father/mother/adult son/wife who were poor. Is that permissible?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Is there a difference with an item found in the Hill or the Haram?
quduri.b: No, the ruling is the same.

quduri.f: What is the legal status of a baby born with a penis and vagina i.e. a Khuntha [hermaphrodite]?
quduri.b: If it urinates from the penis, it is a boy. If it urinates from the vagina it is a girl.

quduri.f: And if it urinates from both organs?
quduri.b: It will be attributed to whichever organ it urinates from first. If the urine comes out of both at the same time then it will be attributed to whichever organ more frequent urine comes. This is according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى frequency of urine is not considered.

quduri.f: Are there other signs by which sex can be determined?
quduri.b: If the hermaphrodite attains pubert and grows a beard or is inclinded to women then it is a man. If it grew breasts like a woman/milk merged from its teats/it menstruated/it became pregnant/it allowed sexual penetration into its vagina, then it is a woman.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if none of these signs emerge? [i.e. growing beard, inclination to women, growing breasts, milk emerging from its teats, menstruation, pregnancy or sexual penetration into the vagina]
quduri.b: It will neither be classified as male or female but will be called Khuntha Mushkil [Undetermined Hermaphrodite].

quduri.f: In which row will the Khunta Muskhil stand for Salah?
quduri.b:
He will stand between the men and women, behind the children.194

194 Rulings regarding it will be according to caution. If he prays with the men then due to the possibility that it is a woman, the men on its right, left and behind should repeat their Salah. If it prays with the women then it should repeat its Salah because it might be a man. Hence it will stand between the men and women. It should cover whatever a woman must cover in Salah because of the possibility that it is a woman.
It will be Makruh for its entire life to wear jewellery or silk; to expose itself before men or women; to be alone with a non-Mahram of either sex. If it enters Ihram while not yet pubescent then according to Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى, "I do not know about its attire, because if it is male then it is Makruh to wear stitched clothing. If it is female then it is Makruh to leave the stitched clothing." According to Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى, "it should wear the clothing of women, because if it is female and leaves the stitched clothing it is more shameful than if it s a male and it wears female clothing. There is no fine on it because it is not an adult."

quduri.f: What does the Khuntha Mushkil inherit from its father?
quduri.b:
According to Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it inherits the share of a female. Thus if the deceased left behind a son and the Khunta Mushkil, the son will inherit two-thirds and the Khuntha Mushkil one-third, unless it is established otherwise.195 

According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the Khuntha Mushkil will get half a male's share plus half a female's share. This is the view of ash-Sha'bi رحمه الله تعالى.

195 This is an indication that the Khunta Mushkil sometimes inherits as a male, e.g. a woman dies and leaves behind her parents, husband and Khunta Mushkil child. The estate is divided into 12 shares. The husband gets 3; the parents get 4; the Khunta Mushkil gets 5. Had it been a daughter she would have gotten 6 and the total shares reclassified as 13. Another scenario is that a woman dies and leaves behind her husband, a maternal-brother; and a Khunta Mushkil who is her full sibling. The estate will be divided into 6 shares. The husband gets 3 shares; the brother gets 1 share and the Khunta Mushkil gets the remainder of 2. Had the Khunta Muskil been a sister she would have gotten 3 shares.

quduri.f: Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى adopted the view of ash-Sha'bi [i.e. regarding the inheritance of the Khuntha Mushkil]. Is there a difference in the interpretation?
quduri.b: Yes, according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the money will be divided into 7 between a son and a Khunta Mushkil. The son gets 4 shares and the Khuntha Muskil 3. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the money will be divided into 12 shares between them. The son will get 7 and the Khunta Mushkil 5.

quduri.f: Who circumcises a Khunta Mushkil?
quduri.b: A slave-girl will be bought for him from his money; or if he does not have money the ruler will buy her from him from the public treasury. After she circumcises him, the ruler will sell her and return the price to the treasury.

quduri.f: What is Nikah in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: It is a contract deliberately aimed at owning the right to Mut'ah [enjoyment]. Ownership of Mut'ah refers to a man's right with a woman to sex, touching and kissing.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated "deliberately"? [i.e. "a contract deliberately aimed at owning the right to Mut'ah]
quduri.b: Because ownership of Mut'ah is sometimes attained automatically such as when buying or inheriting a slave-girl.

quduri.f: How is marriage contracted?
quduri.b: It is contracted by offer and acceptance, with words in the past tense; or at least one in the past tense and one in the future tense. An example of the first is where the guardian says, "Zawwajtuha Iyya - I have married her to you," and the groom replies, "Qabiltuha - I have accepted her." An example of the second is where the groom says, "Marry her to me," and the guardian says, "I have given her to you in marriage." Whilst the groom used the command tense it is interpreted as future tense here.

quduri.f: With which words is the marriage contracted?
quduri.b: With Nikah and Tazawwuj [to marry], also from the side of the guardian if he uses Inkah/Tazwij [grant in marriage]; Tamlik [grant ownership]; Hibah [gift]; and Sadaqah on condition that accepted is uttered thereafter.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the guardian says, "I have hired her to you/I have lent her to you/I have made her permissible to you"?
quduri.b: Thse words do not establish marriage.

quduri.f: Are there other conditions besides offer and acceptance?
quduri.b: Yes, it is a condition that there be two witnesses present. They must be free, sane, Muslim adults; or a man and two women with the same qualities mentioned. It is necessary that the witnesses hear the offer and acceptance. The marriage is not valid if the witnesses are deaf or sleeping. It is valid with blind witnesses who listened.

quduri.f: The offer was made with witnesses who are not adil [just]. Is the marriage valid?
quduri.b: Yes, it is not a condition for the validity of the marriage contract that the witnesses be adil.

quduri.f: Is the marriage contract valid if the witnesses are men who were punished with the Hudd for slander?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A Muslim married a lady-Zimmi. Two Zimmis were the witnesses. Is the marriage valid?
quduri.b: It is valid according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى. The contract is not in effort according to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى who stipulates Muslim witnesses in this case.

quduri.f: Can a man or woman in Ihram marry?
quduri.b: They may marry but not engage in sex and its incitements.

quduri.f: Does the Shari'ah set a limit for the amount of wives one may marry?
quduri.b: Yes, a free man can have a maximum of four free or slave women as his wives at a given moment. If he divorces any and her 'iddah is complete or any die, then he may marry another. A slave however cannot have more than two wives at a time. A woman cannot marry a man besides the man in whose marriage she is, until he divorces her or dies and she completes her 'iddah. This is because it is Haram for a woman to be married to two men at the same time.

quduri.f: What is the status of a marriage if the man married two women in a single ceremony but one of them was not permissible for him to marry?
quduri.b: The marriage with the woman he was permitted to marry is valid and the other is void. The entire Mahr [dowry] will go to the one whose marriage is valid.

quduri.f: A man gives another his sister or daughter in marriage on condition that he in turn gives his sister or daughter in exchange. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: Both marriages are valid. The dowry of each will be Mahr Mithl [average dowry for that family, status etc]

quduri.f: A man got another man or woman married without permission. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The marriage is suspended until the person who had not been asked either validates ir or repudiates it. This is called Nikah al-Faduli in the terminology of the jurists.

quduri.f: What is the status of Muwqattat1 and Mut'ah2 marriages?
quduri.b:
Both are void.

1 Marriage with a time limit, e.g. the marriage was performed with witnesses and stipulated to last 10 days.
2 He says to a woman, "I shall enjoy you for such an amount of time for such amount of money."

quduri.f: How should a man who has several wives treat them?
quduri.b: He must treat them well. THis includes being just in his time amongst them.

quduri.f: What form does this justice take? [i.e. being just in his time amongst several wives]
quduri.b: He should share his nights with each. Thus if he spends one night for example with one, he must spend a night with the next one.

quduri.f: Is it Wajib upon him to have sex with his wife when he spends her turn with her?
quduri.b: The sharing is Wajib in as far as spending the night is concerned, not with regards to sex. Sex requires energy which might not be available every night.

quduri.f: Is there a difference in Qasm [i.e. sharing time between wives] between a virgin and a non-virgin; between and old and new wife?
quduri.b: No, he must be ewual whether any is a virgin, non-virgin, old wife or new.

quduri.f: How does he share if one wife is a free-woman and the other a slave?
quduri.b: He will spend two nights with the free wife for every one he spends with the slave.

quduri.f: What is the regulation of Qasm during a journey?
quduri.b: The wives do not have a right to Qasm when the husband is travelling. He may take whom he wishes with him. It would be best if he drew lots and took whomever's name emerged, so that their hearts will be pleased.

quduri.f: One wife was happy to give her Qasm to another wife. Is this allowed?
quduri.b: Yes, but she can claim her right back whenever she wishes.

quduri.f: Which women are Haram to marry?
quduri.b: There are several categories of Haram - women forbidden by lineage [nasabiyah]; women forbidden by Rada' [fosterage i.e. by the drinking of a particular woman's milk]; Musaharah [in-laws]; Jam' [uniting certain women together in one's marriage]; women upon whom there are rights of others; and women of Kufr and Shirk.

quduri.f: Explain the women forbidden by lineage.
quduri.b: They are mothers, daughters, sisters, sisters of one's father, sisters of one's mother, daughters of one's brother, daughters of one's sister - all these have been explicitly mentioned in the Quraan in Suratun Nisa. Mothers include a man's actual mother, as well as his grandmothers from both his father's and mother's side and thus going back and forbidding all female ancestors. Similarly daughters include a man's biological daughter, the daughters of his sons and daughter and thus all female descendants. Sisters include full sisters as well as half-sisters from either the mother's or father's side. In this way, daughter of a brother includes daughters of full-brothers, and daughters of half-brothers from either the mother's or father's side. Deduce the same for nieces from one's three kind of sisters. In the same way a paternal aunt is Haram whether she is one's father's full sister or half sister with a common father or half-sister with a common mother. Deduce the same for a maternal aunt in all three cases.

quduri.f: Which women are forbidden through Rada?
quduri.b: It is Haram for a man to marry his mother who suckled him; the foster-sister i.e. the girl who drank from that mother; and hence all those who are forbidden through lineage are forbidden through fosterage. There are exceptions which we shall explain in the chapter on Rada' Inshaallaah.

quduri.f: Which women are forbidden by Musaharah?
quduri.b: A man may not marry a woman his father had married, whether intercourse occurred or not. Similarly he may not marry the women of his grandfathers, whether paternal or maternal, or the wives of any ancestor further up. He may not marry his son's wife, his grandson's wife or the wife of any descendant further down- whether these said descendants had intercourse with these women or not. A man may not marry the mother of his wife, whether they had intercourse or not. He may not marry his wife's daughter, whether the daughter was in his care or not.

quduri.f: Which women cannot be married at the same time [Jam']?
quduri.b:
One may not join blood relatives in marriage at the same time. Thus one may not marry two sisters at the same time as explicitly stated in the Quraan.

Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ forbade marrying a woman when married to her paternal aunt; a paternal aunt when married to her brother's daughter; a woman when married to her maternal aunt; a maternal aunt when married to her sister's daughter. Do not marry the small one when married to the big one. Do not marry the big one when married to the small one. [Abu Dawud and at-Tirmizi]

From this the jurists have derived a general rule. If either one of the two women has to be regarded as a man, and marriage between them would not be allowed (whether by lineage or fosterage) then marrying both at the same time is also forbidden.

quduri.f: Which women cannot be married because of Kufr and Shirk?
quduri.b:
If a man is outside the pale of Islaam then a Muslim lady may not marry him, whatever religion he may belong to. A Muslim man may not marry a polytheist, an idol-worshipper, a fire-worshipper or any other kind of Kafir3 unless she is a Christian or Jew.4 

3 A man may also not have sex with a polytheist or fire-worshipper slave. A Kafir is anyone who denies the necessary beliefs of Islam. This includes the Qadianis, the Batiniyah, the Shi'ah and the Ithna 'Ashariyah who claim the Quran is corrupted. SOme Muslims have been deceived by their claims of Islam and have married their daughters despite them being Kafirs.
4 Although marriage to a female Christian or Jew is permissible, 'Umar رضي الله عنه forbade it.

quduri.f: Can the prohibition through Musaharah arise through Zina as well?
quduri.b: Yes, thus if a man commits Zina with a woman or touches her with lust or she touches him with lust, then it is Haram for him to marry her mother or daughter.

quduri.f: Can a man marry at the same time a woman and her ex-husband's daughter from another woman?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man divorces a woman. Can he marry her sister?
quduri.b:
If he has divorced her Batt5 or Raj'i then he may not marry the sister until her 'iddah is complete.

5 Includes Mughallazh and Bain.

quduri.f: A man owns two slaves who are sisters. Can he have sex with them by right of ownership?
quduri.b: He may not have sex with both of them, but may choose whichever one of the two he wishes to enjoy. Once he has used the first, he may not have sex with the second until he prohibits the first unto himself.

quduri.f: How will he prohibit her unto himself? [i.e. a man used to have sex with a slave]
quduri.b: He will marry her to another man; or make her a Mukatab; or remove her from his possession by freeing her; or gifting her away; or selling her; or giving her as charity.

quduri.f: Who is the Wali [guardian]?
quduri.b:
Guardianship of marriage arises from four sources: Qarabah [relationship]; Wala [setting a slave free]; Imamah [government]; and Milk [ownership].

As from the aspect of relationship, paternal relatives ['asabat] are the guardians in the same order as in inheritance. The closes then the closest has preference. The closest guardian to a woman is her son; then her son's son and proceeding down. Then the father; then the father's father and proceeding up. Then a full brother; then a half-brother with a common father. Then a son of a full-brother; then a son of a half-brother with a common father. Then a son of a full-brother; then a son of a half-brother with a common father and then proceeding down. Then a paternal uncle who is a full brother of her father. Then a paternal uncle who is a half-brother sharing a father with her father. Then a son of a paternal uncle who is a full brother of her father. Then a son of a paternal uncle who is a half-brother sharing a father with her father. Then proceeding downwards. Then a paternal uncle of her father who is a full brother of her father's father. Then a paternal uncle of her father who is a half-brother sharing a father with her father's father. Then their descendants in this order.

Then from the aspect of Wala which refers to the rights the master retains when freeing a slave; if a woman does not have a guardian from paternal relatives then the owner who freed her from slavery is the guardian. He is counted as the last of paternal relatives. If there are no paternal relatives then her maternal relatives will be her guardians, whether she is a child or adult.

If there are no such relatives at all then the guardianship falls on the Imamah or government, referring to the ruler or judge.

Guardianship of Milk refers to the right of the slave's owner (whether the slave is male or female) to get them married, even if they are displeased. If the male or female slave marries without the owner's permission then the marriage is suspended pending the owner's ratifying it or rejecting it.

quduri.f: What is the status of a free adult woman's marriage if she willingly married without the guardian contracting it?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the marriage is valid as long as she is a sane adult. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the marriage is not validated without the guardian's permission.

quduri.f: Can a guardian force a sane, adult virgin to marry?
quduri.b: No. She has a greater right to herself whether she is a virgin or not.

quduri.f: We accept that she cannot be forced. [i.e. a sane adult virgin] However, women generally do not get married themselves, but their guardians get them married. Must the guardian ask her permission?
quduri.b: Since he cannot force her he has to ask her permission, "I wish to marry you to that person." If she agrees then the marriage will be valid or else if she refuses it is not.

quduri.f: A virgin is shy to respond verbally. How can she give her consent?
quduri.b: If the guardian asks her and she remains silent or laughs or cries without any sound then that counts as consent. If someone besides the guardian asks her or a guardian besides whom there is a more entitled guardian then her consent must be expressed verbally.

quduri.f: If she refuses, what can the guardian do? [i.e. the sane adult girl]
quduri.b: He cannot marry her when she refuses.

quduri.f: A woman married and became a widow. Must her guardian ask her permission if he wishes to get her married a second time?
quduri.b:
It is necessary for him to ask her and it is also necessary for her to give verbal consent. Her silence, laugh or cry will not suffice as consent.6

6 The Nabi ﷺ said, "Do not get a widow married until her order has ben asked. Do not get a virgin married until her consent has been asked." They asked, "Ya Rasulullaah ﷺ! How is her consent?" He replied, "If she keeps quiet." [al-Bukhari and Muslim]

quduri.f: A woman never got married, but her physical virginity was broken by jumping, menses, a wound, or through length period of not marrying. Is she legally a virgin or not?
quduri.b: She is likely a virgin. Her silence and the like will suffice as her consent.

quduri.f: A woman did not marry and terminated her virginity through fornication. What is her status in this mas-alah?
quduri.b: She is legally a virgin according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. Hence her silence will suffice. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى she is not a virgin.

quduri.f: A man got his adult virgin daughter married. Her new husband says, "When the proposal reached you, you remained silent." She replies, "I did not keep quiet. I rejected it." What is their status?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى her word will be accepted and she need not take an oath. This is amongst those Masail wherin no oath is demanded according to him but is demanded according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى.

quduri.f: A guardian got a child, male or female, married without asking permission. Is this marriage valid?
quduri.b:
Yes it is valid. The guardian need not ask them permission, and this is what is meant by the guardian forcing them. This rule is general for the girl, whether she is a virgin or not.7

7 The meaning of her not being a virgin is that her guardian got her married before and her husband died before she attained puberty.

quduri.f: A closest guardian is absent and a need arose to get them married. Can the further guardian get the married?
quduri.b: If the close guardian is firmly absent then the far guardian can get them married.

quduri.f: What is a firm absence? [i.e. with regards to the closest guardian being firmly absent]
quduri.b: To be in a place where caravans pass only once a year or once in a while.

quduri.f: An insane woman has two guardians - her father and her son. Who is her guardian in marriage?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is her son. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is her father.

quduri.f: The guardians got children married in their childhood. Do the boy and the girl have a right to cancel the marriage when they attain puberty?
quduri.b: If a father or grandfather got them married then they have no choice. If someone else got them married then each of them may decide whether to continue the marriage or to cancel it.

quduri.f: Can non-male relatives such as sisters, mothers and mothers' sisters get a small boy or girl married?
quduri.b:
Yes.8

8 Meaning that when there are no relatives from the male side.

quduri.f: A father got his small daughter married and halved the Mahr Mithl, or the father of a small boy got him married and increased on the Mahr Mithl. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The father and grandfather may do that, nobody else may.

quduri.f: Are there any other conditions for guardianship besides Qarabah and the others already mentioned?
quduri.b: Yes, the guardian must be a sane adult. A child or madman does not have guardianship.

quduri.f: What is the status of the guardianship of a Kafir?
quduri.b: A Kafir cannot have guardianship over a male or female Muslim, even if he is the closest person to him/her.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that a guardian cannot force a woman to marry. If an adult woman marries and reduces her dowry to less than Mahr Mithl, can the guardian object to what she has chosen for herself?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the guardians have a right to object to her reduction until her Mahr Mithl is completed or her husband leaves her.

quduri.f: A woman's guardian is her paternal uncle's son. He marries her to himself. Is this permissible?
quduri.b: It is and the marriage is valid if there were witnesses present.

quduri.f: An adult woman authorised a man to marry her to himself. They got married in the presence of witnesses. Is the marriage valid?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: What is Kaf and Kafaah?
quduri.b: Kafaah is equality or peerage. Kaf is someone who is one's equal or peer. Kafa in marriage is based on lineage, Din, wealth and occupation.

quduri.f: What is peerage in Din?
quduri.b: It is matching in religious observance i.e. Taqwa and piety. A Fasiq [open sinner] is not a peer for a pious Muslimah.

quduri.f: How is peerage in wealth established?
quduri.b: If the husband can pay her dowry and living expenses then they are peers in wealth.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of peerage in occupation?
quduri.b: It means that the husband should not be of such occupations which are looked down at such as cupping, tanning, sweeping etc.

quduri.f: A woman married a non-peer. Her guardians object. What is the status of their objection?
quduri.b:
They are entitled to object and may separate the couple.9

9 To remove embarrasment from themselves [al-Hidayah]. It is necessary that a judge be brought to separate them [al-Jawharah].

quduri.f: Can a woman marry her slave; and can a man marry his slave-girl?
quduri.b: Neither of them may do that. However, a man may benefit from his slave-girl in the same was as he benefits from his wife if the slave-girl is a Muslim, Christian or Jew. He may not have intercourse with a fire- or idol-worshipper. Another condition is that he may not have sex with two sisters as we had explained before.

quduri.f: Can a Muslim man marry the slave-girl of another man?
quduri.b: Yes, if she is a Muslim, Christian or Jew.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of marrying a slave-girl when already married to a free woman; and marrying a free woman when already married to a slave-girl?
quduri.b: The first is not permissible; the second is.

quduri.f: A man got his slave-girl married and then freed her. Does she have a right concerning maintaining the marriage?
quduri.b: She has a choice, irrespective whether her husband is free or a slave.

quduri.f: A slave-girl married without her owner's permission. She was then set free. What is the status of her marriage?
quduri.b: The marriage is valid and she has no choice.

quduri.f: A man got his slave-girl married. Must he send her to live in her husband's house?
quduri.b: He is not obligated to. She must still serve him. Her husband may have intercourse with her when they find an opportunity.

quduri.f: If he keeps her at his house [i.e. a man who got his slave-girl married], who must pay her living expenses?
quduri.b: It is the duty of her husband.

quduri.f: The owner let her [i.e. a man who got his slave-girl married] stay in her husband's house. He then felt a need to use her services. Can he do that?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A slave married with his owner's permission. Who must pay the dowry?
quduri.b: If the owner does not give it then it is a debt against the slave who will be sold to pay it.

quduri.f: What is Mahr?
quduri.b:
The money which is Wajib upon the husband upon contracting the marriage in exchange for the benefits of the private part, whether by specification or by the contract itself.10 

10 Synonyms for Mahr include Sadaq, Nihlah and Faridah.

quduri.f: What are the minimum and maximum amounts of Mahr?
quduri.b: The minimum is 10 Dirham. If less than 10 was stipulated then she must still receive 10. There is no maximum. Whatever they willingly agreed upon becomes Wajib upon him to pay.

quduri.f: If a Mahr was not named, and the offer and acceptance took place in the presence of witnesses, is the marriage valid?
quduri.b: The marriage is valid and she must be given Mahr Mithl if he has sex with her or dies after the marriage. If he divorces her before sex or Khalwah Sahihah [complete seclusion] then she is entitled to Mu'ah which we shall define later InshaAllaah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he marries her on condition that she will not receive any dowry?
quduri.b: The ruling will be the same as one who did not mention her dowry in terms of Mahr Mithl or Mut'ah as we had just mentioned.

quduri.f: A Mahr was stipulated and then he divorced her. Is the entire amount Wajib?
quduri.b: If he had sex; or died with her in his marriage even without sex; then she is entitled to the entire amount. If he divorced her without sex or Khalwah Sahihah then she is entitled to half. Allaah says, "If you divroce them before touching them and you had stipulated an amount then it is half that amount."

quduri.f: A Muslim woman accepted wine and pig as dowry. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The marriage is valid and she is entitled to Mahr Mithl.

quduri.f: A woman got married for a stipulated Mahr. He then increases on it or she reduces it. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: Both scenarios are allowed. However, his increase becomes obligatory if he has sex with her or dies with her in his marriage; while the increase is forfeit if he divorces her before sex.

quduri.f: A man marries a woman for 1000 Dirham and on condition that he will not take her out of the city, nor marry another woman while they are married. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: If he fulfils the condition then she gets the stipulated amount. If he takes her out of the city or marries another woman then she is entitled to Mahr Mithl.

quduri.f: He marries her for an unspecified animal.11 Is that correct?
quduri.b:
The stipulation is valid. She is entitled to a medium quality animal. The husband may choose to give her the animal or to pay her its price.

11 What is meant here is that the type of animal such as horse or donkey was given, but no further description. If even that was not mentioned then he must pay Mahr Mithl.

quduri.f: He married her for an unspecified cloth. What must he pay?
quduri.b:
Mahr Mithl.12

12 Because there are different types of cloths. If however he specified, e.g. Hirawi, then it is valid.

quduri.f: They married and no Mahr was stipulated. Thereafter they both agree on a Mahr. What is she entitled to?
quduri.b: She is entitled to what they agreed upon if he has sex with her or dies while she is in his marriage. If he divorces her before sex or complete seclusion, then she is entitled to Mut'ah.

quduri.f: A man marries a free woman in exchange for serving her for a year or teaching her the Quraan. Is this valid?
quduri.b: The stipulation is invalid. She is entitled to Mahr Mithl.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if a slave marries a free woman with his owner's permission in exchange for serving her for a year?
quduri.b: The marriage is valid and she is entitled to a year's service from him.

quduri.f: The guardian takes liability for the woman's dowry. Is this valid?
quduri.b: Yes, she may demand her dowry from the guardian or her husband.

quduri.f: The marriage was Fasid and the court separated the couple. What is the status of giving the dowry?
quduri.b: She is not entitled to any Mahr if they were separated before sex; even if there was complete seclusion. If they did have sex then he will pay her Mahr Mithl but not more than the Mahr they had agreed upon.

quduri.f: What is the status of her 'iddah after such a separation [i.e. the marriage was Fasid and the court separated the couple], and attribution of lineage if she gives birth to his child?
quduri.b: She will fulfil the iddah of divorce and the child will be attributed to him.

quduri.f: The Majbub [amputated penis] was alone with the woman and then divorced her. What Mahr does he owe her?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he must pay the full Mahr because she had surrendered herself to him. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى she is entitled to half Mahr.

quduri.f: What is Khalwah Sahihah?
quduri.b: That there be no obstacle to sex, e.g. none of them is sick, fasting Ramadan, being in Ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah, nor is the woman in menses.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated that the fast be that of Ramadan?
quduri.b: If a man is alone with his wife whilst either one is keeping a voluntary fast then it is deemed Khalwah Sahihah.

quduri.f: You have mentioned Mahrul Mithl over and over again in your answers. What is it?
quduri.b: Dowry similar to the dowries of her sisters, paternal aunts and daughters of paternal uncles if these women are similar to her in age, beauty, wealth, intelligence, piety, city and time. Her mother and maternal aunts are not considered if they are not of the same tribe as her.

quduri.f: What is Mut'ah?
quduri.b:
It is three pieces of clothing of her worth13, Dir' [loose outer garment with sleeves], Khimar [head covering] and Milhafah [wrap].

13 This would seem to mean that the clothing be according to her status, whereas it is according to his, because Allaah says, "Upon the wealthy his ability and upon the straitened his ability."

quduri.f: For which divorcees is Mut'ah Wajib and for which is it only recommended?
quduri.b: It is Wajib for a woman who's husband divorced her without having sex with her and they did not stipulate what her Mahr is. It is Mustahab for every other divorcee except for woman whose husband divorced her without having sex with her but did mention a specific Mahr.

quduri.f: A man married a woman who has a defect. Can he cancel the marriage?
quduri.b: He may not. He may however divorce her at any time.

quduri.f: If a woman marries a man and she then discovers him to be mad or a leper, can she claim Faskh (termination)?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى she may not. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى she may.

quduri.f: A woman discovered her husband to be impotent. She requested the judge to terminate the marriage. What should he rule?
quduri.b: The judge will summon the husband and give him a year's respite to undergo treatment. If he has intercourse with her in that period she has no further option. Otherwise the judge will separate them if she so requests [after the year of unsuccesful treatment].

quduri.f: What is the status of the separation if the judge separates them? [i.e. a woman discovered her husband to be impotent and requested the judge to terminate the marriage]
quduri.b: It is deemed Talaq Bain.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Mahr in this case? [i.e. a woman discovered her husband to be imported and requested the judge to terminate the marriage]
quduri.b: Full Mahr if he was secluded with her.

quduri.f: What will the judge rule if she finds her husband Majbub [amputated penish] and demands that he separate them?
quduri.b: He will immediately separate them because there is no hope that the husband will be able to have sex for the rest of his life.

quduri.f: And if she finds him castrated and demands a separation?
quduri.b: He will be given a year's respite just as for an impotent man.

quduri.f: A woman embraces Islaam. Her husband is a Kafir. Will she be separated from him because of her Islaam?
quduri.b: She will not be separated solely because of her Islaam. The judge will offer Islaam to him. If he accepts then she remains his wife. If he refuses, then the judge will separate them. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the separation will be a Talaq Bain. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is a separation without divorce.

quduri.f: A man married to a fire-worshipper embraces Islaam. Will she be separated from him?
quduri.b: She will not be separated solely because of her Islaam. The judge will offer Islaam to her. If she accepts then she remains his wife. If she refuses, then the judge will separate them. This separation will not be a divorce because it arose from her refusal.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Mahr in that case? [i.e. a man married to a fire-worshipper embraces Islaam, she refuses to accept Islaam and the judge separates them]
quduri.b: If they had had intercourse then she is entitled to full Mahr, otherwise none.

quduri.f: The husband of a Christian/Jew embraces Islaam. Will they be separated?
quduri.b: There is no need for separation. If a Muslim man can initiate a marriage with a Christian/Jewish woman then he can also maintain his marriage with her.

quduri.f: A woman in the land of the Kuffar is married to a Kafir. She embraces Islaam. Are they separated?
quduri.b: She will not be separated from him until she completes three menstrual periods. When she finishes the third, then they are separated.

quduri.f: A husband/wife left the hands of the Kuffar for the lands of the Muslims, as a Muslim. When are they separated?
quduri.b: His/her leaving for the lands of Islaam separates them in itself. There is no additional factor required.

quduri.f: A woman embraces Islaam in the lands of the Kuffar and makes Hijrah to the lands of Islaam. Her husband is there. Must she spent an 'iddah?
quduri.b: No, she may marry immediately according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى if she is not pregnant. If she is pregnant then she may not marry until she gives birth.

quduri.f: One of the spouses apostatises from Islaam - Allaah protect us. When does the separation occur?
quduri.b: They are separated immediately without divorce.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Mahr in that case? [i.e. when one of the spouses apostatises from Islaam]
quduri.b: If it is the husband who is the apostate and they had sex, then he owes her the full Mahr. If they did not, then he owes her half Mahr. If the wife is the apostate then she is still entitled to full Mahr if she apostatised after sex; if before then she is not entitled to Mahr.

quduri.f: A couple abandonded Islaam together - Allaah save us - and returned to Islaam together. What is the ruling on separating them?
quduri.b: They will not be separated and they remain married to each other.

quduri.f: If a man or a woman leaves Islaam whom can they marry?
quduri.b: A male apostate may not marry a female Muslim, or an aspostate, or a woman who was always a Kafir. Similarly a female apostate may not marry a Muslim, or an apostate, or a man who was always Kafir.

quduri.f: A Kafir husband or wife living in the lands of the Kuffar was captured and brought to the lands of Islaam. When will they be separated?
quduri.b: They are separated immediately upon entry into the lands of Islaam. If they are captured together then their marriage is not terminated.

quduri.f: Of his two parents, only a child's father is Muslim. Whose religion does the child follow?
quduri.b: He will follow his father. If any parent accepts Islaam and the child is small, then the child will be Muslim due to whichever parent's Islaam.

quduri.f: A child's one parent is a Christian/Jew and the other a Fire-worshipper. Which religion will he follow?
quduri.b:
He will follow the Christian/Jew on the principle of following the parent with the better religion.

NOTE: 
If a Kafir marries without witnesses or marries during the 'iddah period and then the couple embraces Islaam then their marriage is valid if those practices are valid in their religion. They are not required to perform a second marriage.
If a Fire-worshipper marries his mother or daughter and then they embrace Islaam, they will be separated.

quduri.f: What is the maximum allowed period for breastfeeding after which it is not allowed?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is 30 months. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is 2 years.

quduri.f: Which laws apply due to breastfeeding?
quduri.b:
If breastfeeding has taken place within the period as per the difference in opinion, be it a little or much, then marriage is Haram between two Radi', and between a Radi' and its Murdi'ah [wet-nurse], her ancestors, descendants and her relatives of the same line. Allaah has mentioned the prohibition of marrying one's wet-nurse and sisters through breastfeeding. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Allaah has forbidden through breastfeeding what He has forbidden through lineage."15

15 Narrated by Muslim.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if a woman breastfeeds a boy or a girl after the prescribed period?
quduri.b: Breastfeeding after the prescribed period is not permissible. If done it does not bring about the prohibition of marriage.

quduri.f: Explain the regulations of prohibition through breastfeeding in detail.
quduri.b:
Understand and remember the following Masail:
If a boy and a girl drank from the same woma, they may not marry each other.16 
A woman may not marry any descendant of the woman who breastfed her.
When a woman breastfeeds a girl, that girl is prohibited unto her husband, her ancestors and her descendants. The husband through whom the nurse got her milk will be the girl's father through breastfeeding. The jurists term this mas-alah Labanul Fahl [stallion's milk].
A boy may not marry the sister of the husband of the woman who breastfed him, because she is his paternal aunt through breastfeeding.
A man may not marry the wife of a boy who is his son through breastfeeding just as he cannot marry the wife of his biological son.
A man may marry the sister of his Radi' brother just as in certain scenarios one may marry one's brother's sister e.g. someone has a half-brother with a common father. He can marry the half-brother's half-sister who shares the same mother with the half-brother.
16 Nor may they marry her, her children, or grandchildren etc.

quduri.f: You mentioned that whoever is Haram to marry through lineage is Haram to marry through breastfeeding, with certain exceptions. What are these exceptions?
quduri.b:
The following are exceptions:
One may marry the mother of one's sister through breastfeeding, but not the mother of one's biological sister.
One may marry the sister of one's son through breastfeeding, but not through lineage.
One may marry the mother of the paternal uncle and paternal aunt through breastfeeding, but not through lineage.

quduri.f: The milk of two women was mixed and fed to a boy or girl. To which of the two will the prohibition of marriage be attributed?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it will apply to whichever one's milk was the most. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it applies to both.

quduri.f: If a virgin gets milk in her breast and she feeds a baby, what is the ruling?
quduri.b: The prohibition of marriage applies.

quduri.f: If a man should produce milk and he breastfeeds a boy or a girl, do the laws of marital prohibition apply?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A boy and a girl drank from the same sheep. Do the laws of marital prohibition apply?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man married an adult woman and a girl of breastfeeding age. The adult breast-fed the girl. What is the ruling of this breastfeeding?
quduri.b: Both wives become Haram for him.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Mahr in the above case? [i.e. a man married an adult woman and a girl of breastfeeding age, and the adult breast-fed the girl]
quduri.b: If he did not have sex with the adult then she is not entitled to Mahr and the girl receives half Mahr. He will claim the half Mahr from the adult if she had intended mischief. If she did not then she is not liable.

quduri.f: How is Rada' proven?
quduri.b: Through the Arsh (testification) of two men, or a man and two women. The Arsh of only women is not accepted.

quduri.f: A woman's milk was mixed with water. A boy or a girl drank the mixture. Do the laws of marital prohibition apply?
quduri.b: If it is motly milk they apply. If mostly water then they do not.

quduri.f: And if the woman's milk was mixed with food? [i.e. do the laws of marital prohibiton apply then?]
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى they do not apply even if the milk is dominant. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى they apply if the milk is dominant.

quduri.f: And if the woman's milk was mixed with medicine? [i.e. then do the laws of marital prohibition apply?]
quduri.b: The laws apply if the milk is dominant.

quduri.f: A woman died. Her milk was extracted and put in a vessel and fed to a baby. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The laws of prohibition apply.

quduri.f: A woman's milk was mixed with a sheep's milk. What is the ruling if a baby drinks it?
quduri.b: If the woman's milk is dominant then the laws of prohibition apply. They do not if the sheep's milk dominates.

quduri.f: If a man marries a woman and they are not compatible, what should they do?
quduri.b: Allaah commands, "Treat them [wives] with goodness." If it becomes impossible and he wishes to separate then Allaah has made a way out, which is for the man to divorce his wife. He will take her out of his marriage. The man is called Mutallig and the woman is called Taliq.

quduri.f: Are there different kinds of divorce?
quduri.b:
There are three kinds:
Ahsanut Talaq [the best divorce]
Talaqus Sunnah
Talaqul Bid'ah

The first means to divorce her once whilst she is in a state of purity in which the husband didn ot have sex with her. He then does not have sex with her until her 'iddah finishes.
The second is to divorce thrice the wife whom he had sex with. The three pronouncements will be in three purity periods without sex. The jurists also call this at-Talaq al-Hasan. The Sunnah in this divorce is from two aspects - time and number. The Sunnah of amount applies equally to a woman who had sex with her husband [Madkhul biha] and a woman who did not [Ghayr Madkhul biha]. The Sunnah of time is specific to the woman whom the husband had sex with. He should divorce her in a purity period in which they did not have intercourse.
The third kind is to pronounce three divorces in a single sentence; or to divorce her thrice during a single purity period. If a man pronounces a single divorce on his Madhkhul biha the divorce falls against her. However, she will not separate from him until the completion of her 'iddah. If he wishes to take her back he may do so during her 'iddah. If she is Ghayr Madkhul biha she will separate from him upon one divorce. In this case the husband may not take her back whether during or after the 'iddah. InshaAllaah we shall elaborate on this.

quduri.f: What is the status of Talaqul Bid'ah?
quduri.b: The divorce occurs even though the husband is a sinner for transgressing the Sunnah.

quduri.f: Does divorce occur when given during menses?
quduri.b: It occurs but is forbidden. He is obligated to take her back.17 If he then wishes he may divorce her in a purity period in which they did not have sex. This is if she is Madkhul biha. If she is Ghayr Madkhul biha he may divorce her during menses.

quduri.f: What is the status of divorcing her when she is pregnant?
quduri.b: It is permissible even if it is following intercourse.

quduri.f: A man intends divorcing a Madhkul biha thrice according to the Sunnah. How is it done?
quduri.b: He will pronounce the first divorce in a purity period in which they did not have sex. He will then pronounce the second divorce in the next purity period and the third in the third period.

quduri.f: He intends divorcing her according to the Sunnah, but she does not undergo menses. What should he do?
quduri.b: He should divorce her once in the month. When the month passes he should divorce her in the second month, and like that the third divorce in the third month.

quduri.f: Can one divorce one's wife who does not undergo menses whereby there is no gap of time between the divorce and having had sex with her?
quduri.b: It is permissible.

quduri.f: A man wishes to divorce his pregnant wife according to the Sunnah method. How will he separate the three divorces?
quduri.b: He will separate them in months according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he cannot divorce her according to Sunnah and must divorce her once only.

quduri.f: Does the divorce of every husband take effect?
quduri.b: The divorce of a husband falls if he is a sane adult. The divorce of a child, madman and sleeping man does not take effect.

quduri.f: What is the status of the divorce of a drunken man and one forced to give divorce?
quduri.b:
The divorce occurs.18

18 Referring to a drunk who still has his senses. However, if he has completely lost his senses then the divorce does not occur e.g. he cannot tell the difference between a man and a woman; the earth and the sky. Drink refers to consuming any intoxicant including honey wine, and drugs like opium etc.

quduri.f: What is the status of the divorce of a mute?
quduri.b: His divorce by indication occurs.

quduri.f: A slave marries a woman with the permission of his owner. Who can divorce her?
quduri.b: The slave has the right to divorce her. If the owner divorces her it does not fall.

quduri.f: How do Talaq Raj'i and Bain occur?
quduri.b:
There are two kinds of divorce with regards wording. Sarih [explicit] and Kinayah [indirect]. 

Explicit is when the husband says, "You are divorced/you are now a divorcee/I divorce you." This divorce is Raj'i and only one occurs even if he intended more than one. No attention is paid to whether he actually intended the divorce or not. Amongst those words deemed explicit are, "You are Talaq/You are a divorcee in divorce/You are a divorcee given a divorce". If he had no intention with these words then it is one Raj'i divorce. If he intented two, then it is still one. However, if he intended three then it is three. If he says, "You are divorced. You are divorced," then it is two Raj'i. Allaah says, "If divorce has been given twice retain her in kindness or leave her in an amicable manner."

The second kind, Kinayah, is when the words are not explicit. The divorce will not occur except with an intention or an indication of the condition.

quduri.f: Please explain further? [i.e. see answer to question 1572: how do Talaq Raj'i and Bain occur with regards to Kinayah, indirect divorce]
quduri.b:
There are two kinds of indirect words of which three words result in one Raj'i divorce when if he intended two or three. They are, "Go into 'Iddah/Clear your womb/You are now single." The rest of the indirect words result in one Bainah if he intends one or two, but if he intends three it will be three. These words include, "You are Bain, Battah and Batlah [separated, broken and cut off - because she is cut off from returning]/You have free rein/Go join your family/You are free/You are alone/I have gifted you back to your family/You choose/I have separated from you and you are free/Veil yourself from me/Cover yourself from me/Be a stranger to me/Seek another husband."

If he did not intend divorce then the divorce does not occur with these words. If however it was within the discussion of divorce then legally20 it is a divorce, but not between him and Allaah until he intends it as such.

If it was not in a dicussion of divorce but both were angry or arguing, then the divorce occurs with any indirect word which was not an insult or abuse. If the insult or abise was intended as divorce then the divorce occurs.

In Summary:
Raj'i divorce occurs with explicit words.

Related to this is when he says, "Go into 'Iddah/Clean your womb/You are single." Bain divorce is with indirect words when he intends thereby divorce or the condition indicates thus. The Talaq Raj'i becomes Bain if the 'iddah passes and he did not take her back in it. 

Mughallazh Divorce occurs with three pronouncements, whether it be in three purity periods, three months, in a single sentence, in three sentences in the same purity period, or he intended three divorces with indirect words - except that which are exception from it.

20 Meaning amongst humans. If he protests at a court that he did not mean it then his protest will not be accepted. This applies to words which can be given to the woman as reply to her request for divorce and not a refusal e.g. "Go into 'Iddah/The matter is in your hands, you choose."

quduri.f: What kind of divorce falls if the husband pronounced it with an additional description?
quduri.b:
It will be Bain. The woman will be separated from him and he may not take her back, e.g. "You are divorced Bain/You are divorced in the worst way/in the most shameful divorce/the divorce of the devil/Talaqul Bid'ah/You are divorced like a mountain/ a houseful of divorce."21

21 If he says to her you are divorced in the most intense way/a thousand times/a houseful of divorce", then that is one Bainah unless he intends three."

quduri.f: Does the divorce occur if he attributes the divorce to her body parts?
quduri.b:
The divorce occurs if he attributes it to her in her entirety or that which indicates her entirety, e.g. "You are divorced/your neck is divorced/your soul is divorced/your body is divorced/your physique is divorced/your vagina is divorced/your face is divorced."

Divorce does not occur with, "Your hand is divorced/your leg is divorced", because hands and legs do not symbolise the entirety.

quduri.f: If he instead mentions a fraction of her, e.g. half/a third of you is divorced?
quduri.b: The divorce occurs.

quduri.f: If he fractions the divorce instead e.g. "You are given a third/half/two-thirds divorce."
quduri.b: One complete divorce occurs because divorce cannot be fractioned.

quduri.f: A man says, "If I marry you then you are divorced." What is the status of this addition?
quduri.b: The divorce occurs immediately after the marriage.

quduri.f: If he adds a condition like, "If you enter the house you are divorced", what is the ruling?
quduri.b: The divorce will occur upon fulfilment of the condition whatever the condition is - except if he says, "You are divorced", and immediately adds, "if Allaah wills". Divorce does not occur with that condition.

quduri.f: If he says to a stranger, "If you enter the house you are divorced." He then marries her and she enters the house. Does the divorce fall?
quduri.b: No divorce takes place. It can only occur after the fulfilment of the condition if he "owned" the woman in terms of marriage rights at the time of making the oath or it is attributed to ownership.

quduri.f: What words are used in these conditions, what is the status of using them? [i.e. words used for words for a condition]
quduri.b: The words include in, iza, iza ma, mata and mata man [if/when]. If the divorce is attributed to one of these words, then the divorce takes place after the condition occurs. He is then released from the oath.

quduri.f: What do you mean by release from the oath?
quduri.b: The effect of the condition takes place only once. When it occurs the divorce occurs. Thereafter if the condition arises again there will not be another divorce from that oath and condition.

quduri.f: Are there such words whereby the divorce will recur if the condition recurs?
quduri.b:
Yes it recurs with kullama [every time/whenever].

A man says, "Every time you enter the house you are divorced." She enters the house and is divorced. She enters again and is divorced again. She enters again and is divorced again. Thereafter there is no divorce from this because there is no more than three divorce in Shari'ah.

quduri.f: She was divorced thrice because of the recurring condition as above. [i.e. a man says "Every time you enter the house you are divorced" and she entered the house thrice]. She marries another man and then remarries the first husband. If she again enters the house is she divorced?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: If he says, "Every woman I marry I divorce" will each woman be divorced whom he marries for the rest of his life?
quduri.b: Yes, his words encompass every woman.

quduri.f: He says to her, "If you enter the house you are divorced." He then divorces her with a normal pronouncement. After her 'Iddah he remarries her. She then enters the house. Does the divorce fall?
quduri.b: Yes, the loss of marriage does not fulfil the oath. It is fulfilled when the condition is found and she is divorced.

quduri.f: He attached a condition to divorce but divorced her normally before the condition could occur. She was separated from him and then the condition occurred. He then remarries her. Is she divorced?
quduri.b: No, the condition occurred outside of his ownership. He is released from the oath.

quduri.f: He made a divorce attached to a condition. The couple then dispute whether the condition is found. Whose word will be accepted?
quduri.b: His word will be accepted, unless she produces proof that the condition os found.

quduri.f: Certain matters are only known to the wife. If he made a condition of such matters then whose word is accepted, e.g. he says, "If you bleed your menstruation then you are divorced." How will the matter be resolved if they dispute the occurrence of the condition?
quduri.b: In such matters affecting the woman personally her word will be accepted.

quduri.f: What do you mean, "...affecting the woman personally"? [i.e. see the answer to question 1598 with regards to a man who said "If you bleed your menstruation then you are divorced" and then they dispute about the occurrence of the condition; in such matters affecting the woman personally her word will be accepted.]
quduri.b:
It will be clear to you from the following examples. He says to her, "If you menstruate then you and your co-wife are divorced." If she says, "I am menstruating", then she will be divorced and not the co-wife, unless the husband accepts her word.
If he says, "If you love me/are angry with me then you are divorced." She says, "I love you/I am angry with you." Her words will be proof against her even if they contradict what is in her heart. Her words will not be used against a third party however.22 

22 Such as if he said, "If you love me then you and your co-wife are divorced." If she says, "I love you" then she is divorced but not the co-wife.

quduri.f: If he says, "If you menstruate you are divorced/If you menstruate a menses period then you are divorced", what is the status of the conditions?
quduri.b:
They have two separate rulings:
When he says, "If you menstruate you are divorced", and she sees her menstrual blood, the divorce does not occur until she bleeds for three days and nights. Upon the completion of the three days and nights it will be ruled in retrospect that the divorce fell upon the bleeding. That is because bleeding for less than that is not menstruation, but is Istihadah. That is why she must wait for the minimum period of menses.

When he adds, "... a menses period ..." then she is not divorced until she enters her purity after her menses. The difference between the two lies in the additional words which stipulate a complete menstruation.

quduri.f: If he says, "You are divorced in Makkah", and she is not in Makkah, what is the ruling?
quduri.b: She is divorced immediately wherever she may be. Similarly she is divorced if he says, "You are divorced in the house", and she is not in the house. He did not make entry of Makkah or the house a condition for divorce.

quduri.f: If he says, "You are divorced if you enter Makkah", is that different from the above question?
quduri.b: Yes, here he makes entry into Makkah a condition, hence the divorce does not occur until she enters Makkah.

quduri.f: If he says, "You are divorced tomorrow", when does the divorce occur?
quduri.b: When true dawn rises.

quduri.f: If he says, "You are divorced thrice except one/thrice except two", what is the status of the exception?
quduri.b: The exception will be taken into consideration; hence two divorces occur in the first scenario and one divorce in the second scenario.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of divorce between consummation?
quduri.b: If a man pronounces divorce before consummation then the divorce occurs. If he pronounces three divorces in one sentence then all occur. If he pronounces them separately, she becomes Bain with the first pronouncement and the second and third do not fall on her. Divorce in the case of non-consummation will never be Raj'i. It will either be Bain or Mughallazh.

quduri.f: He says to her, "You are divorced one and one/ one before one/ one after it another one." How many divorces fall on her?
quduri.b: Only one falls in all these cases.

quduri.f: If he says, "You are divorced one after one/one with one/one with it one", how many fall in these cases?
quduri.b: Two divorces occur in all these cases.

quduri.f: He says, "if you enter the house you are divorced one and one." She enters the house. What is the ruling?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى one divorce occurs. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى two occur.

NOTE: That distinction is for a woman whose husband did not consummate the marriage. If it was consummated then two apply in all cases.

quduri.f: A man says to his wife, "Choose yourself", meaning divorce or he says, "Divorce yourself." Can she divorce herself?
quduri.b: She may divorce herself from him in these two cases as long as she remains in that gathering. If she leaves the gathering or begins doing some other deed then she loses the option, unless he said, "Divorce yourself whenever you want to." She may then divorce herself in the gathering or thereafter.

quduri.f: If he told her, "Choose yourself", and she does in the gathering, what is the ruling?
quduri.b: A single Bain divorce occurs. Her divorce will not be three, even if the husband intended that. For the divorce to occur, it is necessary that either he or she mention nafs [self].

quduri.f: If he told her, "Divorce yourself", and she did so, which divorce falls?
quduri.b: One Raj'i. If the husband intented three then three occurs. If he intended two then that is not correct unless his wife is a slave.

quduri.f: If he appoints an agent and says to him, "Go divorce my wife." Is the agency confined to the gathering?
quduri.b: No, he may divorce her in the gathering and after, if he left it general and did not mention any wish. If he says, "Divorce her if you wish", then it is confined to the gathering.

quduri.f: Are there situations when the woman still inherits from the man after he divorces her?
quduri.b: If a man divorces his wife Talaq Bain during his final illness and dies before her 'Iddah is complete, she inherits from him. If he dies after the 'Iddah then she does not inherit. The ruling of Talaq Mughallazh is the same as Bain in this. The jurists call this Mas-alatul Fazz [jumping] because the husband hastens the divorce to disinherit her. She remains entitled to inheritance during the 'Iddah. The 'Iddah will be deemed the longer of the two periods, as will be discussed in the chapter on 'Iddah InshaAllaah.

quduri.f: How many divorces can a freeman and a slave give?
quduri.b: According to the Ahnaf this is determined according to the wife, not the husband. If the woman is a slave, then she can get two divorces and her 'Iddah is two menstruations, whether her husband is a slave or a freeman. A freewoman can be divorced thrice, whether her husband is free or a slave. In summary, a slave-girl's husband does not own more than two divorces. If he divorces her twice then he has used up what he got. Two regarding her is like three regarding a freewoman and the divorce is Mughallazh.

quduri.f: Can a man and woman be separated by something besides divorce?
quduri.b: If a man comes to own his wife or a share of her; or if she comes to own her husband or a share of him then they're separated.

quduri.f: Is there another way for a woman to leave the marriage besides divorce?
quduri.b:
If the couple are at ends and fear that they will not be able to adhere to Allaah's limits then there is no harm for the wife to ransom herself with money to free herself from her husband. If she says, "I cast you off [Khul] for such-and-such amount", and he accepts, a Bain divorce takes place and she is liable to pay the amount. This is called Khul'.

If the breakdown in the marriage was from his side then it is Makruh for him to take the money. If it is from her side then it is Makruh for him to take more than what he gave her. In both cases he may legally take the money and the divorce is Bain.

quduri.f: He divorced her in exchange for money and she agreed. Neither used the word Khul'. Is the divorce valid?
quduri.b: Yes, the divorce falls and she is liable to pay the money. The divorce is Bain.

quduri.f: A Muslim woman offered wine/pig for Khul'. The husband accepts. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: She will not pay anything. The separation will be Bain.

quduri.f: He divorced her for wine/pig without mention of Khul'. Does the divorce occur?
quduri.b:
Yes, the divorce occurs as Raj'i23 and the compensation is void.

23 Because in the previous mas-alah the factor was the Khul' and here it is an explicit divorce.

quduri.f: What kind of wealth kind the wife pay as Khul'?
quduri.b: Whatever is a valid Mahr can be offered as a valid Khul'.

quduri.f: She says, "Grant me Khul' in exchange for whatever is in my hand." He accepts and learns there is nothing in her hand. What does she owe?
quduri.b: She owes nothing. The divorce is Bain.

quduri.f: She says, "Grant me Khul' in exchange for whatever wealth is in my hand." He accepts and learns there is nothing in her hand. What does she owe?
quduri.b: She must return her Mahr if she took possession of it. The divorce is Bain.

quduri.f: She says, "Grant me Khul' in exchange for whatever Darahim is in my hand." He accepts and learns there is nothing in her hand. What does she owe?
quduri.b:
She owes three Darahim.24 

24 Because she used the plural term and the smallest plural [in 'Arabic] is 3.
