If the Kuffar captured a slave of a Muslim. One of them bought him and returned him to Darul Islaam. One of his eyes was put out and he claimed Arsh. The old owner can claim him at the price the man paid the enemy but will not take the Arsh.
The Kuffar captured a slave of a Muslim. A man bought him for 1000 Dirham. He was captured a second time and taken to Darul Harb. Another man bought him for 1000 Dirham. The old owner cannot claim him from the second buyer. The first buyer can claim him from the second buyer for 1000. If the old owner then wishes he can claim him from the first buyer for 2000.
When the Kuffar captures a Mudabbar, Ummul Walad or Mukatab belonging to the Muslims, their ownership is not recognised, as when they capture a free person of us. On the other hand, we will own whichever of the above we capture.
A slave belonging to a Muslim flees to the Kuffar and they take him. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى they do not own him. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى they own him.
A slave belonging to a Muslim flees with a horse and goods to the Kuffar. The Kuffar take all that. A man buys these items and takes them to Darul Islaam. The original owner can take the slave back without compensation and the horse and goods at the price the man paid. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى if he wants them back he must pay, including for the slave.
A Harbi enters Darul Islaam with aman and buys a Muslim slave. He takes him to Darul Harb. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the slave is free. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he is not.
A slave of a Harbi embraces Islaam and flees to us or is captured in their lands. He is now free as any of their slaves who flees to the Muslim camp.

quduri.f: What are the regulations of Muslims who abandon Islaam?
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
When a man abandons Islaam he will be presented with an opportunity to re-embrace it. If he has nay doubts, these should be explained to him. He will be imprisoned for three days. If he accepts, well and good. If he refuses he will be killed.
It is Makruh to kill him before offering him Islaam. Nevertheless there is neither Qisas nor Diyah upon his killer.
If a woman abandons Islaam, she will not be killed. She will be imprisoned until she embraces Islaam, even if forever.
The apostate's ownership of his wealth is suspended. If he returns to Islaam his wealth returns to him. If he is executed or dies upon his apostasy, the wealth he earned during his Islaam goes to his Muslim heirs. What he earned after apostasy is Fay and will be deposited in the public treasury.
If the apostate flees to Darul Harb and the judge declares it official, his Mudabbar and Ummul Walad are free and his debts are absolved. His earnings as a Muslim are distributed amongst his Muslim heirs. His debts which he incurred as a Muslim will be paid from his wealth earned as Muslim. His debts which he incurred as an Apostate will be paid from his wealth earned as an Apostate.
All his buying, selling and transacting as an apostate are suspended. If he returns to Islaam they are valid, if he dies, is killed or flees as an apostate to Darul Harb then they are void.
If he returns to Darul Islaam as a Muslim after the court had declared his going to Darul Harb official, then he may claim what remains of his wealth in the hands of his heirs.
The transactions of a female apostate during her apostasy are valid.

quduri.f: What should the ruler do if a people withdraw from the obedience of Islaam and overwhelm a region?
quduri.b: The ruler should calll them to return and will attempt to answer their grievances. He will not commence hostilities until they do so first. Once they attakc he should endeavour to split their ranks asunder. If they have a group they flee to, he should swiftly slay their wounded and pursue those who flee. If they do not have such a group, he should not kill their wounded nor pursue those who flee. Their children will not be captured and their wealth will not be plundered.

quduri.f: The ruler's army captured rebel weapons. Can they use them?
quduri.b: If the Muslims are in need, they may do so.

quduri.f: The ruler's army captured wealth of the rebels. What should he do with them?
quduri.b: He will impound it and will not return it to them until they repent.

quduri.f: The rebels have collected Khiraj and 'Ushr from the lands they control. The ruler then reconquers those lands. Will he collect the taxed a second time?
quduri.b: No. If the rebels had spent it correctly then it suffices on behalf of those who had paid. If they had not, then it is the personal responsibility of the people of that land in their relation with Allaah to pay a second time.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of Hazhr and Ibahah?
quduri.b: Hazhr is literally "prohibition". Mahzhur is prohibited. Ibahah is the right of the Mukallaf [one answereable in Shari'ah] to do or to omit certain acts without entitlement of either reward or punishment.

quduri.f: Which attire is permissible and which are prohibited for men and women?
quduri.b:
There are details to this question:
Neither a man nor a woman may imitate the Kuffar in clothing, apparel and appearence. Men may not imitate women and women may not imitate men.137 
Extravagance and waste are not allowed.
Men may not wear silk. Women may.
Men may wear silk and brocade in war according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. It is Makruh according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى.
There is no harm in men wearing a silken garment if the lengthwise thread is cotton.
It is Haram for men to wear their loin-cloths, trousers, shirts etc. to below the ankles.138
137 Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "May Allah curse the men who imitate women and women who imitate men." [al-Bukhari]

138 Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "That which falls below the ankles of the loin-cloth is in Jahannum (Hell)." [al-Bukhari]

quduri.f: What is the status of silken pillows?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى there is no harm. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is Makruh.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of using gold and silver?
quduri.b:
The rules are as follows:
Men may not adorn themselves with gold and silver. Women may.
It is not permissible to dress a child in gold and silk.
There is no harm in a man wearing a silver ring as long as it does not reach a Mithqal. Anything besides silver is not allowed.
Gold and silver vessels may not be used for eating, drinking, oiling or perfuming. Thus neither men nor women may use gold and silver spoons or antimony sticks.
There is no harm in using glass, lead, crystal and carnelian vessels.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it is permissible to drink from a silver plated vessel, sit on a silver plated saddle or seat, as long as one avoids the actual silvered area.
There is no harm in decorating the Manuscripts of the Quraan, engraving the Masjid and beautifying it with gold water.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a man looking at a strange woman?
quduri.b:
It is not permissible for him to look at her, except her face and hands.139 If he is not safe from lust, then he should not look at her face even, except under dire necessity. He may not touch her face or hand, even if it is without lust.

139 That is not a license for women to roam about displaying their faces to all in this age of sin and rebellion. What security is there that the men are not gazing at them with lust?

quduri.f: What is a valid reason to look at her face? [i.e. a man looking at a strange woman]
quduri.b: A witness has a valid reason to look at her when giving Arsh on her, as does the judge when ruling about her. They may look even if they fear that they will feel lust.

quduri.f: A woman has a sore on her thigh. The doctor needs to examine it. What should he do?
quduri.b: He may examine the place of the sore only. He should not look at the rest of the thigh.

quduri.f: What is the law of men looking at man and women looking at women?
quduri.b: A man may look at another man's body except the region from the navel to the knees, as may a woman look at another woman except from the navel to the knees.

quduri.f: Which parts of a man may a woman look at?
quduri.b: She may see of a man whatever a man may see of a man.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a man looking at his slave-girl and wife?
quduri.b:
He may see the entire body of his permitted140 slave-girl and wife.

140 I.e. a slave-girl who is a Fire-worshipper, Mukatabah, married to another, or forbidden unto him by way of breastfeeding or Musaharah is just like a strange woman unto him in terms of what he may see or her.

quduri.f: What may a man see of his Mahram women?
quduri.b:
He may see her face, head, chest and calves.141 He may not see her back, thighs and stomach. There is no harm in him touching that which he may see.

141 This is also on condition that both parties are safe from lust.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a man looking at a slave-girl not belonging to him?
quduri.b: He may see the same parts which are permissible for him to look at from his female Mahram relatives. There is no harm if he touches those parts if he intends purchasing her, even if he fears lust will arise.

quduri.f: Can a male slave look at his female owner?
quduri.b: No, he may only look at those parts which are permissible for a strange man to look at as per the previously mentioned conditions.

quduri.f: What is the status of hoarding essential foods?
quduri.b: It is not permissible to hoard foods essential to men and beasts in a land where its hoarding harms its people.

quduri.f: A man kept back the grain of his farm, or the grain he imported. Is this deemed prohibited hoarding as well?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the status of the government fixing prices?
quduri.b: It is not appropriate. The government should leave the people to trade as they wish.

quduri.f: Sundry regulations
quduri.b:
It is Makruh to divide the Quraanic ayat in groups of ten [Ruku'] and to place dots and diacritical marks therein.142 
It is Makruh to use eunuchs.
There is no harm in castrating animals.
There is no harm in mating a horse and donkey to breed a mule.
It is permissible to accept the word of a slave or minor that the owner or adult had allowed the guest to enter or had given the recipient a gift.
The word of an open sinner will be accepted in transactions.
In matters of Din only an 'adil [does not openly sin] is accepted.
An eunuch gazing at a strange woman is the same as a normal man's regulations.
A man may practice coitus interuptus with his slave-girl without her permission. He may not do so with his wife, except with her permission.
It is Makruh to sell weapons during times of strife.143 
There is no harm in selling juice to one whom knowns will make wine of it.
142 Because the 'Arabs could read the Quran without them. Putting the dots and marks these helps ensure correct reading.

143 To those known to cause strife and rebellion.

quduri.f: What is Wasiyah and what is its status?
quduri.b:
Literally it is a request that someone perform some act, whether during the life or after the death of the one requesting. In the terminology of the jurists it is the transfer of ownership to someone upon the one's death, whether it be of a physical item or of a benefit,

Its status is that if the Musi [one making the bequest] has obligations upon him to Allaah e.g. unpaid Zakah, he did not perform Hajj when it became compulsory upon him, etc. then it is Wajib upon him to make a bequest that these be fulfilled on his behalf. It is also Wajib upon him to leave a bequest for the fulfilment of rights of people against him and debts he owes them. He must also leave instructions for the return of trusts and Wadi'ah he has by him.

If he does not have any outstanding rights of Allaah or humans or debts to be paid, then it is Mustahhab for him to leave a bequest that some of his wealth be spent in good avenues.

If his debts encompass his entire estate, then he may not make a bequest for anyone. If he does make a bequest, it is not valid and will not be implemented unless the creditors agree out of their kindness.

quduri.f: Can a Muslim leave a bequest for a Kafir? Can a Kafir leave a bequest for a Muslim?
quduri.b: Both are permissible.

quduri.f: Is a minor's bequest valid?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Are there people for whom one's bequest is void?
quduri.b: A bequest for one's murderer is void, be the murder deliberate or accidental, if he was directly involved in the slaying.

quduri.f: Are there other people for whom bequests are not valid?
quduri.b: One cannot make a bequest for one's heir, unless all the other sane, adult heirs agree.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated that the bequest be of "some of his wealth"? Can he not make a bequest with all his wealth?
quduri.b: A bequest is only valid up to a third of the estate, not more, unless the heirs agree after the death of the one making the bequest. Their consent during his life is disregarded. It is Mustahabb that one keeps the bequest to less than a third.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest for another. The recipient accepted or rejected it during the bequest maker's life. What is the status of his acceptance or rejection?
quduri.b: It is of no effect. Once the bequest maker actually dies, the recipient may then accept or reject.

quduri.f: Does ownership transfer with acceptance?
quduri.b: The one for whom the bequest was made assumes ownership upon acceptance, except in one scenario. If the one making the bequest dies and the one for whom the bequest was made dies before acceptance, the bequest is immediately transferred to the ownership of the beneficiary's heirs.

quduri.f: A man appointed an executor i.e. someone who will fulfil his bequest. He accepted in the presence of the one making the bequest and then rejected it in his absence. Has his status changed?
quduri.b: The status has changed if he refuses in his presence and the bequest is void. If he refuses in his absence then it does not change.

quduri.f: A man appoints a Kafir, slave or open sinner as executor. Is this valid?
quduri.b: The judge will replace them with another executor.

quduri.f: Can one appoint one's own slave as executor?
quduri.b: If there are adults amongst the heirs then it is not valid, otherwise it is.

quduri.f: If a man appoints an executor who is unable to implement the bequest, what happens?
quduri.b: The Judge will appoint someone with him.

quduri.f: A man appointed two executors. Must they transact together?
quduri.b: Yes, according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى none may transact without the other, except for purchasing funeral cloth and making funeral arrangements for the deceased; feeding and clothing his minor children; returning trusts; implementing specific instructions of the bequest; freeing specific slaves; fulfilling debts; and representing the deceased in legal disputes.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that bequests cannot exceed a third of the estate. A man makes a bequest for a man for a third of his estate and another third for another man. The heirs do not consent. How will this bequest be implemented?
quduri.b: A third of the estate will be equally divided between the two.

quduri.f: And if he bequeathed a third for one and a sixth for the other? [i.e. a man makes a bequest for two men, but the heirs do not consent (for it to be above the maximum one third)]
quduri.b: The first will get two-thirds of a third of the estate and the other will get a sixth of a third.

quduri.f: He bequeathed his entire estate to one man and a third to another. The heirs do not consent. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى a third will be shared equally between them. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى they will share a third between them in quarters. Three for the first man and one for the second.

quduri.f: Is there any scenario according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى where the beneficiary can receive more than a third?
quduri.b:
It is not allowed except in three cases - Mahabah [partiality]144, Si'ayah [striving]145 and Darahim Mursalah146 [unrestricted dirhams].

144 For example, a man has two slaves. One is worth 1,100 and the other is 600. He leaves a bequest that the one be sold to someone for 100 and the other to someone else for 100. The first has thus gained 1000 and the second 500. If there is no other wealth in the estate and the heirs do not consent, they will share in a third of 1500 as follows - the first gets paid 100 plus two-thirds of 1000 and the other 100 plus two-thirds of 500.
145 A man has two slaves, nothing else. He bequests that they be freed. The one is worth 1000 and the other 2000. If the heirs agree they will be freed in total, if not then from one third which is worth 1000. The one worth 2000 will be freed from the estate to the extent of two-thirds of 1000 and will earn to reimburse the rest of his 2000. The one worth 1000 will be freed from the estate to the extent of a third of 1000 and will earn to reimburse the extent for the rest of his 1000.
146 A man leaves a bequest of 2000 Dirhams for one man and 1000 for another. One third of his known estate is 1000. Each is entitled to his full share on the possibility that there is more to the estate, although at the moment each will only get two thirds of 1000 and a third of 1000 respectively.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest of a third of his Dirhams or goats for a man. Two thirds of it perished. Only a third remains. What will the beneficiary receive?
quduri.b: If all that remains equals a third of the estate the beneficiary takes everything.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest for another for a third of his clothing. Two-third got destroyed. The remaining third equals a third of the estate. What is the beneficiary entitled to?
quduri.b:
A third of the remaining clothing.147

147 If they are of different kinds. If they are all the same then the ruling is the same as in Dirhams.

quduri.f: A man left a bequest of 1000 Dirhams to the beneficiary. His estate consists of wealth at hand and debts owing to the deceased. How will the beneficiary be paid out?
quduri.b: If a third of the wealth at hand covers the 1000, it should be handed to him. If not, he will be given a third of the cash at hand and every time the debts are colllected, a third will be given to him until he gathers his 1000.

quduri.f: Can a bequest be made in favour of a foetus?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Can a bequest of a foetus be made?
quduri.b: Yes, if it is born in less than six months from the day of the bequest.

quduri.f: A man bequethed his slave-girl to someone and excepted her foetus she was carrying. What is the status of the bequest?
quduri.b: The bequest and the exception are both valid.

quduri.f: A man bequeathed his pregnant slave-girl to a man and made no mention of the foetus. She gave birth after the bequest maker died. Only then did the beneficiary accept the bequest. Does he receive the slave only or her child as well?
quduri.b: If both are covered by a third of the estate then they are both his. If not, then they are valued over the third and he will take both of them in that proportion according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he will first claim his proportion from the mother. If there is anything remaining then he will take it from the child.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest for the children of a man or for the heirs of a man. How will they share the bequest?
quduri.b: In the first case they share equally and the second as per inheritance i.e. a male gets double the share of a female.

quduri.f: A man left a bequest for Zayd and 'Amr of a third of his wealth. 'Amr  dies. How will the bequest be shared?
quduri.b: Zayd gets the entire amount.

quduri.f: If he left a third of his estate to be shared between 'Amr and Zayd and Zayd dies?
quduri.b: 'Amr gets half of the third.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest of a third of his wealth. He has no wealth. He then earns some wealth. What is the beneficiary entitled to?
quduri.b: A third of whatever he owned at the time of death.

quduri.f: The beneficiary dies before the one who made the bequest. What is the status of the bequest?
quduri.b: It is void.

quduri.f: What is the status of a bequest, "equal to the share of my son"?
quduri.b: It is valid, for example if he had two sons, they get two third and the beneficiary a third.

quduri.f: A man left a bequest of a "share" and did not stipulate what the share is.
quduri.b: The beneficiary is entitled to the least share of the heirs. If that is less than a sixth he is entitled to a sixth.

quduri.f: And if the bequest was for a "part" of the estate? [i.e. a man left a bequest and did not stipulate what the share is]
quduri.b: The heirs may give whatever they wish to.

quduri.f: A bequest was made in favour of the neighbours. Who are entitled?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it refers to the adjacent neighbours.

quduri.f: Who are entitled if the bequest was for "ashar" [in-laws] and "akthan" [sons-in-law]?
quduri.b: A bequest for Ashar is for every Mahram blood relative of his wife. Akthan are all the husbands of his female blood relatives.

quduri.f: And if he bequeathed to his Aqarib [family]?
quduri.b: It includes his blood relative Mahrams from the closest then the next closest and so on. Parents and children are not included. It includes two individuals and more.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest for his family. He has two paternal uncles and two maternal uncles.
quduri.b: The bequest is interpreted for the paternal uncles.

quduri.f: And if he has one paternal uncle and two maternal? [i.e. a man made a bequest for his family]
quduri.b: The paternal uncle gets half and the maternal uncles share the other half. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى a bequest for Aqarib covers all whose lineage is attributed to the furthest male ancestor in Islaam.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to free one's slave, sell on Muhabah or grant a gift on one's deathbed?
quduri.b: These are all permissible, but must be taken from the third of the estate. The beneficiaries are treated just as the beneficiaries of an explicit bequest.

quduri.f: A man manumitted then made Muhabah; or made Muhabah then manumitted. Which will be implemented first?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى if Muhabah is made first it has preference, if second then both are equal. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى both are equal in both scenarios.

quduri.f: A man made several bequests for the pleasure of Allaah. Which will be implemented first?
quduri.b: His Fard obligations must first be attended to, whether he put them first or last, e.g. outstanding Hajj, Zakah and Kaffarah. That which is not Fard will be implemented as per his instructions.

quduri.f: A man left a bequest that his Fard Hajj be fulfilled. What is the duty of the heirs?
quduri.b: A man of his city should perform the Hajj on his behalf. He will do it with conveyance. If he did not leave sufficient funds to have the Hajj performed from his city, someone will be appointed from where the funds will suffice.

quduri.f: A man died on his way for Hajj. He left a bequest that Hajj be performed on his behalf. From where must the Hajj be performed?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it is from his city. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is from where he died.

quduri.f: Sundry regulations
quduri.b:
A Mukatab's bequest is not implemented even if he left sufficient funds.
One may annul one's bequest, but the cancellation must be explicit.
One may make a bequest of the services of one's slave or residence of one's house for a specified time, just as one may do it for an indefinite time. If the value of the slave is within the third, the slave will be handed to the beneficiary for service. If the slave is the entire estate, he will serve the heirs two days and the beneficiary one day. When the beneficiary dies then the slave is entirely for the heirs.

quduri.f: What is Faraid?
quduri.b:
It is the plural of Faridah, which is applied to that which Allaah has written upon His salves. He ordered us to do it, with emphasis, and there is no escape from fulfilling it. The one who does not do it and has no Shari' excuse is a Fasiq [open sinner].

In common usage it has come to refer to the shares of inheritance Allaah has stipulated for males and females from the estate of the deceased. He says, "Allaah instructs you regarding your children, the male will receive double the share of the female."148

148 An-Nisa: 11-12

quduri.f: Explain the order of Inheritance.
quduri.b:
The estate of the deceased will first be used to cover his burial and funeral expenses which should neither be extravagant nor unduly frugal. Whatever is left will be used to pay his debts. After the payment of his debts a third of the remainder is used to fulfil any bequests he made. Thereafter the remainder will be divided amongst the heirs as per Allaah's instructions in His Book or what He conveyed via the tongue of His Rasul ﷺ.

One begins with the Ashabul Faraid, who are those whose shares have been defined in the Quraan. Then the 'Asabat will receive what the Ashabul Faraid have left. If there are no Ashabul Faraid, the 'Asabat will take everything. If there are no 'Asabat then the remainder returns to those Ashabul Faraid who have the same lineage as per their shares.

If there are neither Ashabul Faraid nor 'Asabat, or there are no Ashabul Faraid to whom the remainder can return, then the Ulul Arham receive. If there are no Ulul Arham also, then the Mawlal Muwalah is entitled. If there are none then the beneficiary of the bequest is entitled to everything. If there are none then the estate is given to the public treasury.

quduri.f: Which males inherit from the deceased?
quduri.b:
There are ten:
Son
Son's son and descending
Father
Father's father and ascending
Brother
Brother's son
Father's brother
Father's brother's son
Husband
Mawlan Ni'mah i.e. the one who holds the Wala of freeing a slave.

quduri.f: Which females inherit from the deceased?
quduri.b:
There are seven:
Daughter
Sons' daughter
Mother
Grandmother, paternal and maternal
Sister
Wife
Mawlan Ni'mah

quduri.f: What are the causes of disinheritance?
quduri.b:
There are four:
Slavery
Murder
If the deceased and the heir are of different religions.
If one party lives in Darul Islaam and the other in Darul Harb.
An Apostate and a slave thus do not inherit from anyone. A murderer cannot inherit from his victim. A Muslim cannot inherit from a Kafir, a Kafir cannot inherit from a Muslim. A Harbi cannot inherit from a Zimmi, a Zimmi cannot inherit from a Harbi. Two Harbis cannot inherit from each other if they are in different Dars.

quduri.f: What are the shares Allaah has stipulated in the Quraan?
quduri.b:
They are six:
Half
Quarter
Eight
Two-thirds
A third
A sixth

quduri.f: Who is entitled to a half? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b:
There are five such parties:
Daughter.
Son's daughter if there is no direct daughter.
Full sister.
A sister on the father's side if there is no full sister.
A wife if there is no son of the deceased or son's child and descending.

quduri.f: Who is entitled to the quarter? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: The husband if his late wife has no children or son's children whether from him or another man. Similarly the wife of the deceased, if he had no children or son's children whether from her or another woman. If there are several wives they all share in the quarter.

quduri.f: Who is entiteld to the eight? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: The wife if the late husband had a child or son's child. If there are several wives they share in the eight.

quduri.f: Who is entitled to two-thirds? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: Two or more daughters if the deceased does not have a son. Also, two or more daughters of a son if the deceased has no direct children or son's son. Also two sisters if they have the same parents as the deceased or at least the same father, and the deceased has no child, male or female. The father is also entitled to two-thirds if the deceased leaves behind both parents, but no son or daughter.

quduri.f: Who is entitled to the third? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: The mother if the deceased did not leave behind a child, nor a child of the son, nor two or more brothers or sisters. Also entitled are if there are two or more children of the mother if the deceased has neither child, nor son's child, nor father, nor grandfather. In this case the males and females and males are equal in shares and entitlement.

quduri.f: Who is entitled to the sixth? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: Each of the parents if the deceased has a child or son's child and descending. Also the mother if two or more brothers or sisters, irrespective from which side. Grandfathers and grandmothers if there is a child and son's child. The son's daughters with the daughter if they have no brother. Children of the mother if the deceased has no child or son's child and descending, male or female, and no father or grandfather.

quduri.f: Are there certain relatives who nullify the shares of others?
quduri.b:
Yes, there are several which nullify others:
Maternal and paternal grandmothers are nullified if there is a mother.
The father nullifies the grandfathers and brothers.
A mother's child is nullified by any of these four - a child, son's child, father and grandfather nullify.
When daughters acquire two-thirds the son's daughters are dropped, unless there is equal to them or lower than them a son's son, in which case they inherit as 'Asabat.149 
When the full sisters acquire two-thirds the sisters who share only a father with the deceased are dropped, unless they have a brother, in which case they inherit as 'Asabat.
149 A male gets double the share of each female.

quduri.f: What is the order of inheritance of the 'Asabat?
quduri.b:
The closest 'Asabat are the sons; then their sons; then the father; then the grandfather; then the father's sons i.e. brothers'; then the grandfather's sons i.e. paternal uncles; then the sons of the grandfather's father.

If the father's sons are equal in rank, then the full brothers have preference. Sons, sons' sons and brothers share with their respective sisters on the basis of double share for each male and single for each female. The other 'Asabat are exclusively male, without females.

These 'Asabat are by way of lineage. There is also the Mawlal 'Itaqah i.e. the ex-owner who had freed a slave who has now died. These are 'Asabah by way of cause. Next entitled are the closest then the next closest 'Asabat of the ex-owner. The ex-owner is only entitled after the 'Asabat by lineage, but before the Zawil Arham.

quduri.f: What is Hajb?
quduri.b: It is the deprivation of certain heirs from inheriting by the presence of other heirs. If the heir is entirely deprived it is termed Hajb al-Hurman. If his allotment is reduced, it is termed Hajb an-Nuqsan.

quduri.f: Explain both kinds [i.e. Hajb al-Hurman and Hajb an-Nuqsan].
quduri.b:
A mother's share is reduced from a third to a sixth by the presence of a child, a son's child and descending. Two brothers or sisters, from whichever parent they may be, reduce the husband's share from half to quarter when the deceased has a child, just as a wife is reduced from quarter to eight when her late husband has a child. These are Hajb an-Nuqsan.

Hajb al-Hurman is enacted when there are two daughters and a son's daughter. The son's daughter is completely deprived in their presence. If however he left one daughter and a son's daughter, the daughter gets half and the son's daughter gets a sixth to combine as two-thirds. If he left two full sisters and a sister with a common father, the half-sister is completely deprived. If there is one full sister and with a sister with a common father, the altter gets a sixth adding up with the other to two-thirds.

quduri.f: You had mentioned that if there are no 'Asabat then the remainder of the inheritance after the Ashabul Faraid get their shares the remainder gets shared amongst the Ashabul Faraid. Is this when both categories of 'Asabat are not to be found i.e. 'Asabat by lineage and 'Asabat by cause or only if the 'Asabat by lineage are not found.
quduri.b: It applies to both. Thus if the deceased has a Mawlal 'Itaq the remainder goes to him, not the Ashabul Faraid.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated 'Asabat by lineage?
quduri.b: Because the remainder will not go to the husband or wife.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that if there are no Ashabul Faraid and no'Asabat, the Ulul Arham will inherit the estate. Who are the Ulul Arham?
quduri.b:
They are ten:
Daughter's child
Sister's child
Brother's daughter
Paternal uncle's daughter
Maternal uncle
Maternal aunt
Mother's father
Mother's father's brother
Paternal aunt
Son of brother with common mother.
The closest of these are more entitled than the further ones.

quduri.f: Is there an order to their entitlement or are they all equal?
quduri.b: There is an order to their entitlement to inheritance as follows - the most entitled is the one from the child of the deceased i.e. the daughter's child. Then the descendants of the parents or one of them i.e. brother's daughters and sister's children. Then the child of the parents of the parents or one of them i.e. maternal uncles, maternal aunts and paternal aunts.

quduri.f: If two people have the same degree of relation to the deceased, do both inherit or is one preferred over the other?
quduri.b:
The one who is closest to the deceased in inheritance will be preferred.150

150 A deceased leaves a paternal uncle's daughter and paternal aunt's son. Everything is for her. If he left a daughter's daughter's daughter and a son's daughter's daughter everything is for the son's granddaughter. [al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: Sundry regulations
quduri.b:
A mother receives a third of what remains in two cases: Firstly, when a woman dies and leaves her parents and husband. The husband takes half and the remainder is shared in thirds amongst the parents, a third for the mother and two-thirds for the father. Secondly, a man dies and leaves a wife and his parents. The wife gets a quarter and the remainder is for the parents in thirds, one third for the mother and two-thirds for the father.
A man dies and leaves two sons of his paternal uncles and his brother on their mother's side. The brother gets a sixth and the remainder is divided between the two equally.
A woman dies and leaves a husband and mother or grandmother and brothers from the mother's side and a full brother. The husband gets half, the mother a sixth, the half brothers a third and nothing for the full brother.
A group drowns or a wall falls on them. It is not known who died first. The estate of each of them is for the surviving heirs.
If a Fire-worshipper has a double relation in two persons. The one inherits with the other and he inherits from both.151 
A Fire-worshipper does not inherit from invalid marriages which their religion permits.
'Asabat of an illegitimate child or a child of Mula'anah are the Mawla of their mothers.

According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى if a man dies and leaves a foetus heir, the estate is suspended until the woman gives birth.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى a grandfather is more entitled to inheritance than brothers. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he will be treated as one of the brothers unless his share thereby falls to less than a third.
If there are several grandmothers then the sixth is for the closest of them.
A grandfather deprives his mother. A mother's father's mother does not inherit a share. Every grandmother disinherits her mother.
A freed-slave leaves behind his Mawla's father and son. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى his wealth goes to the son. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the father gets a sixth and the rest is for the son.
If he leaves his Mawla's grandfather and brother then according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the wealth is for the grandfather. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is between them.
Walaul 'Itaqah cannot be sold or gifted.
151 E,g, he marries his daughter and she gives birth to two girls. He dies, then one of the girls dies. She thus leaves behind her mother who is also her sister from her father's side and she leaves her full sister. The mother gets a sixth by virtue of being her mother; the full sister gets half; and the mother gets another sixth by virtue of being a sister on the father's side.

quduri.f: How are the calculations for the division of the estate done?
quduri.b:
It is done as follows:
If one heir gets a half and another gets a half e.g. a woman leaves her husband and full sister, or there is a half and the remainder to the other heir e.g. a woman leaves a husband and a paternal uncle; then the asl [the number used in the division of the estate] is based on the number 2.
If there is a third and what remains e.g. the deceased left a mother and paternal uncle, or there is two-thirds and what remains e.g. he left two daughters and a paternal uncle; then the asl is 3.
If it is a quarter and what remains e.g. the deceased leaves a wife and a brother, or there is a quarter and a half e.g. the deceased left a husband, daughter and brother; then the asl is 4.
If there is an eight and what remains e.g. he left a wife and a son, or an eight and a half e.g. he left a wife and a daughter; then the asl is 8.
If there is a half and a third, e.g. he left a wife, mother and brother, or a half and sixth e.g. he left a mother, daughter and brother; then the asl is 6.
If there is a quarter and a third e.g. he left a wife and mother, or there is a quarter and a sixth e.g. she left her husband, mother and son; then the asl is 12.
If there is a share of an eight and two shares of a sixth e.g. he left his wife, parents and son, or there is an eight with two-thirds, e.g. he left a wife and two daughters; then the asl is 24.

quduri.f: After the total allotted shares are added together the total does not reach one. How is the estate divided?
quduri.b: The denominator is adjusted to a higher number which can be added together. This number is called 'Awl. This process is called 'Ailah. You have learned that the denominators are 7, four denominators are not affected by 'Ailah i.e. 2, 3, 4 and 8. Three are adjusted to 'Awl. 6 is adjusted to 7, 8, 9, and 10. 12 is adjusted to 13, 15 and 17. 24 is adjusted to 27.

quduri.f: Sometimes the shares of a group cannot be divided according to the denominator used. How are the figures adjusted?
quduri.b:
Firstly, understand that the mathematical relationship between the numbers of the denominators are one of the following:
Tamathul

Tadakhul
Tawafuq
Tabayun 
Tamathul is where the numbers are equal e.g. 3 and 3
Tadakhul is where one number is a factor of the others e.g. 3 and 9
Tawafuq is where the smaller number is not in itself a factor of the larger number, but a third number exists as a common factor between them e.g. 8 and 20 can both be divided by 4
Tabayun is where neither number is a factor of the other, nor is there a third number which is a common factor e.g. 9 and 10.

Once this is understood, know that if the shares of a group do not match with the total denominator, multiply the numbers in which the group needs to be divided with the 'asl or the 'Awl and the result will encompass the various snares inshaAllaah.

For example, a man leaves his wife and two brothers. The wife gets a quarter and the brothers three-quarters. The denominator of 4 cannot cleanly divide amongst the parties. Hence multiply the asl of 4 with the number of brothers of 2 and use the result of 8. The wife gets 2 shares of 8 and the brothers get 6. This was an example of Tabayun.

In Tawafuq denominator is multiplied by the common factor. For example, a man leaves his wife and 6 brothers. The wife gets a quarter and the brothers get 3 quarters. Divide the number of brothers by their shares, which is 6 divided by 3, which equals 2. Now multiply the shares by 2. The total shares are now 8. The wife gets 2 and each brother gets 1. This is in a case where there was no 'Awl.

An example with 'Awl and Tabayun is when the estate is divided amongst the husband and three full sisters. The Asl of 6 is made Awl to 7. Tashih is then made out of 21.

An example with 'Awl and Tabayun is when the estate is divided amongst the husband, parents and 6 daughters. The Asl is 12. The husband gets a quarter i.e. 3 shares. Each parent gets a sixth which totals 4 shares. The 6 daughters get two-thirds which equals 8 shares. The denominator cannot accomodate the total shares and 'Awl is made to 15 and the daughters' shares (8) are divided by the number of daughters (6). 8 and 6 can both be divided by 2, which reduces the number of daughters to 3. 3 is multiplied with the 'Awl (15) and the result is a denominator of 45. The shares are now completely balanced. The husband gets 9 of the 45, the parents get 12 and the daughters 24, each daughter gets 4.

quduri.f: You have mentioned problems where the shares cannot be divided according to the number of individuals in one group. What if there are more than one group like that?
quduri.b:
Multiply the first group with the second and if there is a third like that multiply the result with the third. Take the final result and multiply it with the Asl. This is if there is Tabayun between the groups. For example, a man leaves two wives, 5 grandmothers, 3 brothers on the father's side and 1 paternal uncle. The Asl is 12. The wives get a quarter or 3 shares. The grandmother gets a sixth or 2 shares. The half brothers get a third which is 4 shares. The uncle gets the remainder of 3. The shares of all three groups cannot be divided by the number of people in the group. Multiply the number of wives (2) by the number of grandmothers (5). Multiply the result (10) by the numer of brothers (3). Multiply that result (30) by the Asl. The result is 360 by which denominator the shares balance for each individual.

If the number in each group equals the number in the other, that same number will satisfy the other group if used to multiply. For example, a man leaves 2 wives and 2 brothers. The Asl is 4. The 2 wives get a quarter (1 share) and the 2 brothers get the remaining 3 shares. The shares of each party cannot be divided amongst the individuals. Multiply the number in each group by the Asl. The result is 8. The shares are balanced. The wives get 2 shares, each takes 1. The brothers get 6 shares, each gets 6.

If the smaller number can be divided into the bigger number then the bigger number will suffice, e.g. with 4 wives and 2 brothers, simply multiply by 4.

If the numbers in each group have a common factor, multiply the remaining factors with each other and the Asl. For example a man leaves 4 wives, a sister and 6 paternal uncles. 4 and 6 can both be divided by 2. Multiply the remainders of 2 by 3, and then the result by the Asl to give a final result of 48. With this number the estate balances and each heir gets a proper calculated share.

quduri.f: Sometimes an heir dies before receiving his inheritance. How do the surviving heirs of both deceased parties inherit?
quduri.b:
If the shares received by the second deceased can only be shared amongst the remaining heirs, then the first calculation will be used for the second death as well. For example, a woman dies leaving behind her husband, son and 2 daughters. The Asl is 4. The husband gets 1 share and the children 3 according to Allaah's command, "For the male is double the share of the female." To divide the children's shares their number will be multiplied by the Asl (4). They are treated as 4 people because of the son getting double the daughters. The result is 16. The husband gets 4, the son 6 and each daughter gets 3. The husband then dies because they receive their shares. He leaves behind the mentioned son and daughters. The estate remains in 16 shares. The son gets 8 shares and each daughter gets 4. This was an example where the Asl of the second estate is equal [Tasawi] to the number shares which the second deceased obtained from the first deceased. No further multiplication or other calculation was needed.

If the relationship is instead Tawafuq or Tadakhul, multiply the remaining factor of the second estate with the final adjusted denominator of the first estate. Then multiply that according to the remaining factors of the numbers of the heirs of the first deceased. Both estates will be balanced. For example, a woman dies and leaves behind her husband and two brothers. The adjusted denominator will be 4. The husband takes 2 and the brothers take the remainder of 1 each. The husband then dies before the estate is shared. He leaves 4 sons only. The Asl of the second estate (4) and the number which the second deceased inherited from the first deceased (2) are both divisible by 2. So multiplu half the Asl of the second estate (2) with the final denominator of the first estate (4). The result is 8. Multiply remaining factor of 8 (4) with the remaining factor of the shares of the brothers of the first estate (2). The brothers take 2 shares each and the husband's son 1 each.

If the relationship is Tabayun then multiply the second adjusted denominator with the first adjusted denominator. The shares of the first deceased's heirs are multiplied by the second adjusted denominator or the remaining factor. The shares of the second deceased's heirs by what is in his hands or the remaining factor. For example, a woman dies and leaves her husband, daughter, mother and brother. The estate is divided into 12 shares. The husband takes quarter (3), the daughter half (6), the mother a sixth (2) and the brother takes the remainder (1). The husband dies and leaves a wife besides the first deceased wife. He also leaves his parents. His estate will be divided into 4. The wife takes a quarter (1) and the parents take the remaining 3. There is Tabayun between the Asl of the second estate (4) and the husband's share from the first estate (3). The two Asl are multiplied resulting in 48 by which both estates are balanced. The shares of the surviving heirs of the first deceased are multiplied by the second Asl (4). The shares of the heirs of the second deceased are multiplied by the shares the second deceased got from the first estate (3). The first deceased daughter gets 24 shares, the first deceased mother gets 8, her brother gets 4, the second wife gets 3, the father of the second decease gets 6 and his mother gets 3. This totals 48.

NOTE:
Once the shares of the Munasakhah [when an heir dies before receiving his share] have balanced and the Dirham is divided amongst the heirs and there is a remainder after dividing the Dirhams into 48, share the remainder according to the Habbah [units Dirhams are divided into] for each share, and Allaah knows best.

In  it is used as  a metaphorical phrase to mean do not keep your hand stackled to your neck out of miserliness, do not be niggardly. In verse  unuqun is metaphorically used and refers to the principle that every action produces an effect which is "made to cling to a person" and that his deeds will be recorded in a Book and that their effect will be seen on the day of resurrection. ithaf.f: مَا أَرْكَانُ الْوُضُوءِ؟
ithaf.b: أَرْكَانُ الْوُضُوءِ أَرْبَعَةٌ: غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ، وَغَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ مَعَ الْمِرْفَقَيْنِ، وَمَسْحُ الرَّأْسِ، وَغَسْلُ الرِّجْلَيْنِ مَعَ الْكَعْبَيْنِ.

en.f: What are the pillars (arkan) of wudu?
en.b: Wudu has four pillars: washing the face, washing the arms including the elbows, wiping the head, and washing the feet including the ankles.

ithaf.f: مَا سُنَنُ الْوُضُوءِ؟
ithaf.b: النِّيَّةُ، وَالتَّسْمِيَةُ، وَغَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ إِلَى الرُّسْغَيْنِ قَبْلَ إِدْخَالِهِمَا الإِنَاءَ، وَالسِّوَاكُ، وَالْمَضْمَضَةُ، وَالاِسْتِنْشَاقُ، وَتَخْلِيلُ اللِّحْيَةِ وَالأَصَابِعِ، وَتَثْلِيثُ الْغَسْلِ، وَمَسْحُ كُلِّ الرَّأْسِ وَالأُذُنَيْنِ، وَالتَّرْتِيبُ، وَالْمُوَالَاةُ، وَالدَّلْكُ.

en.f: What are the sunnahs of wudu?
en.b: The intention, saying Bismillah, washing the hands to the wrists before putting them in the vessel, the miswak, rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose, running wet fingers through the beard and between the fingers, washing each part three times, wiping the whole head and the ears, keeping the order, washing without pause, and rubbing.

ithaf.f: مَا مُسْتَحَبَّاتُ الْوُضُوءِ؟
ithaf.b: التَّيَامُنُ، وَمَسْحُ الرَّقَبَةِ، وَالأَدْعِيَةُ الْمَأْثُورَةُ فِيهِ.

en.f: What are the recommended acts (mustahabbat) of wudu?
en.b: Starting with the right, wiping the neck, and the du'as transmitted for it.

ithaf.f: مَا الَّذِي يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ؟
ithaf.b: مَا خَرَجَ مِنَ السَّبِيلَيْنِ، وَسَيْلَانُ نَجَسٍ مِنْ غَيْرِهِمَا، وَقَيْءٌ مَلَأَ الْفَمَ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ بَلْغَمًا، وَنَوْمُ غَيْرِ مُتَمَكِّنٍ، وَالإِغْمَاءُ، وَالْجُنُونُ، وَالسُّكْرُ، وَقَهْقَهَةُ مُصَلٍّ بَالِغٍ، وَمُبَاشَرَةٌ فَاحِشَةٌ.

en.f: What breaks wudu?
en.b: Anything that comes out of the two private passages; impurity flowing from elsewhere; vomit that fills the mouth and is not phlegm; sleep while not firmly seated; fainting; insanity; intoxication; an adult laughing aloud in prayer; and intimate skin contact (mubasharah fahishah).

ithaf.f: مَا فُرُوضُ الْغُسْلِ؟
ithaf.b: غَسْلُ الْفَمِ، وَالْأَنْفِ، وَالْبَدَنِ، وَيَكْفِي بَلُّ أَصْلِ ضَفِيرَةِ الْمَرْأَةِ.

en.f: What are the obligations (fara'id) of ghusl?
en.b: Washing the mouth, the nose and the whole body. For a woman it is enough to wet the roots of her braids.

ithaf.f: مَا سُنَنُ الْغُسْلِ؟
ithaf.b: الْبَدَاءَةُ بِغَسْلِ يَدَيْهِ وَفَرْجِهِ، وَدَلْكُهُ عَلَى بَدَنِهِ، ثُمَّ يَتَوَضَّأُ، ثُمَّ يُفِيضُ الْمَاءَ عَلَى بَدَنِهِ ثَلَاثًا.

en.f: What are the sunnahs of ghusl?
en.b: Beginning by washing the hands and private parts, rubbing the body, then making wudu, then pouring water over the body three times.

ithaf.f: مَا مُوجِبَاتُ الْغُسْلِ؟
ithaf.b: إِنْزَالُ الْمَنِيِّ بِشَهْوَةٍ، وَإِيجَالُ حَشَفَةٍ فِي قُبُلٍ أَوْ دُبُرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا، وَرُؤْيَةُ مُسْتَيْقِظٍ مَنِيًّا أَوْ مَذْيًا، وَانْقِطَاعُ الْحَيْضِ وَالنِّفَاسِ.

en.f: What makes ghusl obligatory?
en.b: Emission of semen with desire; entry of the tip of the penis into the front or back passage, (making ghusl obligatory) on both; a person waking to find semen or madhy; and the end of menstruation and post-natal bleeding.

ithaf.f: فِيمَ يُسَنُّ الْغُسْلُ؟
ithaf.b: يُسَنُّ الْغُسْلُ لِلْجُمُعَةِ، وَالْعِيدَيْنِ، وَالإِحْرَامِ، وَلِعَرَفَةَ.

en.f: When is ghusl sunnah?
en.b: Ghusl is sunnah for Jumu'ah, the two Eids, ihram, and the day of 'Arafah.

ithaf.f: بِأَيِّ مَاءٍ يَصِحُّ التَّطْهِيرُ؟
ithaf.b: يَصِحُّ التَّطْهِيرُ بِمَاءٍ مُطْلَقٍ كَمَاءِ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَإِنْ تَغَيَّرَ بِالْمُكْثِ.

en.f: With what water is purification valid?
en.b: Purification is valid with plain water (ma' mutlaq), such as rainwater and ground water, even if it has changed from standing still.

ithaf.f: مَا الْمَاءُ الَّذِي لَا يَصِحُّ التَّطْهِيرُ بِهِ؟
ithaf.b: لَا يَصِحُّ التَّطْهِيرُ بِمَاءٍ زَالَ طَبْعُهُ بِالطَّبْخِ، أَوْ خَالَطَهُ طَاهِرٌ فَغَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ، أَوْ تَغَيَّرَ بِنَجَاسَةٍ.

en.f: With what water is purification not valid?
en.b: Purification is not valid with water whose nature has changed through cooking, water mixed with something pure that has overcome it, or water changed by impurity.

ithaf.f: هَلْ يَصِحُّ التَّطْهِيرُ بِمَاءٍ رَاكِدٍ قَلِيلٍ وَقَعَتْ فِيهِ نَجَاسَةٌ؟
ithaf.b: لَا يَصِحُّ التَّطْهِيرُ بِمَاءٍ رَاكِدٍ قَلِيلٍ وَقَعَتْ فِيهِ نَجَاسَةٌ.

en.f: Is purification valid with a small amount of still water into which impurity has fallen?
en.b: No, purification is not valid with a small amount of still water into which impurity has fallen.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ الْمَاءِ الْمُسْتَعْمَلِ فِي رَفْعِ الْحَدَثِ أَوْ فِي قُرْبَةٍ؟
ithaf.b: هُوَ طَاهِرٌ غَيْرُ مُطَهِّرٍ، فَلَا يَصِحُّ التَّطْهِيرُ بِهِ.

en.f: What is the ruling on water used to lift ritual impurity (hadath) or for an act of worship?
en.b: It is pure but not purifying, so purification with it is not valid.

ithaf.f: مَتَى لَا يَنْجُسُ الْمَاءُ الْجَارِي وَالدَّائِمُ؟
ithaf.b: لَا يَنْجُسُ الْمَاءُ الْجَارِي وَالدَّائِمُ الَّذِي بَلَغَ عَشَرَةَ أَذْرُعٍ فِي مِثْلِهَا، إِلَّا بِظُهُورِ أَثَرِ النَّجَاسَةِ.

en.f: When does flowing water, or a large still body of water, not become impure?
en.b: Flowing water, and still water that reaches ten by ten cubits, does not become impure unless a trace of the impurity appears.

ithaf.f: مَا أَثَرُ النَّجَاسَةِ الَّذِي إِذَا ظَهَرَ فِي الْمَاءِ نَجُسَ؟
ithaf.b: أَثَرُ النَّجَاسَةِ هُوَ الطَّعْمُ أَوِ اللَّوْنُ أَوِ الرِّيحُ.

en.f: What is the trace of impurity which, if it appears in water, makes it impure?
en.b: The trace of impurity is its taste, colour or smell.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ سُؤْرِ الْآدَمِيِّ وَمَأْكُولِ اللَّحْمِ؟
ithaf.b: سُؤْرُ الْآدَمِيِّ وَمَأْكُولِ اللَّحْمِ طَاهِرٌ.

en.f: What is the ruling on the leftover water (su'r) of a human and of an animal whose meat is eaten?
en.b: The leftover of a human and of an animal whose meat is eaten is pure.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ سُؤْرِ الْكَلْبِ وَالْخِنْزِيرِ وَسِبَاعِ الْبَهَائِمِ؟
ithaf.b: سُؤْرُ الْكَلْبِ وَالْخِنْزِيرِ وَسِبَاعِ الْبَهَائِمِ نَجَسٌ.

en.f: What is the ruling on the leftover of the dog, the pig and predatory animals?
en.b: The leftover of the dog, the pig and predatory animals is impure.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ سُؤْرِ الْهِرَّةِ وَالدَّجَاجَةِ الْمُخَالَاةِ وَسِبَاعِ الطَّيْرِ؟
ithaf.b: سُؤْرُ الْهِرَّةِ وَالدَّجَاجَةِ الْمُخَالَاةِ وَسِبَاعِ الطَّيْرِ مَكْرُوهٌ.

en.f: What is the ruling on the leftover of the cat, the free-roaming chicken and birds of prey?
en.b: The leftover of the cat, the free-roaming chicken and birds of prey is disliked (makruh).

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ سُؤْرِ الْحِمَارِ وَالْبَغْلِ؟
ithaf.b: سُؤْرُ الْحِمَارِ وَالْبَغْلِ مَشْكُوكٌ فِيهِ.

en.f: What is the ruling on the leftover of the donkey and the mule?
en.b: The leftover of the donkey and the mule is doubtful.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ الْعَرَقِ؟
ithaf.b: الْعَرَقُ كَالسُّؤْرِ.

en.f: What is the ruling on sweat?
en.b: Sweat takes the ruling of the leftover (of the same creature).

ithaf.f: مَنْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ التَّيَمُّمُ؟
ithaf.b: مَنْ عَجَزَ عَنِ اسْتِعْمَالِ الْمَاءِ لِبُعْدِهِ مِيلًا، أَوْ لِمَرَضٍ، أَوْ بَرْدٍ، أَوْ خَوْفِ عَدُوٍّ، أَوْ عَطَشٍ، أَوْ عَدَمِ آلَةٍ.

en.f: Who may perform tayammum?
en.b: Whoever is unable to use water because it is a mile away, or because of illness, cold, fear of an enemy, thirst, or having nothing to draw it with.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَكُونُ التَّيَمُّمُ؟
ithaf.b: يَتَيَمَّمُ نَاوِيًا بِضَرْبَتَيْنِ، مُسْتَوْعِبًا وَجْهَهُ وَيَدَيْهِ مَعَ مِرْفَقَيْهِ.

en.f: How is tayammum done?
en.b: One performs tayammum with the intention, with two strikes, covering the whole face and the arms including the elbows.

ithaf.f: بِمَاذَا يَصِحُّ التَّيَمُّمُ؟
ithaf.b: يَصِحُّ التَّيَمُّمُ بِطَاهِرٍ مِنْ جِنْسِ الْأَرْضِ.

en.f: With what is tayammum valid?
en.b: Tayammum is valid with anything pure that is of the earth's kind.

ithaf.f: هَلْ يَصِحُّ التَّيَمُّمُ لِلْجُنُبِ وَالْحَائِضِ؟
ithaf.b: نَعَمْ، يَصِحُّ التَّيَمُّمُ لِلْجُنُبِ وَلِلْحَائِضِ.

en.f: Is tayammum valid for someone in major ritual impurity (janabah) and for a menstruating woman?
en.b: Yes, tayammum is valid for someone in janabah and for a menstruating woman.

ithaf.f: هَلْ يَصِحُّ التَّيَمُّمُ قَبْلَ دُخُولِ الْوَقْتِ؟
ithaf.b: نَعَمْ، يَصِحُّ التَّيَمُّمُ قَبْلَ دُخُولِ الْوَقْتِ.

en.f: Is tayammum valid before the prayer time begins?
en.b: Yes, tayammum is valid before the prayer time begins.

ithaf.f: هَلْ يَجُوزُ بِالتَّيَمُّمِ الْوَاحِدِ أَدَاءُ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ فَرْضٍ؟
ithaf.b: نَعَمْ، يَجُوزُ بِالتَّيَمُّمِ الْوَاحِدِ أَدَاءُ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ فَرْضٍ.

en.f: May more than one obligatory prayer be performed with a single tayammum?
en.b: Yes, more than one obligatory prayer may be performed with a single tayammum.

ithaf.f: مَا الَّذِي يَنْقُضُ التَّيَمُّمَ؟
ithaf.b: يَنْقُضُ التَّيَمُّمَ نَاقِضُ الْوُضُوءِ، وَالْقُدْرَةُ عَلَى اسْتِعْمَالِ الْمَاءِ الْكَافِي.

en.f: What breaks tayammum?
en.b: Whatever breaks wudu, and becoming able to use enough water.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ مَنْ كَانَ أَكْثَرُ بَدَنِهِ مَجْرُوحًا؟
ithaf.b: إِذَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُ بَدَنِهِ مَجْرُوحًا تَيَمَّمَ.

en.f: What is the ruling for someone most of whose body is wounded?
en.b: If most of his body is wounded, he performs tayammum.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ مَنْ كَانَ أَقَلُّ بَدَنِهِ مَجْرُوحًا؟
ithaf.b: إِذَا كَانَ أَقَلُّ بَدَنِهِ مَجْرُوحًا غَسَلَ وَلَا يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَ الْغَسْلِ وَالتَّيَمُّمِ.

en.f: What is the ruling for someone the lesser part of whose body is wounded?
en.b: If the lesser part of his body is wounded, he washes (the rest), and he does not combine washing with tayammum.

ithaf.f: مَتَى يَجُوزُ الْمَسْحُ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ؟
ithaf.b: يَجُوزُ الْمَسْحُ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ لِلْمُحْدِثِ إِنْ لَبِسَهُمَا عَلَى طُهْرٍ.

en.f: When is wiping over leather socks (khuffs) permitted?
en.b: Wiping over khuffs is permitted for someone in minor impurity if he put them on in a state of purity.

ithaf.f: مَا مُدَّةُ الْمَسْحِ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ لِلْمُقِيمِ وَالْمُسَافِرِ؟
ithaf.b: مُدَّةُ الْمَسْحِ لِلْمُقِيمِ يَوْمٌ وَلَيْلَةٌ، وَلِلْمُسَافِرِ ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ وَلَيَالِيهَا، مِنْ وَقْتِ الْحَدَثِ.

en.f: How long may a resident and a traveller wipe over khuffs?
en.b: A resident may wipe for one day and night, and a traveller for three days and nights, counted from the time of the (first) minor impurity.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَكُونُ الْمَسْحُ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ؟
ithaf.b: يَكُونُ الْمَسْحُ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ بِثَلَاثِ أَصَابِعَ عَلَى ظَاهِرِهِمَا مَرَّةً.

en.f: How is wiping over khuffs done?
en.b: Wiping over khuffs is done once, with three fingers, over their upper surface.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ الْخُفِّ ذِي الْخَرْقِ الْكَبِيرِ فِي الْمَسْحِ عَلَيْهِ؟
ithaf.b: الْخَرْقُ الْكَبِيرُ يَمْنَعُ الْمَسْحَ عَلَى الْخُفِّ.

en.f: What is the ruling on wiping over a khuff with a large tear?
en.b: A large tear prevents wiping over the khuff.

ithaf.f: مَا الَّذِي يَنْقُضُ الْمَسْحَ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ؟
ithaf.b: يَنْقُضُهُ نَاقِضُ الْوُضُوءِ، وَنَزْعُ الْخُفِّ، وَمُضِيُّ الْمُدَّةِ.

en.f: What breaks the wiping over khuffs?
en.b: Whatever breaks wudu, removing a khuff, and the end of the time period.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ الْمَسْحِ عَلَى الْجَبِيرَةِ؟
ithaf.b: الْمَسْحُ عَلَى الْجَبِيرَةِ كَالْغُسْلِ، وَلَوْ شُدَّتْ بِلَا وُضُوءٍ.

en.f: What is the ruling on wiping over a splint (jabirah)?
en.b: Wiping over a splint is like washing (the limb), even if it was tied on without wudu.

ithaf.f: مَتَى يَبْطُلُ الْمَسْحُ عَلَى الْجَبِيرَةِ؟
ithaf.b: إِنْ سَقَطَتِ الْجَبِيرَةُ عَنْ بُرْءٍ بَطَلَ الْمَسْحُ، وَإِنْ سَقَطَتْ لِغَيْرِ بُرْءٍ فَلَا يَبْطُلُ.

en.f: When is the wiping over a splint cancelled?
en.b: If the splint falls off because the wound has healed, the wiping is cancelled; if it falls off without healing, it is not.

ithaf.f: مَا أَقَلُّ الْحَيْضِ وَأَكْثَرُهُ؟
ithaf.b: أَقَلُّ الْحَيْضِ ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ، وَأَكْثَرُهُ عَشَرَةُ أَيَّامٍ.

en.f: What is the minimum and maximum of menstruation?
en.b: The minimum of menstruation is three days, and the maximum is ten days.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ مَا نَقَصَ عَنْ أَقَلِّ الْحَيْضِ أَوْ زَادَ عَلَى أَكْثَرِهِ؟
ithaf.b: مَا نَقَصَ عَنْ أَقَلِّ الْحَيْضِ أَوْ زَادَ عَلَى أَكْثَرِهِ فَهُوَ اسْتِحَاضَةٌ.

en.f: What is the ruling on bleeding less than the minimum of menstruation, or more than its maximum?
en.b: Bleeding less than the minimum or more than the maximum is istihadah (irregular bleeding).

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ الدَّمِ الَّذِي تَرَاهُ الْحَامِلُ؟
ithaf.b: الدَّمُ الَّذِي تَرَاهُ الْحَامِلُ اسْتِحَاضَةٌ.

en.f: What is the ruling on blood seen by a pregnant woman?
en.b: Blood seen by a pregnant woman is istihadah.

ithaf.f: مَا أَكْثَرُ النِّفَاسِ؟ وَهَلْ لِأَقَلِّهِ حَدٌّ؟
ithaf.b: أَكْثَرُ النِّفَاسِ أَرْبَعُونَ يَوْمًا، وَلَا حَدَّ لِأَقَلِّهِ.

en.f: What is the maximum of post-natal bleeding (nifas)? Does it have a minimum?
en.b: The maximum of nifas is forty days, and it has no minimum.

ithaf.f: مَا أَقَلُّ مُدَّةِ الطُّهْرِ؟
ithaf.b: أَقَلُّ مُدَّةِ الطُّهْرِ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا.

en.f: What is the minimum period of purity (between two menstruations)?
en.b: The minimum period of purity is fifteen days.

ithaf.f: مَا الَّذِي يَحْرُمُ بِالْحَيْضِ وَالنِّفَاسِ؟
ithaf.b: يَحْرُمُ بِالْحَيْضِ وَالنِّفَاسِ الصَّلَاةُ، وَالصَّوْمُ، وَقِرَاءَةُ الْقُرْآنِ، وَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا بِغِلَافٍ، وَدُخُولُ الْمَسْجِدِ، وَالطَّوَافُ، وَقُرْبَانُ مَا تَحْتَ الْإِزَارِ.

en.f: What becomes unlawful because of menstruation and post-natal bleeding?
en.b: Prayer, fasting, reciting the Qur'an, touching it except with a separate cover, entering the mosque, tawaf, and approaching what is beneath the waist-wrapper.

ithaf.f: مَا الَّذِي يَحْرُمُ بِالْجَنَابَةِ؟
ithaf.b: يَحْرُمُ بِالْجَنَابَةِ الصَّلَاةُ، وَقِرَاءَةُ الْقُرْآنِ، وَمَسُّهُ، وَدُخُولُ الْمَسْجِدِ، وَالطَّوَافُ.

en.f: What becomes unlawful because of janabah?
en.b: Prayer, reciting the Qur'an, touching it, entering the mosque, and tawaf.

ithaf.f: مَا الَّذِي يَحْرُمُ عَلَى الْمُحْدِثِ؟
ithaf.b: يَحْرُمُ عَلَى الْمُحْدِثِ الصَّلَاةُ، وَالطَّوَافُ، وَمَسُّ الْقُرْآنِ.

en.f: What is unlawful for someone in minor impurity (without wudu)?
en.b: Prayer, tawaf, and touching the Qur'an.

ithaf.f: مَتَى تَتَوَضَّأُ الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ وَمَنْ بِهِ عُذْرٌ؟
ithaf.b: تَتَوَضَّأُ الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ وَمَنْ بِهِ عُذْرٌ، كَسَلَسِ الْبَوْلِ أَوِ الرُّعَافِ الدَّائِمِ، لِوَقْتِ كُلِّ فَرْضٍ.

en.f: When does a woman with istihadah, or anyone with a chronic excuse, make wudu?
en.b: She, and anyone with an excuse such as incontinence or a constant nosebleed, makes wudu for the time of each obligatory prayer.

ithaf.f: مَاذَا يَجُوزُ لِلْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ وَمَنْ بِهِ عُذْرٌ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ بِوُضُوءِ الْوَقْتِ؟
ithaf.b: يُصَلُّونَ بِوُضُوءِ الْوَقْتِ مَا شَاءُوا.

en.f: What may a woman with istihadah, or someone with an excuse, pray with the wudu of that time?
en.b: They may pray whatever they wish with the wudu of that time.

ithaf.f: بِمَاذَا يَطْهُرُ الْبَدَنُ وَالثَّوْبُ؟
ithaf.b: يَطْهُرُ الْبَدَنُ وَالثَّوْبُ بِالْمَاءِ، وَبِكُلِّ مَائِعٍ مُزِيلٍ.

en.f: With what are the body and clothes purified?
en.b: The body and clothes are purified with water, and with any liquid that removes (the impurity).

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَطْهُرُ الْخُفُّ إِذَا كَانَتِ النَّجَاسَةُ ذَاتَ جِرْمٍ؟
ithaf.b: يَطْهُرُ الْخُفُّ مِنَ النَّجَاسَةِ ذَاتِ الْجِرْمِ بِالدَّلْكِ.

en.f: How is a khuff purified if the impurity has a body (jirm)?
en.b: A khuff is purified from impurity that has a body by rubbing it off.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَطْهُرُ السَّيْفُ وَنَحْوُهُ؟
ithaf.b: يَطْهُرُ السَّيْفُ وَنَحْوُهُ بِالْمَسْجِحِ.

en.f: How is a sword or something similar purified?
en.b: A sword and the like are purified by wiping.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ تَطْهُرُ الْأَرْضُ مِنَ النَّجَاسَةِ؟
ithaf.b: تَطْهُرُ الْأَرْضُ بِالْيُبْسِ وَذَهَابِ الْأَثَرِ.

en.f: How is the ground purified from impurity?
en.b: The ground is purified by drying and the trace disappearing.

ithaf.f: عَمَّاذَا عُفِيَ مِنَ النَّجَاسَةِ الْمُغَلَّظَةِ؟
ithaf.b: عُفِيَ عَنْ قَدْرِ الدِّرْهَمِ مِنَ النَّجَاسَةِ الْمُغَلَّظَةِ، كَالدَّمِ، وَالْخِنْزِيرِ، وَبَوْلِ مَا لَا يُؤْكَلُ، وَالرَّوْثِ.

en.f: How much heavy impurity (mughallazah) is excused?
en.b: An amount the size of a dirham of heavy impurity is excused, such as blood, (anything of) the pig, the urine of animals not eaten, and dung.

ithaf.f: عَمَّاذَا عُفِيَ مِنَ النَّجَاسَةِ الْمُخَفَّفَةِ؟
ithaf.b: عُفِيَ عَمَّا دُونَ رُبْعِ الثَّوْبِ مِنَ النَّجَاسَةِ الْمُخَفَّفَةِ، كَبَوْلِ مَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ.

en.f: How much light impurity (mukhaffafah) is excused?
en.b: Less than a quarter of the garment of light impurity is excused, such as the urine of animals whose meat is eaten.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَطْهُرُ الْمُتَنَجِّسُ بِنَجَاسَةٍ مَرْئِيَّةٍ؟
ithaf.b: يَطْهُرُ الْمُتَنَجِّسُ بِنَجَاسَةٍ مَرْئِيَّةٍ بِزَوَالِ عَيْنِ النَّجَاسَةِ.

en.f: How is something soiled with visible impurity purified?
en.b: By removing the substance of the impurity.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَطْهُرُ الْمُتَنَجِّسُ بِنَجَاسَةٍ غَيْرِ مَرْئِيَّةٍ؟
ithaf.b: يَطْهُرُ الْمُتَنَجِّسُ بِنَجَاسَةٍ غَيْرِ مَرْئِيَّةٍ بِالْغَسْلِ ثَلَاثًا.

en.f: How is something soiled with invisible impurity purified?
en.b: By washing it three times.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَطْهُرُ جِلْدُ الْمَيْتَةِ؟
ithaf.b: يَطْهُرُ جِلْدُ الْمَيْتَةِ بِالدِّبَاغَةِ وَبِالذَّكَاةِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ، إِلَّا الْخِنْزِيرَ وَالْآدَمِيَّ.

en.f: How is the skin of a dead animal purified?
en.b: By tanning, and by lawful slaughter, except for the pig and the human.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ شَعْرِ الْإِنْسَانِ وَالْمَيْتَةِ وَعَظْمِهِمَا؟
ithaf.b: شَعْرُ الْإِنْسَانِ وَالْمَيْتَةِ وَعَظْمُهُمَا طَاهِرٌ.

en.f: What is the ruling on the hair and bones of a human and of a dead animal?
en.b: The hair and bones of a human and of a dead animal are pure.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَكُونُ الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ بِالْأَحْجَارِ؟
ithaf.b: يَكُونُ الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ بِنَحْوِ حَجَرٍ مُثْقِلٍ، وَالِاسْتِنْجَاءُ سِتَّةٌ.

en.f: How is istinja' (cleaning after relieving oneself) done with stones?
en.b: Istinja' is done with something like a stone that cleans; istinja' is a sunnah.

ithaf.f: أَيُّهُمَا أَفْضَلُ: الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ أَمِ الْغَسْلُ؟
ithaf.b: الْغَسْلُ أَفْضَلُ.

en.f: Which is better: wiping with stones or washing?
en.b: Washing is better.

ithaf.f: بِمَاذَا يُكْرَهُ الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ؟
ithaf.b: يُكْرَهُ الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ بِعَظْمٍ، وَرَوْثٍ، وَطَعَامٍ، وَبِالْيَمِينِ.

en.f: With what is istinja' disliked?
en.b: Istinja' is disliked with bone, dung, food, and with the right hand.

ithaf.f: مَا الَّذِي يُكْرَهُ عِنْدَ قَضَاءِ الْحَاجَةِ مِنْ جِهَةِ الْقِبْلَةِ؟
ithaf.b: يُكْرَهُ اسْتِقْبَالُ الْقِبْلَةِ وَاسْتِدْبَارُهَا فِي الْحَالِ.

en.f: What is disliked regarding the qiblah when relieving oneself?
en.b: Facing the qiblah, or turning one's back to it, at that time is disliked.

ithaf.f: مَا الْأُمُورُ الَّتِي تُكْرَهُ عِنْدَ قَضَاءِ الْحَاجَةِ؟
ithaf.b: يُكْرَهُ الْكَلَامُ، وَاسْتِقْبَالُ عَيْنِ الشَّمْسِ وَالْقَمَرِ، وَمَهَبِّ الرِّيحِ، وَالتَّخَلِّي تَحْتَ شَجَرَةٍ مُثْمِرَةٍ.

en.f: What is disliked when relieving oneself?
en.b: Speaking; facing the sun or moon directly; facing into the wind; and relieving oneself under a fruit-bearing tree.

ithaf.f: مَا وَقْتُ صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ؟
ithaf.b: وَقْتُ الْفَجْرِ مِنَ الصُّبْحِ الصَّادِقِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ.

en.f: What is the time of Fajr prayer?
en.b: From true dawn until sunrise.

ithaf.f: مَا وَقْتُ صَلَاةِ الظُّهْرِ؟
ithaf.b: وَقْتُ الظُّهْرِ مِنَ الزَّوَالِ إِلَى بُلُوغِ الظِّلِّ مِثْلَيْهِ سِوَى الْفَيْءِ.

en.f: What is the time of Zuhr prayer?
en.b: From the sun's passing its zenith until an object's shadow is twice its length, not counting the noon shadow.

ithaf.f: مَا وَقْتُ صَلَاةِ الْعَصْرِ؟
ithaf.b: وَقْتُ الْعَصْرِ مِنْ بَعْدِ بُلُوغِ الظِّلِّ مِثْلَيْهِ سِوَى الْفَيْءِ إِلَى الْغُرُوبِ.

en.f: What is the time of 'Asr prayer?
en.b: From when the shadow reaches twice the object's length, not counting the noon shadow, until sunset.

ithaf.f: مَا وَقْتُ صَلَاةِ الْمَغْرِبِ؟
ithaf.b: وَقْتُ الْمَغْرِبِ مِنَ الْغُرُوبِ إِلَى غُرُوبِ الشَّفَقِ.

en.f: What is the time of Maghrib prayer?
en.b: From sunset until the twilight disappears.

ithaf.f: مَا وَقْتُ صَلَاةِ الْعِشَاءِ؟
ithaf.b: وَقْتُ الْعِشَاءِ مِنْ غُرُوبِ الشَّفَقِ إِلَى الصُّبْحِ.

en.f: What is the time of 'Isha' prayer?
en.b: From the disappearance of the twilight until dawn.

ithaf.f: مَا شَرَائِطُ الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: شَرَائِطُ الصَّلَاةِ: طَهَارَةُ الْبَدَنِ مِنَ الْحَدَثِ وَالْخَبَثِ، وَطَهَارَةُ الثَّوْبِ وَالْمَكَانِ، وَسَتْرُ الْعَوْرَةِ، وَاسْتِقْبَالُ الْقِبْلَةِ، وَالْوَقْتُ، وَالنِّيَّةُ، وَالتَّحْرِيمَةُ.

en.f: What are the conditions of prayer?
en.b: Purity of the body from ritual and physical impurity, purity of the clothes and the place, covering the 'awrah, facing the qiblah, the time, the intention, and the opening takbir.

ithaf.f: مَا عَوْرَةُ الرَّجُلِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: عَوْرَةُ الرَّجُلِ مَا تَحْتَ سُرَّتِهِ إِلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ.

en.f: What is a man's 'awrah in prayer?
en.b: A man's 'awrah is from below his navel to (and including) his knees.

ithaf.f: مَا عَوْرَةُ الْأَمَةِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: عَوْرَةُ الْأَمَةِ مِثْلُ عَوْرَةِ الرَّجُلِ، وَتَزِيدُ عَلَيْهِ بِظَهْرِهَا وَبَطْنِهَا.

en.f: What is a slave-woman's 'awrah in prayer?
en.b: Her 'awrah is like a man's, with her back and stomach in addition.

ithaf.f: مَا عَوْرَةُ الْحُرَّةِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: عَوْرَةُ الْحُرَّةِ جَمِيعُ بَدَنِهَا إِلَّا الْوَجْهَ وَالْكَفَّيْنِ وَالْقَدَمَيْنِ.

en.f: What is a free woman's 'awrah in prayer?
en.b: A free woman's 'awrah is her whole body except the face, the hands and the feet.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ مَنْ فَقَدَ مَا يُزِيلُ بِهِ النَّجَاسَةَ؟
ithaf.b: يُصَلِّي مَعَ النَّجَاسَةِ، وَلَا إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ.

en.f: What is the ruling for someone who has nothing with which to remove an impurity?
en.b: He prays with the impurity, and need not repeat the prayer.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ مَنْ اشْتَبَهَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْقِبْلَةُ؟
ithaf.b: يَتَحَرَّى الْقِبْلَةَ، فَإِنْ أَخْطَأَ لَمْ يُعِدْ.

en.f: What is the ruling for someone unsure of the qiblah?
en.b: He tries his best to determine the qiblah; if he turns out to be mistaken, he does not repeat the prayer.

ithaf.f: مَا أَرْكَانُ الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: أَرْكَانُ الصَّلَاةِ: الْقِيَامُ لِلْقَادِرِ فِي غَيْرِ النَّفْلِ، وَقِرَاءَةُ آيَةٍ فِي رَكْعَتَيْ الْفَرْضِ، وَفِي كُلِّ النَّفْلِ وَالْوَتْرِ، وَالرُّكُوعُ، وَالسُّجُودُ، وَتَرْتِيبُ الْقِيَامِ عَلَى الرُّكُوعِ، وَالرُّكُوعِ عَلَى السُّجُودِ، وَالْقُعُودُ الْأَخِيرُ قَدْرَ التَّشَهُّدِ.

en.f: What are the pillars of prayer?
en.b: Standing, for one able to, except in voluntary prayer; reciting a verse in two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer, and in every rak'ah of voluntary prayer and witr; bowing; prostration; placing standing before bowing and bowing before prostration; and the final sitting for the length of the tashahhud.

ithaf.f: مَا الْمَقْصُودُ بِالْقِيَامِ مِنْ أَرْكَانِ الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: هُوَ الْقِيَامُ لِلْقَادِرِ فِي غَيْرِ النَّفْلِ.

en.f: What is meant by standing as a pillar of prayer?
en.b: Standing, for one able to, in other than voluntary prayer.

ithaf.f: كَمْ يَجِبُ مِنَ الْقِرَاءَةِ فِي الْفَرْضِ؟
ithaf.b: تَجِبُ قِرَاءَةُ آيَةٍ فِي رَكْعَتَيْ الْفَرْضِ.

en.f: How much recitation is required in an obligatory prayer?
en.b: Reciting one verse in two rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer.

ithaf.f: كَمْ يَجِبُ مِنَ الْقِرَاءَةِ فِي النَّفْلِ وَالْوَتْرِ؟
ithaf.b: تَجِبُ قِرَاءَةُ آيَةٍ فِي كُلِّ النَّفْلِ وَالْوَتْرِ.

en.f: How much recitation is required in voluntary prayer and witr?
en.b: Reciting one verse in every rak'ah of voluntary prayer and witr.

ithaf.f: مَا وَاجِبَاتُ الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: وَاجِبَاتُ الصَّلَاةِ: قِرَاءَةُ الْفَاتِحَةِ، وَضَمُّ سُورَةٍ أَوْ مَا يَقُومُ مَقَامَهَا فِي الْأُولَيَيْنِ مِنَ الْفَرْضِ، وَجَمِيعِ الْوَتْرِ وَالنَّفْلِ، وَتَعْيِينُ الْقِرَاءَةِ فِي الْأُولَيَيْنِ، وَرِعَايَةُ التَّرْتِيبِ فِيمَا تَكَرَّرَ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ، وَالِاطْمِئْنَانُ فِي الْأَرْكَانِ، وَالْقُعُودُ الْأَوَّلُ، وَالتَّشَهُّدُ فِي الْقَعْدَتَيْنِ، وَلَفْظُ السَّلَامِ مَرَّتَيْنِ، وَقُنُوتُ الْوَتْرِ، وَتَكْبِيرَاتُ الْعِيدَيْنِ، وَجَهْرُ الْإِمَامِ فِيمَا يَجْهَرُ، وَالْإِسْرَارُ فِيمَا يُسِرُّ.

en.f: What are the necessary acts (wajibat) of prayer?
en.b: Reciting al-Fatihah; adding a surah, or what takes its place, in the first two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer and in every rak'ah of witr and voluntary prayer; making the first two rak'ahs the place of that recitation; keeping the order of what is repeated in each rak'ah; calmness in the pillars; the first sitting; the tashahhud in both sittings; saying the word al-salam twice; the qunut of witr; the takbirs of the two Eids; the imam reciting aloud where it is aloud, and quietly where it is quiet.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ قِرَاءَةِ الْفَاتِحَةِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: قِرَاءَةُ الْفَاتِحَةِ مِنْ وَاجِبَاتِ الصَّلَاةِ.

en.f: What is the ruling on reciting al-Fatihah in prayer?
en.b: Reciting al-Fatihah is one of the wajibat of prayer.

ithaf.f: أَيْنَ تَجِبُ قِرَاءَةُ سُورَةٍ أَوْ مَا يَقُومُ مَقَامَهَا؟
ithaf.b: تَجِبُ قِرَاءَةُ سُورَةٍ أَوْ مَا يَقُومُ مَقَامَهَا فِي الْأُولَيَيْنِ مِنَ الْفَرْضِ، وَفِي جَمِيعِ الْوَتْرِ وَالنَّفْلِ.

en.f: Where is it wajib to recite a surah, or what takes its place?
en.b: In the first two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer, and in every rak'ah of witr and voluntary prayer.

ithaf.f: مَا الْمَقْصُودُ بِتَعْيِينِ الْقِرَاءَةِ فِي الْأُولَيَيْنِ؟
ithaf.b: الْمَقْصُودُ أَنْ تَكُونَ الْقِرَاءَةُ فِي الْأُولَيَيْنِ مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ.

en.f: What is meant by making the first two rak'ahs the place of recitation?
en.b: That the (extra) recitation is done in the first two rak'ahs of the prayer.

ithaf.f: مَا الْمَقْصُودُ بِرِعَايَةِ التَّرْتِيبِ فِيمَا تَكَرَّرَ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ؟
ithaf.b: هُوَ رِعَايَةُ التَّرْتِيبِ فِي الْأَفْعَالِ وَالْأَذْكَارِ الَّتِي تَتَكَرَّرُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ.

en.f: What is meant by keeping the order of what is repeated in each rak'ah?
en.b: Keeping the order of the actions and words that are repeated in every rak'ah.

ithaf.f: مَا الَّذِي يَجِبُ فِي الْأَرْكَانِ مِنْ حَيْثُ السُّكُونُ؟
ithaf.b: يَجِبُ الِاطْمِئْنَانُ فِي الْأَرْكَانِ.

en.f: What is wajib in the pillars as regards stillness?
en.b: Calmness (itmi'nan) in the pillars is wajib.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ الْقُعُودِ الْأَوَّلِ وَالتَّشَهُّدِ؟
ithaf.b: الْقُعُودُ الْأَوَّلُ وَالتَّشَهُّدُ فِي الْقَعْدَتَيْنِ مِنْ وَاجِبَاتِ الصَّلَاةِ.

en.f: What is the ruling on the first sitting and the tashahhud?
en.b: The first sitting, and the tashahhud in both sittings, are among the wajibat of prayer.

ithaf.f: كَمْ مَرَّةً يُلْفَظُ بِالسَّلَامِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: يُلْفَظُ بِالسَّلَامِ مَرَّتَيْنِ.

en.f: How many times is the salam said in prayer?
en.b: The salam is said twice.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ قُنُوتِ الْوَتْرِ؟
ithaf.b: قُنُوتُ الْوَتْرِ مِنْ وَاجِبَاتِ الصَّلَاةِ.

en.f: What is the ruling on the qunut of witr?
en.b: The qunut of witr is one of the wajibat of prayer.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ تَكْبِيرَاتِ الْعِيدَيْنِ؟
ithaf.b: تَكْبِيرَاتُ الْعِيدَيْنِ مِنْ وَاجِبَاتِ الصَّلَاةِ.

en.f: What is the ruling on the takbirs of the two Eids?
en.b: The takbirs of the two Eids are among the wajibat of prayer.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ جَهْرِ الْإِمَامِ وَإِسْرَارِهِ فِي الْقِرَاءَةِ؟
ithaf.b: يَجْهَرُ الْإِمَامُ فِيمَا يُجْهَرُ فِيهِ، وَيُسِرُّ فِيمَا يُسَرُّ فِيهِ.

en.f: What is the ruling on the imam reciting aloud or quietly?
en.b: The imam recites aloud in prayers recited aloud, and quietly in prayers recited quietly.

ithaf.f: مَا سُنَنُ الصَّلَاةِ؟
ithaf.b: مِنْ سُنَنِ الصَّلَاةِ: الْأَذَانُ، وَالْإِقَامَةُ لِلْفَرَائِضِ، وَرَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ لِلتَّحْرِيمَةِ، وَجَهْرُ الْإِمَامِ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ، وَالثَّنَاءُ، وَالتَّعَوُّذُ، وَالتَّسْمِيَةُ، وَالتَّأْمِينُ، وَوَضْعُ يَمِينِهِ عَلَى يَسَارِهِ تَحْتَ سُرَّتِهِ.

en.f: What are the sunnahs of prayer?
en.b: Among the sunnahs of prayer are: the adhan and iqamah for the obligatory prayers, raising the hands for the opening takbir, the imam saying the takbir aloud, the opening praise (thana'), seeking refuge (ta'awwudh), saying Bismillah, saying Amin, and placing the right hand over the left below the navel.

ithaf.f: مَا السُّنَّةُ فِي طُولِ السُّورَةِ الْمَقْرُوءَةِ فِي الصَّلَوَاتِ؟
ithaf.b: تَكُونُ السُّورَةُ مِنْ طِوَالِ الْمُفَصَّلِ فِي الْفَجْرِ وَالظُّهْرِ، وَمِنْ أَوْسَاطِهِ فِي الْعَصْرِ وَالْعِشَاءِ، وَمِنْ قِصَارِهِ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ.

en.f: What is the sunnah length of the surah recited in each prayer?
en.b: In Fajr and Zuhr, from the long surahs of the Mufassal; in 'Asr and 'Isha', from its middle surahs; and in Maghrib, from its short surahs.

ithaf.f: مَا سُنَنُ الرُّكُوعِ؟
ithaf.b: مِنْ سُنَنِ الرُّكُوعِ: تَكْبِيرُ الرُّكُوعِ، وَتَسْبِيحُهُ ثَلَاثًا، وَأَخْذُ الرُّكْبَتَيْنِ بِالْيَدَيْنِ، وَتَفْرِيجُ الْأَصَابِعِ، وَبَسْطُ الظَّهْرِ، وَالرَّفْعُ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ.

en.f: What are the sunnahs of bowing (ruku')?
en.b: Among them: the takbir for bowing, glorifying (Allah) three times in it, holding the knees with the hands, spreading the fingers, straightening the back, and rising from the bowing.

ithaf.f: مَا السُّنَّةُ فِي الذِّكْرِ عِنْدَ الرَّفْعِ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ لِلْإِمَامِ وَالْمُؤْتَمِّ وَالْمُنْفَرِدِ؟
ithaf.b: التَّسْمِيعُ لِلْإِمَامِ، وَالتَّحْمِيدُ لِلْمُؤْتَمِّ، وَالْمُنْفَرِدُ بَيْنَهُمَا.

en.f: What is the sunnah dhikr when rising from ruku' for the imam, the follower and the one praying alone?
en.b: The imam says "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah", the follower says the praise ("Rabbana laka'l-hamd"), and the one praying alone says both.

ithaf.f: مَا سُنَنُ النُّزُولِ إِلَى السُّجُودِ؟
ithaf.b: مِنْ سُنَنِ النُّزُولِ إِلَى السُّجُودِ وَضْعُ الرُّكْبَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ الْيَدَيْنِ ثُمَّ الْوَجْهِ.

en.f: What is the sunnah way of going down into prostration?
en.b: Placing the knees, then the hands, then the face.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَكُونُ النُّهُوضُ مِنَ السُّجُودِ؟
ithaf.b: يَكُونُ النُّهُوضُ بِعَكْسِ تَرْتِيبِ النُّزُولِ، فَيَرْفَعُ وَجْهَهُ ثُمَّ يَدَيْهِ ثُمَّ رُكْبَتَيْهِ.

en.f: How does one rise from prostration?
en.b: In the reverse order of going down: lifting the face, then the hands, then the knees.

ithaf.f: مَا سُنَنُ السُّجُودِ؟
ithaf.b: مِنْ سُنَنِ السُّجُودِ: تَكْبِيرُ السُّجُودِ، وَالرَّفْعُ مِنْهُ، وَتَسْبِيحُهُ ثَلَاثًا، وَمُجَافَاةُ الرَّجُلِ مِرْفَقَيْهِ عَنْ جَنْبَيْهِ، وَبَطْنَهُ عَنْ فَخِذَيْهِ، وَذِرَاعَيْهِ عَنِ الْأَرْضِ.

en.f: What are the sunnahs of prostration (sujud)?
en.b: Among them: the takbir for prostration and for rising from it, glorifying (Allah) three times in it, and a man keeping his elbows away from his sides, his stomach from his thighs, and his forearms off the ground.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَضَعُ الْمُصَلِّي يَدَيْهِ فِي الْجَلْسَةِ؟
ithaf.b: يَضَعُ يَدَيْهِ عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ كَالتَّشَهُّدِ.

en.f: How does the one praying place his hands while sitting (between the prostrations)?
en.b: He places his hands on his thighs, as in the tashahhud.

ithaf.f: كَيْفَ يَجْلِسُ الْمُصَلِّي فِي الْجَلْسَةِ؟
ithaf.b: يَفْتَرِشُ رِجْلَهُ الْيُسْرَى وَيَنْصِبُ الْيُمْنَى.

en.f: How does the one praying sit (between the prostrations)?
en.b: He sits on his left foot and keeps his right foot upright.

ithaf.f: مَا حُكْمُ قِرَاءَةِ الْفَاتِحَةِ فِيمَا بَعْدَ الْأُولَيَيْنِ مِنَ الْفَرْضِ؟
ithaf.b: قِرَاءَةُ الْفَاتِحَةِ فِيمَا بَعْدَ الْأُولَيَيْنِ مِنَ الْفَرْضِ مِنْ سُنَنِ الصَّلَاةِ.

en.f: What is the ruling on reciting al-Fatihah after the first two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer?
en.b: It is one of the sunnahs of prayer.

ithaf.f: مَا سُنَّةُ الْجُلُوسِ الْأَخِيرِ؟
ithaf.b: مِنْ سُنَّةِ الْجُلُوسِ الْأَخِيرِ الصَّلَاةُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَالدُّعَاءُ بِالْمَأْثُورِ فِيهِ.

en.f: What is sunnah in the final sitting?
en.b: Among its sunnahs are sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ and making a transmitted du'a.

ithaf.f: مَا سُنَّةُ الْمُصَلِّي فِي التَّسْلِيمِ؟
ithaf.b: مِنْ سُنَنِهِ الِالْتِفَاتُ بِالتَّسْلِيمَتَيْنِ.
